Train After You Measure: a Pre-Registered Learning Curve for Fine-Tuning Typed Decision Models on One User's Labels
先测量后训练：针对单个用户标签微调类型化决策模型的预注册学习曲线
Fine-tuning a small typed decision model on one user's email labels did not clear the margin we pre-registered over a logistic regression trained on the same labels. In earlier work, about two hundred labels and a TF-IDF logistic regression had the highest point accuracy on this inbox, though not significantly above the best hosted model; we ask whether the same labels, given to a decision model, close the gap. A first registered study, on a generic 4B base with cross-validation and message type only, stayed below the baseline at every label budget (-1.8 to -7.3 points). The main study was registered before any fine-tuning run: a fixed test set of 135 emails never used for selection, LoRA adapters on the public Tev1-0.8B and Tev1-4B decision models, nested subsets of 50 to 587 labels, two seeds and five decision fields on a free T4 GPU. Four of its five hypotheses are refuted--two in the fine-tunes' favour--and one is confirmed for one model. On message type the 4B model misses the registered three-point margin at 400 labels (+2.6) and passes it with all 587 (+3.3); with all labels both models are above the baseline by +0.7 and +3.3 points, where one email is 0.74 points and a 95% interval is about 15 points wide, and the 4B model is clearly ahead in type macro-F1 (0.581 vs. 0.406). On the three action switches the baseline is ahead at every label budget for both models (0.931 vs. 0.904 and 0.899 mean accuracy with all labels), at under a millisecond per question against 306 and 1681 ms. The 0.8B type curve barely improves after 300 labels and then falls. The baseline never predicts the two rarest classes (7 offers and 8 spam in the training pool); the fine-tuned models find spam in some runs, not consistently across seeds. We list the explanations we did not test and say when a new attempt would be worth making. Scripts are public; weights and emails are not.
中文翻译
在单个用户的邮件标签上微调一个小的类型化决策模型，并未达到我们预先注册的逻辑回归模型在相同标签上的性能差距。在前期工作中，约两百个标签与TF-IDF逻辑回归在该收件箱中取得了最高点准确率，尽管未显著优于最佳托管模型；我们探讨相同标签提供给决策模型是否能缩小这一差距。首次注册研究在通用4B基础模型上进行，采用交叉验证和仅消息类型作为特征，结果在每个标签预算下均低于基线（-1.8至-7.3分）。主研究在任何微调运行前已注册：固定测试集包含135封未用于选择的邮件，对公开的Tev1-0.8B和Tev1-4B决策模型使用LoRA适配器，嵌套子集标签数为50至587，两个种子和五个决策字段，使用免费T4 GPU。其五个假设中有四个被证伪——其中两个对微调有利——一个仅在一个模型上得到证实。在消息类型任务上，4B模型在400个标签时未能达到注册的三点优势（+2.6），但在全部587个标签时达到（+3.3）；使用全部标签时，两个模型均高于基线0.7和3.3分，其中一封邮件对应0.74分，95%置信区间约15分，且4B模型在类型宏F1上明显领先（0.581 vs. 0.406）。在三个操作开关任务上，两个模型在所有标签预算下均落后于基线（0.931 vs. 0.904 和 0.899 平均准确率），每题响应时间不足1毫秒，而微调模型分别需306和1681毫秒。0.8B模型在超过300个标签后几乎没有改善，随后下降。基线模型始终无法预测两个最罕见类别（训练集中7个优惠和8个垃圾邮件）；微调模型在某些运行中发现了垃圾邮件，但跨种子并不一致。我们列出未测试的解释，并说明何时应重新尝试。脚本已公开；权重和邮件数据未公开。

LATTE-WordSeg-Lite: Multi-Granularity Thai Word Segmentation on a CPU, with a Reproducible Benchmark
LATTE-WordSeg-Lite：在CPU上实现多粒度泰语分词并提供可复现的基准
Large language models read Thai through subword tokens, without a word segmenter. Yet Thai treebanks, speech metrics and morphological resources are built on words, often at several granularities, and word boundaries resolve ambiguities that subword tokens leave open. LATTE (Lattice ATTentive Encoding) reads a text at several granularities at once, through a lattice of dictionary words, but it is a large GPU model. We distil it into LATTE-WordSeg-Lite, a CPU segmenter of 1.17M parameters that keeps the lattice as features. It outputs compounds, words and morphemes in one pass, and learns only from annotated data and text whose licences allow commercial use. To compare it with other tools, published Thai scores do not suffice, as they come from different files, splits and scorers. We therefore rebuild seven test sets from pinned sources and score twelve systems under one protocol. With the unit that fits each test set, LATTE-WordSeg-Lite scores above DeepCut on five sets, four of them from corpora that its teachers learnt from. Called line by line on one CPU thread, it runs 23 times as fast as DeepCut. We release the model, the benchmark scripts and all predictions.
中文翻译
大型语言模型通过子词标记读取泰语，缺乏专门的分词器。然而，泰语语料库、语音指标和形态资源均基于词构建，常涉及多个粒度级别，且词边界有助于解决子词标记留下的歧义问题。LATTE（格网注意力编码）通过词典词构成的格网，同时以多种粒度读取文本，但其本身是大型GPU模型。我们将其蒸馏为LATTE-WordSeg-Lite，一个参数量仅为1.17M的CPU分词器，保留格网作为特征。它能在一次遍历中输出复合词、词和词素，且仅从标注数据和允许商业使用的文本中学习。为公平比较，现有公开的泰语得分不足，因来自不同的文件、划分方式和评分工具。因此，我们从固定来源重建了七个测试集，并在统一协议下对十二个系统进行评分。在适配各测试集的单位下，LATTE-WordSeg-Lite在五个测试集中优于DeepCut，其中四个来自其教师模型学习过的语料库。在单个CPU线程上逐行调用时，其速度比DeepCut快23倍。我们已发布模型、基准脚本及所有预测结果。

Benchmarking Large Language Models for Linguistic Annotation
面向语言学标注的大语言模型基准测试
Assessing large language models for linguistic annotation requires task-specific evaluation under documented conditions. We present dhAIBench, a Python benchmarking and annotation tool with a web interface for exploring and sharing results. It records prompts, configurations and predictions, enabling comparisons of annotation quality, confidence calibration, repeatability and estimated cost. We demonstrate the framework and the associated methodology through 293 runs of 48 models on nine linguistic annotation tasks spanning morphology, syntax, semantics, discourse-pragmatics, spelling normalization and learner-language correction. Models achieve high agreement with reference annotations on several tasks, including those on non-standardized, historical varieties as well as requiring contextual interpretation. The results support evaluating models against specific linguistic tasks, rather than relying on general rankings. To this end, we make the current and future benchmarks publicly available at dhaibench.silent3.ff.cuni.cz.
中文翻译
评估大语言模型在语言学标注任务中的表现，需在明确条件下进行特定任务的评估。我们提出dhAIBench，一个具有Web界面的Python基准测试与标注工具，用于探索和共享结果。它记录提示、配置和预测，支持对标注质量、置信度校准、可重复性及估算成本的比较。我们通过在九个语言学标注任务（涵盖形态学、句法、语义、话语-语用、拼写规范化及学习者语言修正）上对48个模型执行293次运行，展示了该框架及其相关方法。模型在多个任务上与参考标注达成高一致性，包括非标准化、历史变体以及需要上下文理解的任务。结果支持针对具体语言学任务评估模型，而非依赖通用排名。为此，我们将在dhaibench.silent3.ff.cuni.cz公开当前及未来基准。

Validating LLM-Based Essay Scorers: A Comparative Analysis in Critical Online Reasoning in Medical Education
验证基于大语言模型的作文评分器：医学教育中批判性在线推理的比较分析
Automated essay scorers (AES) based on large language models (LLMs) promise human-level accuracy. However, training, fine-tuning, and evaluating LLMs for specific assessment tasks is costly. In particular, the question arises whether these AES should be trained for specific domains or whether models based on generic LLMs might be sufficient. Human annotations, by contrast, are often more valid but far more expensive. This study evaluates whether ensembles of AES systems based on general-purpose LLMs can approximate human ratings of medical-education writing tasks by leveraging encoded linguistic and conceptual knowledge. The goal is to assess whether general-purpose models are applicable for assisting or potentially replacing human annotation in this domain. We experiment with 11 AES systems and 8 different LLMs and evaluate 668 student responses to 12 tasks, using \numprint{2076} evaluations by 7 human annotators. These ratings are aggregated to create consistent performance levels that can be used as target classes for classifiers trained on AES outputs. Our results show that learner classes based on human ratings can be accurately reconstructed using a linear SVM trained on a small set of AES features. A single classifier generalized well across tasks and domains, with reasoning and content features being most predictive. This suggests that out-of-the-box LLMs, even without domain-specific fine-tuning, can support automatic essay grading in medical education. While individual AES systems are insufficient alone, their combination approximates human evaluators, pointing to a reduced need for manual scoring or its supplementation with automated methods.
中文翻译
基于大语言模型（LLM）的自动作文评分系统（AES）有望达到人类水平的准确性。然而，为特定评估任务训练、微调和评估LLM成本高昂。特别是，存在一个关键问题：这些AES是否应针对特定领域进行训练，还是通用LLM模型已足够？相比之下，人工标注通常更具有效性，但成本远高于前者。本研究评估了基于通用LLM的AES系统集成能否通过利用编码的语言与概念知识近似人类对医学教育写作任务的评分。目标是判断通用模型是否适用于辅助甚至替代该领域的手工标注。我们实验了11个AES系统和8种不同的LLM，评估了668名学生对12项任务的作答，共获得7位人工标注者提供的2076次评分。这些评分被聚合以创建一致的性能等级，作为基于AES输出训练分类器的目标类别。结果表明，仅使用少量AES特征训练的线性SVM即可准确重建基于人工评分的学习者类别。单一分类器在任务和领域间具有良好的泛化能力，其中推理和内容特征最具预测力。这表明，无需领域特定微调的现成LLM即可支持医学教育中的自动作文评分。尽管单个AES系统不足以独立完成任务，但其组合能逼近人类评价者，提示对人工评分的需求可减少，或可通过自动化方法补充。

Seeing Isn't Resolving: Visual and Linguistic Disambiguation with Conversational Grounding
看见并不等于解决：基于对话情境的视觉与语言消歧
Visual grounding benchmarks usually do not consider the contextual uncertainty of real-world scenarios. In this study, we construct a novel benchmark, the Japanese evaluation for Ambiguous visual Grounding with Dialogue (JAG-D) dataset. It consists of human-robot conversational multimodal interactions covering different types of ambiguity, arising from visual and linguistic categories. We evaluate the capabilities of different state-of-the-art Visual Language Models (VLMs) for ambiguity recognition and resolution. We compare dialogue context grounding performance for visual and linguistic ambiguity resolution. Our experiments show that VLMs can substantially improve the resolution of linguistic ambiguity, especially Japanese zero anaphora, by using dialogue context. We further conduct a comparative analysis to understand whether grounding improvements arise from the semantic content of the dialogue or from its conversational structure.
中文翻译
视觉定位基准通常未考虑现实场景中的上下文不确定性。本研究构建了一个新基准——日本模糊视觉定位对话评估数据集（JAG-D），包含涵盖多种类型模糊性的跨模态人机对话交互，源于视觉和语言类别。我们评估了不同前沿视觉语言模型（VLMs）在模糊性识别与消解方面的能力。对比分析了在视觉与语言模糊性消解中，对话上下文定位的表现差异。实验表明，VLMs能显著提升语言模糊性的消解能力，尤其是日语零回指现象，主要得益于对话上下文的使用。我们进一步进行了对比分析，以理解定位改进是源于对话的语义内容，还是其对话结构。

Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
编辑建议：大语言模型能否预判用户的编辑请求，以及何时可以？
After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M. Through benchmarking and failure analysis, we identify a practical challenge that some cases are inherently difficult to predict in real-world settings. To address this, we introduce decision model-based gating to filter out cases where predictions are unlikely to be correct before they are presented to the user. Our trained model outperforms existing decision models and raises pass@5 among shown suggestions by 12--25 points at a gating threshold. Our code is available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation.
中文翻译
大语言模型（LLM）代理生成成果后，用户常会提出编辑请求。本文研究LLM是否能在请求发出前预判这些请求。此类预判在实践中非常有用，因为它可减少用户审阅与反馈的工作量。我们将此任务形式化为编辑建议，并基于WildChat-4.8M中的真实对话日志构建了EditRecBench基准，用于评估LLM在此任务上的表现。通过基准测试与失败分析，我们识别出一个实际挑战：某些情况在真实场景下本质上难以预测。为应对这一问题，我们引入基于决策模型的门控机制，在将预测结果展示给用户前过滤掉预测可能性低的情况。我们训练的模型优于现有决策模型，在门控阈值下使展示建议的pass@5指标提升了12–25个百分点。相关代码已公开于https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation。

From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
从代码仓库到训练环境：通过环境演化循环扩展长时程编码智能体
Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) often requires model rollouts or model training followed by downstream evaluation, with costs and feedback delays amplified on long-horizon tasks. How can we use timely, reliable proxy signals to improve training value and synthesize environments at scale? We present RepoFactory, an automated pipeline that converts real repositories into verifiable environments where agents build complete projects from scratch given a language specification. Its Environment Evolution Loop optimizes a multiplicative objective combining validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope through proxy feedback. RepoFactory produces 10,159 environments across 17 software domains. Training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on these environments yields RepoHorizen-35B-A3B, which achieves gains of 22.6 percentage points on NL2Repo-Bench and 8.5 points on average across five benchmarks covering long-horizon coding and agentic tasks in real-world production settings, compared with 17.5 and 6.4 points without environment evolution. These results highlight the training value of RepoFactory environments and the additional gains from the Environment Evolution Loop.
中文翻译
训练用于长时程任务的编码智能体需要具备可验证反馈的环境。现有流程通常为线性过程，以验证结束，虽能确立可用性，但对提升训练价值指导有限。递归自改进（RSI）通常需要模型推演或模型训练后进行下游评估，而长时程任务中成本和反馈延迟被放大。如何利用及时、可靠的代理信号来提升训练价值并大规模合成环境？我们提出RepoFactory，一个自动化流水线，将真实代码仓库转化为可验证环境，使智能体在给定语言规范下从零开始构建完整项目。其环境演化循环通过代理反馈优化有效性、结构耦合性和实现范围的乘积目标。RepoFactory在17个软件领域生成了10,159个环境。在这些环境中训练Qwen3.5-35B-A3B得到RepoHorizen-35B-A3B，在NL2Repo-Bench上取得22.6个百分点的提升，五个涵盖真实生产环境中长时程编码与智能体任务基准的平均分提升8.5点，相比无环境演化时的17.5和6.4点。结果凸显了RepoFactory环境的训练价值以及环境演化循环带来的额外增益。

SWE-WhatIf: Simulating Real Users of Coding Agents from Recorded Session
SWE-WhatIf：基于记录会话模拟编码智能体的真实用户
Recorded sessions between users and coding agents offer a way to evaluate how agents complete real-world tasks and interact with users. However, these sessions cannot simply be replayed with new agents, because recorded user replies may no longer apply when an agent takes a different trajectory. We introduce SWE-WhatIf, which replays recorded sessions with new agents by modeling the user's intents, the criteria for satisfying them, and the conditions under which they arise. Using this model, a user simulator generates replies that adapt to unseen agent turns while remaining grounded in the recording. Across 89 real-world sessions, SWE-WhatIf generated the replies most similar to those of real users and matched the strongest baseline when sessions were rewritten. To test adaptation, we replay sessions with agents instructed to avoid or repeat actions that the recorded user pushed back on. SWE-WhatIf produced the highest win rate for avoiding these actions (66.3%), significantly above chance. We further demonstrate its utility by ranking five LLMs as coding agents, where the highest-ranked model depended on how users specified and developed their intents, and a study with 16 users, where replaying their own sessions changed 14 participants' rankings and informed their future agent use.
中文翻译
用户与编码智能体之间的记录会话为评估智能体完成真实任务及与用户互动提供了途径。然而，这些会话无法简单地用新智能体重播，因为当智能体采取不同路径时，原始用户回复可能不再适用。我们引入SWE-WhatIf，通过建模用户的意图、满足意图的标准以及这些标准出现的条件，实现用新智能体重播记录会话。利用该模型，用户模拟器生成适应未见智能体行为的回复，同时保持与原始记录的一致性。在89个真实会话中，SWE-WhatIf生成的回复最接近真实用户回复，并在会话重写测试中达到最强基线表现。为测试适应能力，我们在指令下让智能体避免或重复记录用户反对的动作，SWE-WhatIf在避免这些动作方面取得最高胜率（66.3%），显著高于随机水平。我们进一步通过排名五种LLM作为编码智能体展示了其效用，最高排名取决于用户如何指定和发展其意图；在16名用户的实验中，重播他们自己的会话改变了14名参与者对智能体的评价，并影响了他们未来的使用决策。

Navital Gym: Rule-Graded Agent Environments for Indian Workflows
Navital Gym：面向印度工作流程的规则评分智能体环境
AI agents are being deployed on Indian workflows such as payments, tax, forms, travel and customer support in Hindi and Hinglish. Public agent evaluations rarely cover these workflows, and many score with another language model. We present Navital Gym, a set of six open environments with 321 public tasks in five task families: trip planning, UPI payments and disputes, GST invoicing and returns, form filling (including a multi-document split) and customer support in Hindi, Hinglish and three experimental Indian languages. Every task is graded by named, deterministic rules that recompute the outcome from a synthetic sandbox world. No language model judges any score. We report one run per task for three models on all six environments, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 4.5, and for Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on two (UPI and the Support core). Opus solves 315 of 321 tasks, Sonnet 302 and Haiku 205. Trip planning and Hindi/Hinglish support separate the models most. We also describe a private held-out set that is not published, and a 7B adapter trained in the gym. Code is Apache-2.0 and task data is CC BY 4.0. The rules are a documented simplification of Indian practice, not the live systems.

Experience Rot: Experienced Agents Fail Where Novices Succeed
经验腐化：有经验的智能体在新手成功的地方失败
Agents are increasingly built to learn from experience: they keep conversation histories, memory files, retrieved notes and skills, and reuse what worked before. We show that this experience turns against them when their tools change silently. We test a range of models with tools defined as in the Model Context Protocol (MCP). After a silent change, experienced agents fail on most tasks, while agents new to the task mostly succeed. We call this failure Experience Rot. Experienced agents copy their earlier call instead of checking the current interface, even when the tool definition shows the change. Then they report success. When the documentation is incomplete, experience is what makes agents succeed. After a change, the same experience leaves them worse off than no experience at all. The failure appears in every form of memory we test and grows with the amount of experience. Simple remedies fall short: announcing the update barely helps, and pointing the agent to the documentation fails whenever the documentation does not spell out the answer.

CuRSE-Bench: A Benchmark for Probing Cultural Blind Spots in Text-to-Image Safety Evaluation
CuRSE-Bench：探测文本到图像安全评估中文化盲区的基准
Text-to-image (T2I) safety evaluation typically assigns each prompt or image a single culture-blind harm label, so content that is harmful only within a particular culture can pass as benign. We introduce CultureCraft, an agentic framework that constructs T2I prompts that appear benign under a general-purpose rubric yet carry a latent harmful meaning in a target culture, and use it to build CuRSE-Bench: 10,709 culture-specific prompts and 2,648 culture-general controls over six regions and ten harm axes, each drawn from a predefined knowledge base of documented harm vectors and traceable to at least two independent sources. Scoring every prompt under six region persona judges and a paired culture-blind judge, we find that the culture-blind judge under-rates culture-specific latent harm while matching the persona judges on the controls. Each persona judge, in turn, chiefly decodes its own region's latent harm under our instrument: a selective cultural blind spot that persists in deployed moderators.

GPRM: Global Perspective Process Reward Model
GPRM：全局视角过程奖励模型
Process Reward Models (PRMs) are widely used for step-level evaluation of multi-step reasoning in large language models, but existing methods are often limited by weak historical dependency modeling and insufficient global awareness. They typically fail to leverage prior step evaluations for coherent judgment and lack visibility into subsequent reasoning, leading to suboptimal assessment of intermediate steps. To address this issue, we propose the Global Perspective Process Reward Model (GPRM), which jointly models the problem, previous reasoning steps and their evaluations, the current step, and future steps to enable history-aware and globally informed process evaluation. We further introduce a structured evaluation framework along four dimensions---look back, look ahead, self-check, and goal alignment---to assess prior consistency, future plausibility, step validity, and task alignment. Based on this framework, we construct datasets for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (GRPO). Experiments show that, despite using less training data and smaller model sizes, GPRM outperforms strong baseline models by 7.8 and 5.4 points on PRMBench and ProcessBench, respectively. GPRM also generalizes well across tasks, surpassing the GPT-4.1 baseline on Agent Error Bench, improving strong baselines by around 4 points under test-time scaling (TTS), and achieving competitive performance on PPE.

Can LLMs Give Good Product Advice? A Framework for Diagnosing Failures
大语言模型能否给出好的产品建议？一种诊断失败的框架
Evaluating product advice from a language model requires assessing whether the recommendation meets the user's needs and identifying where the model falls short when it does not. However, matching a product mentioned in an online reply cannot answer either question on its own: several products may be suitable, and the recorded answer may itself be poor advice. When shown a community-listed alternative alongside their own sampled car recommendation, six models prefer the alternative in 1.9 to 6.5 percent of eligible disagreements, consistently across both source-blind presentation orders. We propose a diagnostic framework that separates the user's stated needs, the model's added assumptions, candidate generation, filtering, and final choice, with 19 possible failure modes and the evidence needed to assess them. We apply this framework to product-advice data and to a separate product-selection task with externally assigned relevance labels. The experiments distinguish naming a community-listed product from selecting it and show how answer extraction and candidate-list construction affect the outcome.

MemEmo: Evaluating Emotion in Memory Systems
MemEmo：记忆系统中情感的评估
Memory systems address the challenge of context loss in Large Language Models during prolonged interactions. However, as an essential tool for warm companionship and personalized services, the effectiveness of memory systems in processing affective information remains underexamined. To bridge this gap, we propose an emotion-enhanced memory evaluation benchmark to assess the performance of mainstream and state-of-the-art memory systems in integrating and harnessing emotional information. First, we design a benchmark called \textbf{MemEmo} to assess the affective reasoning and tracking capabilities of memory systems across four dimensions: emotional information extraction, emotional memory updating, emotional memory question-answering, and emotional conflict detection. Second, we construct the \textbf{H}uman-\textbf{L}ike \textbf{M}emory \textbf{E}motion (\textbf{HLME}) dataset to provide an empirical foundation for scrutinizing memory systems. Finally, We evaluate five representative memory systems on the HLME dataset, reporting 11 performance metrics across four dimensions. Experimental results reveal that aggregating scores for all tested memory systems is up to 45\%, far below 100\% scale, exposing a profound disparity between memory system and affective intelligence.

ANCHOR: Cluster-Grounded 5W1H Extraction via Large-Small Model Collaboration
ANCHOR：基于聚类的大-小模型协作式5W1H抽取
Deep semantic understanding of events requires recognizing related events and distinguishing why an event occurs from how it is carried out. 5W1H extraction provides a structured foundation for such understanding by organizing event information around six fundamental questions. However, single-event slot filling provides limited support for these distinctions. We propose ANCHOR, a cluster-grounded framework that combines a large language model (LLM) with a small language model equipped with discriminative heads for accurate 5W1H extraction. The LLM proposes candidate events and generates their initial 4W records, which guide the selection of an event cluster and the subsequent anchoring of its main event. A shared document encoder provides evidence for joint 4W refinement, and two separate sets of boundary and role-scoring heads then extract why and how under event-specific constraints, respectively. Document representations are reused across events and stages, and unsupported roles can remain empty. Following the same principles, an agent-and-skill annotation workflow constructs a benchmark of 26,110 documents from ten source corpora covering three languages and seven domains. We select nine of the resulting datasets to evaluate ANCHOR against strong baselines using four open-weight LLMs. ANCHOR achieves competitive performance. The datasets and code are available at https://github.com/revolution6575/ANCHOR-5W1H.

对事件的深层语义理解需要识别相关事件，并区分事件发生的原因与执行方式。5W1H抽取通过围绕六个基本问题组织事件信息，为这种理解提供了结构化基础。然而，单个事件的槽位填充对这些区分的支持有限。我们提出ANCHOR，一种基于聚类的框架，结合大型语言模型（LLM）与配备判别性头部的小型语言模型，以实现精确的5W1H抽取。LLM提出候选事件并生成其初始4W记录，指导事件聚类的选择及主事件的锚定。共享文档编码器提供联合4W优化的证据，随后两组独立的边界和角色评分头部分别在事件特定约束下提取“为什么”和“如何”。文档表示在不同事件和阶段间复用，未支持的角色可留空。遵循相同原则，我们构建了一个涵盖十份来源语料库、三种语言和七个领域的26,110篇文档的基准数据集。我们选取其中九个数据集，使用四种开源权重LLM对ANCHOR与强基线进行对比评估。ANCHOR表现出竞争力。相关数据集与代码已公开于https://github.com/revolution6575/ANCHOR-5W1H。

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for industrial tasks, yet few benchmarks evaluate their mastery of industrial knowledge across different types of cognitive demand. We introduce IndustrialKnowEval (IndKnow), a benchmark for industrial knowledge and engineering question answering. It contains 43,282 samples covering 21 task types across seven industrial sectors, including aerospace, electric power, and metallurgy, organized into four levels of cognitive demand: memory, comprehension, reasoning, and engineering application. Enterprise-based domain specialists and experienced researchers participate in all stages of dataset construction and quality control. We conduct a series of experiments on 18 representative LLMs, with domain experts deeply involved in the evaluation. Building upon IndKnow, we propose the Industrial Cognitive Capability Gap (ICCG) metric to characterize the performance differential between foundational industrial knowledge and higher-order reasoning and application, and we analyze it alongside absolute performance to provide a more complete view of model capabilities. We anticipate that IndustrialKnowEval will support the benchmarking of LLMs in industrial scenarios and promote the development of robust industrial intelligence. Code is available at: https://github.com/J4cksonLee/IndKnow

MetaAct: Self-Evolving Executable Action Constraints for Embodied Language Agents
MetaAct：具身语言智能体的自演化可执行动作约束
Self-evolving language agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for continuously improving agent behavior through experience. However, most existing approaches evolve textual artifacts, which can influence action preferences but cannot reliably enforce action admissibility in embodied environments with discrete and often irreversible actions. We propose MetaAct, which shifts self-evolution from textual guidance to executable action constraints by synthesizing GEAR (Grounded Executable Action Rules) from execution feedback. Each rule is represented as a typed specification, compiled into a deterministic guard, and validated offline through trajectory replay without additional model calls or environment interactions. Across four benchmarks, MetaAct improves task performance; on ScienceWorld and WebShop, violations drop from 70% to 0% and 40% to 1%, with score gains of +10.1 and +8.0. Our code is available at https://github.com/BaiCubed/MetaAct.

Venues and benchmarks read LLM review scores as measurements of a paper, while providers replace their models within months. We audit twenty frontier models from OpenAI, Google and Anthropic on ICLR 2027 submissions while they were under review, with tests registered before the decisions. Between an earlier and a later version of Claude Opus and of Gemini, the share of papers placed on the accept side falls by 52 and 53 percentage points on 183 and 60 randomly drawn submissions, and by 43 to 79 points in six further paired comparisons, with no paper moving up in any of them. Stating a 30% acceptance rate in the prompt leaves a gap of 79 points between the two Opus versions. When score-stripped critiques are swapped between versions, the later critiques alone lower the accept share by 35 points for Opus and 51 for Gemini; for Opus the drop is 35 points under a third-party scorer and 24 after a rewrite that keeps each technical point and removes evaluative wording. On 57 papers, the percentiles of Opus 4.6 and 5.5 correlate at 0.73 while their accept shares differ by 44 points. On 99 to 119 submissions, the self-estimated percentiles of three models correlate with two human reviewers more strongly than a third reviewer does (point estimates 0.17 to 0.21, 95% intervals between -0.04 and +0.42). All twenty models give a 2 or a 3 in 473 of their 475 reviews, against 60 of 72 human reviews. Retrospective tests on decided papers can draw on memory. Claude Opus 5.5 names the true first author of 27 decided ICLR 2026 papers from their titles alone, with no wrong name, and Claude Opus 4.6 accepted all 11 decided papers it said it recognized, against 5 expected. Thresholds on LLM-reviewer scores therefore have to be validated against human decisions for each model version; our tests against the ICLR 2027 decisions follow on 16 December 2026.

Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
不变性感知的Harness强化机制：保护LLM智能体免受静默API故障影响
LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. It tests each result against invariants that any correct API must satisfy and withholds values that break one. We find silent failures in 11 of 15 public research APIs, with counts inflated up to 691 times. Current fixes leave over 70% of answers wrong, and agents report 77.4% of counts a judge flags. Across 7 open models, SilentGuard cuts wrong answers on its target faults from 74.0% to 1.7%, with no loss on fault-free tasks. On three frontier models they fall from 70.2% to 0.5%. A warning from the same check leaves 70.1% wrong, so enforcement is the key. On new fault types, the harness alone cuts wrong answers from 61.1% to 24.5%. It avoids wrong answers by abstaining rather than recovering.
中文翻译
LLM智能体通过调用API并信任其结果来回答问题。然而，API可能静默失败——忽略请求中的部分内容（如命名错误的过滤器），但仍返回HTTP 200状态码和看似合理但错误的结果。当前修复方法（如检查清单、评审模型和LLM裁判）要求模型自行发现此类问题，但模型常在发现问题后仍继续作答。我们提出SilentGuard，将决策从模型转移到执行工具调用的Harness中。它通过测试每个结果是否满足任何正确API都必须满足的不变性条件，并屏蔽违反条件的值。我们在15个公开研究API中发现了11个静默故障，错误计数最高被夸大了691倍。现有修复方法仍使超过70%的答案错误，且智能体报告77.4%的计数被裁判标记。在7个开源模型上，SilentGuard将目标故障下的错误答案从74.0%降至1.7%，且在无故障任务上无性能损失；在三个前沿模型上，错误率从70.2%降至0.5%。相同的警告提示仍导致70.1%的答案错误，说明强制执行是关键。对于新型故障类型，仅使用Harness即可将错误答案从61.1%降至24.5%。该方法通过拒绝回答而非尝试恢复来避免错误。

Large language models (LLMs) increasingly drive engineering analysis end to end, turning textual records into the inputs of numerical programs, but a plausible and wrong value can pass silently into a decision. We propose deterministic validation gates for LLM-driven engineering analysis, a general paradigm in which a typed configuration produced by LLMs is consumed only after it passes deterministic checks on units, physical consistency, verbatim quotes, agreement between independent models, consistency with measurement exports and the applicability of trained models. The gates target hallucinations from two directions, since quote checking catches fabricated content while agreement between models catches errors of omission that quote checking misses. We instantiate the paradigm on sine vibration acceptance testing for low Earth orbit mega-constellation satellites, where DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Qwen-plus read Chinese test records and extract a configuration of 76 fields. Fact-level F1 ranged from 0.98 to 1.0 on five input variants, with all repairs frozen on development inputs and evaluated on held-out inputs. With all gates, 20 of 20 configurations produced notching results bit for bit identical to the gold run, and all 17 real and injected errors in consumed fields were stopped, of which 16 would have run without gates. Retraining the bound model on a dataset built from an LLM configuration reproduced its results within GPU nondeterminism. We also report a negative result of practical value. Direct LLM curve forecasting only matches linear extrapolation, whereas a small physics-structured network reduces the over-notched bandwidth by 86% to 89% at calibrated coverage c = 0.90, which delineates where direct LLM prediction should give way to a trained model.

When Should Decision Models Compare Candidates?
决策模型应在何时比较候选方案？
Language-model agents frequently select among candidate actions, such as tools and web elements. Should decision models score candidates independently or allow their scores to depend on other candidates? We investigate this question by comparing three approaches: Pointwise scoring, Setwise scoring, and Candidate Attention. Across five agent-decision benchmarks, Pointwise scoring remains competitive, while Setwise scoring performs better on some tool-selection and binary-decision tasks. Candidate Attention does not consistently improve upon Pointwise scoring, despite allowing cross-candidate interaction. Using two controlled synthetic tasks, we further examine whether models learn to use candidate-set information. With targeted relational training, Setwise models learn candidate dependencies and generalize to shifted inputs, while Candidate Attention shows weaker transfer. Our results show that access to other candidates does not guarantee effective comparison, and that its benefits depend on both task requirements and training.
中文翻译
语言模型代理经常需要在多个候选动作（如工具和网页元素）之间进行选择。决策模型应独立评分还是允许评分依赖于其他候选项？我们通过比较三种方法来探究这一问题：逐项评分（Pointwise scoring）、集合评分（Setwise scoring）和候选注意力（Candidate Attention）。在五个代理决策基准测试中，逐项评分表现依然具有竞争力，而集合评分在部分工具选择和二元决策任务中表现更优。候选注意力虽允许候选项之间的交互，但并未持续优于逐项评分。通过两个受控的合成任务，我们进一步考察模型是否学会利用候选集信息。经过针对性的关系训练，集合评分模型学会了候选依赖关系并能泛化到输入偏移情况，而候选注意力的迁移能力较弱。结果表明，访问其他候选项并不保证有效比较，其优势取决于任务需求和训练方式。

Do We Still Need Fine-Tuned Classifiers? Swapping Typed Decision Models into 24 ACL-Venue Papers
我们是否仍需要微调分类器？在24篇ACL会议论文中替换有类型决策模型
Typed Decision Models such as TypeSafe's Jev, also called System One or System 1 models, answer typed questions about an input with a probability for each option, and they need no training. Many NLP papers still fine-tune a task-specific classifier, and prompted large language models (LLMs) trail such classifiers on most text classification benchmarks. We ask how many of these fine-tuned classifiers a Typed Decision Model can replace under each paper's own evaluation, and what is needed where it cannot. We swap the predictors of 24 ACL-venue papers for Jev, keep each paper's splits, label definitions and metric, and check the results with Cloudflare's Clef, Microsoft-Decision-1 and OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna Decisions. The resulting 46 English test sets, with their questions and published scores, form the TDM-Gauntlet benchmark. With a zero-shot prompt, Jev directly replaced the paper's predictor on 12 of the 46 test sets, mostly single judgments with plain labels, but rarely where the paper's method was trained on its labels. Where Jev scored lower, we most often attributed the shortfall to an annotation convention that the label name does not state. With 500 training labels plus validation and no user-managed GPU, calibration and GEPA-style prompt optimization closed a median 72% of the gap to the paper's method, about twice what off-the-shelf GEPA closed, for a median $1.66 per search. On the same labels, fine-tuned encoders such as RoBERTa and DeBERTa closed 59%, and LoRA fine-tuning of the open LLM Qwen3.8-27B closed 97%. Fine-tuning remains the most accurate option, but a zero-shot prompt is often enough for plain labels, and prompt optimization closes most of the remaining gap.
中文翻译
有类型决策模型（如TypeSafe的Jev，又称系统一或系统1模型）可对输入中的选项回答带概率的问题，且无需训练。然而，许多NLP论文仍会微调特定任务的分类器，且提示过的大型语言模型（LLM）在多数文本分类基准上仍落后于这些分类器。我们探讨在每篇论文自身的评估条件下，有类型决策模型能替代多少微调分类器，以及在无法替代时需要什么。我们将24篇ACL会议论文的预测器替换为Jev，保留每篇论文的数据划分、标签定义和评估指标，并使用Cloudflare的Clef、Microsoft-Decision-1和OpenAI的GPT-6 Luna Decisions验证结果。由此生成的46个英文测试集及其问题和已发表分数构成了TDM-Gauntlet基准。在零样本提示下，Jev直接取代了论文预测器在46个测试集中的12个，主要集中在带有简单标签的单一判断任务，但在论文方法基于标签训练的任务中很少成功。当Jev得分较低时，我们最常归因于标签名称未明确表达标注惯例。在提供500个训练标签及验证集、无需用户管理GPU的情况下，校准和GEPA风格提示优化将差距缩小了72%的中位数，约为现成GEPA的两倍，平均每次搜索成本仅为1.66美元。在同一标签上，微调编码器如RoBERTa和DeBERTa缩小了59%的差距，而开放LLM Qwen3.8-27B的LoRA微调则缩小了97%的差距。微调仍是最高精度的选择，但对简单标签而言，零样本提示通常已足够，而提示优化可弥合大部分剩余差距。

Risk-certified prompt optimization for LLM-as-a-judge guardrails
面向LLM作为裁判防护机制的风险认证提示优化
LLM-as-a-judge guardrails are often controlled primarily through system prompts, yet standard prompt optimization methods target average performance rather than explicit safety constraints. This paper studies system-prompt selection as a constrained optimization problem: maximize benign pass rate while keeping the missed-attack rate below a user-specified level α with finite-sample statistical control. The framework combines LLM-based judging, automatic prompt generation, and distribution-free risk certification. This work instantiates it in two procedures: CPS and CRISP. CPS generates a fixed pool of prompts from training data, then certifies candidates on a held-out evaluation set using simultaneous upper confidence bounds and selects the certified prompt with the highest benign utility. CRISP instead integrates risk feedback into an adaptive search, using hard example-guided rewriting and a reusable-holdout interface to steer generation toward the feasible utility frontier. Experiments on four datasets covering prompt injection, system-prompt leakage, and sensitive-information disclosure show that risk-certified selection consistently respects the target missed-attack level on heldout tests, while utility improves as the permitted risk is relaxed. CRISP is especially useful when fixed-pool search fails to produce certifiable high-utility candidates.
中文翻译
LLM作为裁判的防护机制通常主要通过系统提示进行控制，但标准的提示优化方法侧重于平均性能而非明确的安全约束。本文将系统提示选择建模为一个带约束的优化问题：在保持遗漏攻击率低于用户指定水平α的前提下，最大化良性通过率，并采用有限样本的统计控制。该框架结合了基于LLM的评判、自动提示生成和无分布风险认证。本文实现了两种具体方法：CPS和CRISP。CPS从训练数据中生成一组固定提示池，然后在保留的评估集上使用同时置信上限对候选提示进行认证，并选择具有最高良性效用的认证提示。CRISP则将风险反馈整合到自适应搜索中，利用硬例引导重写和可复用的保留接口，引导生成过程向可行效用边界靠近。在涵盖提示注入、系统提示泄露和敏感信息泄露的四个数据集上的实验表明，风险认证的选择在保留测试中始终遵守目标遗漏攻击水平，同时随着允许风险的放宽，效用持续提升。当固定池搜索无法产生可认证的高效用候选时，CRISP尤其有用。

Can decision models extract clinical data from cancer pathology reports? An evaluation of accuracy, calibration, and failure modes
决策模型能否从癌症病理报告中提取临床数据？准确性、校准性和失效模式的评估
Decision models are a new class of language model that, instead of generating text, choose one option per question from a fixed list and return a probability for every option. They have not yet been evaluated on clinical text. We evaluated two open-weights decision models, Nimble 9B and Tev1 4B, for extracting 25 fields from 1,113 oral cavity cancer pathology reports from a single centre, against a prospectively maintained clinical database. We compared them with two generative models: Qwen3.5 9B, run locally, and GLM-5.3-flash, run through a cloud API. Tev1 reached a mean field accuracy of 0.917 (95% CI 0.913 to 0.920), the same as Qwen3.5 9B (0.918; p = 0.26), and was four times faster (15 s against 61 s per report). Nimble reached 0.862 and GLM-5.3-flash 0.986. Both decision models matched GLM-5.3-flash on simple dichotomous categories. They were weak on measurements binned into categories, on fields whose correct answer was not reported, and on some complex decisions (e.g. involved margins). We found that the main cause of the inferior performance of Nimble's came from asking 25 questions in one request: with two questions per request, its accuracy improved. Pooled over fields, the returned probabilities were well calibrated (expected calibration error 0.022 and 0.026), but they did not flag systematic errors within single fields. A simulated strategy of sending answers with a probability below 0.94 to GLM-5.3-flash raised Tev1's accuracy to 0.982, with 38% of answers escalated. Decision models can extract explicitly stated findings from pathology reports quickly on local hardware and return useful probabilities. They should be validated in the configuration in which they will be used, restricted to the fields in which they are reliable, and combined with other methods for numeric values.

决策模型是一类新型的语言模型，它们不生成文本，而是从固定列表中为每个问题选择一个选项，并返回每个选项的概率。这类模型尚未在临床文本上进行评估。我们评估了两个开源权重的决策模型Nimble 9B和Tev1 4B，从单一中心的1,113份口腔癌病理报告中提取25个字段，对比一个前瞻性维护的临床数据库。我们将它们与两个生成式模型进行比较：本地运行的Qwen3.5 9B和通过云API运行的GLM-5.3-flash。Tev1的平均字段准确率为0.917（95%置信区间0.913至0.920），与Qwen3.5 9B的0.918（p = 0.26）相当，且速度提升四倍（每份报告15秒 vs 61秒）。Nimble得分为0.862，GLM-5.3-flash得分为0.986。两个决策模型在简单二分类任务上与GLM-5.3-flash表现一致。它们在将测量值分箱为类别、正确答案未被报告的字段以及某些复杂判断（如边缘是否受累）方面表现较弱。我们发现Nimble表现较差的主要原因是将25个问题一次性请求处理：当改为每次请求两个问题时，其准确率显著提升。在所有字段上汇总来看，返回的概率具有良好校准性（预期校准误差为0.022和0.026），但未能识别单个字段中的系统性错误。模拟策略中，将概率低于0.94的答案发送给GLM-5.3-flash，使Tev1的准确率提升至0.982，其中38%的答案被升级处理。决策模型能够在本地硬件上快速提取病理报告中明确陈述的发现，并返回有用的概率。它们应在实际使用配置下进行验证，仅限于其可靠的字段范围内使用，并与其他方法结合以处理数值型数据。

Sindhi is a low-resource Indo-Aryan language written mainly in an extended Perso-Arabic script. Several Sindhi tokenizers have been released on public model hubs, but they have not been compared with one another on shared data. We train SentencePiece Unigram tokenizers with byte fallback at four vocabulary sizes (32k to 150k) on about 1.10 million Sindhi sentences and a smaller, repeated Urdu, Persian and Arabic slice, from four public sources, and compare them with fourteen existing tokenizers on four evaluation sets: FLORES+, Sindhi Wikipedia, a news-derived sentiment corpus, and a contemporary news corpus. The metrics are fertility, single-token retention, UNK rate, byte-fallback rate, and round-trip character loss. At 64k, our tokenizer averages 1.147 tokens per word, against 1.208 for the best existing tokenizer and 1.512 for XLM-RoBERTa, and keeps 88.6% of words as single tokens. On fertility, single-token retention and UNK rate it is best or tied for best in all four evaluation sets at 64k and above; at 32k it trails one baseline on FLORES+. Margins over the best Sindhi-adapted baselines are small (0.002 fertility on FLORES+ at 64k), and we report no significance tests. A round-trip check finds no character loss for our tokenizer and silent character deletion (up to 0.85% of characters) in two existing ones; seven others lose less than 0.1%. We evaluate intrinsic metrics only, so effects on downstream tasks remain untested. Code and tokenizer files are public (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23962474).

A Dataset for Misogyny Detection in Polish Social Media: Transferability of Hateful Speech Detection from General to Specific Types of Hate

Harmful language detection is commonly evaluated on broadly defined hate speech and toxicity benchmarks, yet it remains unclear whether models that successfully detect harmful language in general can transfer this capability to more specific forms of hate. We investigate this problem for misogyny detection in Polish, an area for which dedicated resources remain scarce. We introduce a new dataset of Polish social media comments annotated for misogyny, gender-directed hateful speech. Using this resource, we first assess the reliability of LLM-assisted annotation and then evaluate general-to-specific transfer by comparing models trained on general harmful language data, safety-specialized models, and models fine-tuned directly for misogyny detection. Our results show that strong performance on general harmful language detection does not transfer uniformly to misogyny; safety-specialized models demonstrate substantially stronger generalization ability. The study contributes a new Polish resource for gender-directed harmful language and demonstrates that the scope and granularity of prior safety training are important factors in transferring harmful language detection from general to specific forms of hate.

Offline language models could extend access to maternal-health information where internet connectivity is unreliable, but deployment requires both clinically appropriate responses and feasible local execution. This study presents an offline Android assistant integrating ready-made quantized language models, a clinically validated local knowledge package, conversational context, and model-initiated local retrieval. Gemma 4 E2B and Qwen3.5 0.8B were compared across 45 conversations and 312 turns per configuration, including a dedicated offline agentic benchmark. Gemma achieved higher response-quality, context-retention, and safety scores; Qwen offered faster generation and lower memory use. Clinician assessment of 150 Gemma responses across nine clinical domains yielded a mean quality score of 3.80/4, with 147 responses meeting the acceptance criterion. A paired RAG-on/off experiment evaluated 74 questions: retrieval improved 11 responses, left 56 neutral, produced four adverse response changes, and left three pairs unassessable. RAG-on had descriptively higher mean usefulness, safety, correctness, and actionability in the conditional 70-pair subset excluding the four flagged pairs from both conditions. Physical-device testing demonstrated offline responses on a 6 GB Android handset, with a 14.3 s median latency, alongside successful reconnection synchronization in the integrated application. Together, the findings document clinical response quality and practical performance of the integrated offline maternal-health assistant.

Anatomy of an Agent Harness: Decisions, Invariants and Corner Cases
智能体框架剖析：决策、不变性与边界情况
An agent harness is the program around a language model that turns its replies into actions: it builds each request, runs the tools the model asks for, decides what the model may do without asking, stores the conversation, recovers from failures, and shows a person what happened. Most of these decisions are made in code and rarely written down, so each harness meets the same corner cases again. This paper writes them down as invariants to test. It gives a system model with trust boundaries; 30 decision cards in six groups, each with options and costs, an invariant, the corner cases that break it, a test and an evidence tag; six cause classes for failures; a test method built on scripted providers, recorded behaviour and planted changes; and a checklist. The cards come from building one desktop harness, Crewroom, the author's own, and from manually testing ten other harnesses and studying open-source harnesses as reference; some patterns in the cards were adopted from those, so the catalogue is not independent of them. Of the 83 invariant clauses, 56 are tagged Tested, 12 Believed and 15 Open. The checklist is applied to the author's harness as one worked example, by its builder with no second rater: of its 30 items, 11 hold, 14 do not and 5 were not tested. It is not a ranking. The paper makes no claims about answer quality or cost or other platforms, and does not evaluate or rank other harnesses.
中文翻译
智能体框架是围绕语言模型编写的程序，将模型回复转化为具体行动：构建请求、调用模型所需的工具、决定无需询问即可执行的操作、存储对话历史、从故障中恢复，并向用户展示发生的情况。这些决策大多由代码实现，且极少被记录下来，因此每个框架都会反复遭遇相同的边界情况。本文将这些决策以不变性形式明确列出并加以测试。提出一个包含信任边界的系统模型；包含六个类别共30张决策卡，每张卡包含选项与代价、不变性定义、破坏它的边界情况、测试方法及证据标签；六类失败原因分类；基于脚本提供者、记录行为和植入变更的测试方法；以及一份检查清单。这些卡片源自作者开发的桌面框架Crewroom，以及对另外十款框架的手动测试和对开源框架的研究参考；部分模式借鉴自已有框架，因此该目录并非完全独立。在83个不变性条款中，56个已测试，12个被认为成立，15个仍开放。检查清单由作者作为构建者应用到自身框架中，无第二评审者参与：30项中有11项成立，14项不成立，5项未测试。本文不涉及回答质量、成本或其他平台的评价，也不对其他框架进行评估或排名。

Retrieval-augmented systems that research companies are judged by how much they find, yet in markets where public evidence is sparse, a confident answer without support costs more than no answer. We introduce AfriBizClaims, a benchmark of 150 company-research queries across six African markets in English, French and Portuguese, including queries about fictitious companies that a correct system must decline. Each claim a system makes is judged against the page it cites by an AI judge, checked against a second AI judge from another model family and against two human annotators, and abstentions are scored against answerability labels. We compare BM25 over a pooled corpus, standard web retrieval-augmented generation, and a multi-step agent pipeline (Konexium V1), all using the same language model. The two simple baselines are well attributed: 98% of their judged claims are supported by the page they cite, and they decline every field of every fictitious company. Counting claims about a company other than the one asked about as errors, the agent pipeline's per-query precision is 68%, and it never answers a question about a named company correctly: it substitutes other firms, including for 5 of the 24 fictitious names, and it is the least stable between runs and the most expensive. In the pipeline we evaluated, more steps between the query and the evidence did not buy more grounded answers. We will release the queries, system outputs, labels and short evidence excerpts.

Most biomedical bi-encoders are built on BERTBase-sized encoders pretrained with masked language modeling (MLM). These encoders are costly for corpus-scale indexing and latency-sensitive query encoding, and MLM does not explicitly train the [CLS] vector that a bi-encoder uses to represent a whole text. Bioformer-RetroMAE outperformed BioBERT and PubMedBERT bi-encoders fine-tuned under identical settings on all metrics, despite having about 40% of their parameters and producing 512-dimensional rather than 768-dimensional vectors. Compared with PubMedBERT, it improved mean average precision (MAP) by 37.0% and Recall@100 by 29.1%. Compared with the original Bioformer8L}, RetroMAE pretraining improved MAP by 53.6% and Recall@100 by 32.8% without changing model size or inference cost. In hybrid retrieval, fusing Bioformer-RetroMAE with BM25 through weighted reciprocal rank fusion improved MAP and NDCG@10 over BM25 alone by 4.9% and 4.6%, respectively, larger gains than those obtained by fusing BM25 with PubMedBERT or BioBERT.

NoLBERT-Calls: Reading Earnings Calls Without Hindsight
NoLBERT-Calls：无需事后洞察地阅读财报电话会议
Language models are now a standard tool for measuring what managers say on earnings calls, but the encoders behind these measures were usually pretrained on text from the same years a backtest covers. Holding out a test period does not remove that hindsight, because it sits in the features. We adapt NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, to earnings calls without letting it read anything dated after 31 December 2023. The calls supply the training signal themselves: every analyst question is followed by management's answer, and the model learns to pick that answer out from the other answers of the same call. We test on every US call from January 2025 to October 2026 (20,323 calls, 254,575 questions) and make every modeling choice on calls from 2024. The adapted model, NoLBERT-Calls-2023, ranks the true answer first for 78.0% of questions (95% interval 77.8-78.2; chance 8.0%), against 26.3% before adaptation. It is 1.0 point ahead of a call-adapted ChronoBERT, 3.4 points ahead of a call-adapted FinBERT, and 18.7 and 19.8 points ahead of the best off-the-shelf retriever and BM25. A year-by-year test over 2013-2026 finds no look-ahead premium: relative to a model adapted only through 2012, the released model does no better on the years it was trained on than on years it never saw. The price of the cutoff is compute: under one shared 150-minute recipe NoLBERT adapts least well of four encoders, and its lead comes from a longer, staged adaptation of about 13 GPU-hours.

Singapore offers a distinctive testbed for legal reasoning by large language models (LLMs). Its legal system combines inherited English common law with jurisdiction-specific statutes, requiring models to distinguish local doctrine from generic common-law intuition. This setting also highlights the challenge of recognizing underspecification in lay legal queries, because the facts material to a legal outcome depend on the governing doctrine. Yet legal benchmarks rarely cover Singapore law or test this form of ambiguity recognition. To address these gaps, we introduce SG-LegalClarify, a large-scale benchmark for open-ended legal reasoning and ambiguity recognition in Singapore law. SG-LegalClarify contains 1,100 lawyer-authored source questions spanning 10 legal domains, including 340 fully specified and 760 underspecified questions. Each underspecified question has a fixed hidden-fact assignment and a fully specified counterpart, yielding 1,860 evaluation instances. Responses are graded with lawyer-authored Issue, Rule, Application, and Conclusion (IRAC) rubrics. We evaluate 19 LLMs, closed-book and with web search, using a multi-turn pipeline in which models decide whether to answer or clarify, and a user simulator reveals hidden facts only when asked. We find the benchmark far from saturated: the best models satisfy only 69.8% of mandatory rubric items closed-book (average 53.8%) and 77.8% with web search (average 63.0%). Models also struggle to recognize when clarification is necessary. We will release the public split of our benchmark, the model outputs on it, and the evaluation pipeline to support future research.

Large language models (LLMs) achieve high scores on medical benchmarks, but does this performance translate into reliable diagnosis as a conversation unfolds? In diagnostic conversations, users can provide clinical findings across multiple turns, ask for a diagnosis without supplying answer options, and introduce opinions from others. Models must therefore form diagnoses from the available evidence and decide how to respond to subsequent advice. We introduce ROUNDS, a framework that evaluates these abilities after a fixed sequence of clinical evidence delivered over multiple turns. ROUNDS compares diagnosis with and without answer options, presents the same incorrect diagnosis under clinician and lay framing, and varies support for competing diagnoses in written five-clinician panels. Across seven models and 1,035 cases from five datasets, average accuracy was 76.9% with answer options and 57.0% without them. Clinician-framed misleading advice produced lower final accuracy than lay-framed advice in every model, with differences of 4.6 to 38.2 percentage points. Initially correct diagnoses more often became incorrect answers than abstentions, and many adopted the suggested disease. Conversely, accuracy increased as more panel members supported the correct diagnosis, including when the majority opinion remained unchanged. These findings reveal a gap between medical benchmark performance and reliable diagnosis in conversation: models respond to external opinions, but remain vulnerable to abandoning correct diagnoses without new clinical evidence.

We ask whether giving a model access to these resources improves machine translation from the four languages into English, and whether it matters how the access is provided: as analyses computed in advance and written into the prompt, or as tools that the model calls itself through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). We evaluate manually: an expert linguist read every English output of the strongest model under three conditions, 816 sentences in all, accepted or rejected each one, and named the main error in every rejected translation. With the analyses in the prompt, the number of accepted translations rises from 13 to 43 out of 272; with the tools attached it rises to 55. The gain comes from the bilingual dictionary. For Udmurt, whose dictionary has no English side, the prompt-based condition brings no gain at all, while for the other three languages an English gloss reaches the prompt for 74 to 80% of the source words. Tool calling is also much harder to get working than prompt injection. Of 31 open-weight models, 14 never call a tool, 11 of them because they cannot produce a usable call, and half of the calls that are made name a language the toolkit does not support. We release the data set, every model output and all tool-call logs.

Health systems increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to draft summaries of patient medical records, yet evaluations now find omissions, the absence of clinically important information, to be the most common failure mode. Detecting omissions in an LLM-generated summary requires knowing which facts in the record are salient, a signal that existing methods hand-specify, ignore, or recompute at inference with costly LLM judges. We present OmitEHR, a reference-free omission detector that learns clinical salience from historical clinician-written summaries predating widespread LLM use. We apply OmitEHR to brief hospital course (BHC) summarization using 5,000 admissions from a large academic medical center. On held-out admissions, OmitEHR outperformed all evaluated baselines at predicting salient source sentences, including a prompted LLM judge. The full omission detection pipeline took 17.7 to 19.5 seconds and cost \$0.03 to \$0.13 per summary depending on the base model, 1.6 to 1.7 times faster and 5.6 to 6.7 times cheaper than scoring every source sentence with an LLM judge. In a blinded review of 25 admissions, two board-certified clinicians confirmed a mean of 5.6 clinically meaningful omissions per summary surfaced by OmitEHR, compared with 3.3 for a full LLM pipeline, counting candidates confirmed by at least one clinician. The efficiency and validity of OmitEHR make it a practical tool for health systems to flag omissions before a summary reaches the clinician.

Omni-modal agents are expected to move beyond multimodal understanding toward completing complex tasks in realistic multimodal environments. In these settings, information is distributed across heterogeneous files and modalities, with cross-file and cross-modal dependencies requiring agents to continually coordinate perception, reasoning, and tool use as newly gathered evidence informs subsequent actions. However, existing omni-modal benchmarks primarily focus on multimodal perception and understanding, leaving complex task completion through sustained interaction with multimodal workspaces underexplored. We introduce Omni-Workspace, a benchmark comprising 380 deep-research-style tasks across four multimodal workspace types and two difficulty levels. Further analysis identifies multimodal context inflation and task-state drift as recurring challenges. Motivated by these findings, we further propose OmniFocus, a lightweight approach combining multimodal working-memory management with explicit task-state tracking to improve performance and efficiency. Omni-Workspace advances the evaluation and development of omni-modal agents toward autonomous completion of complex tasks in multimodal workspaces.

We introduce BW-PO based on the Blocksworld domain, a controlled benchmark that reduces existing VLM planners and formalizers to near-zero performance, and propose VLM-as-perceiver, a paradigm that narrows the VLM's role to local perception while delegating cross-view evidence reconciliation and plan generation to external solvers. Across model-specific challenging subsets of BW-PO, this raises plan success from 1% to 97% for Gemma-4-31B, 0% to 95% for Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 3% to 84% for Gemini-3.1-Pro. Isolating perception in this way separates two bottlenecks that are otherwise entangled: reconciliation under depth ambiguity, and completeness of visual extraction under scene density.

Absolute accuracy stays low (14 of 40 without retrieval and 20 of 40 with it). Word error rates were low (6.03, 4.93 and 1.47%), but the error on amounts was 13.01% and 12.61% in the cascades, against 2.86% in GPT-Live. With default settings, Pipecat and LiveKit stopped at almost every backchannel and often took it as the carrier's answer: an "ok" spoken over the agent ended in a registered agreement in 3 of 15 Pipecat calls, 2 of 15 LiveKit calls and no GPT-Live call (descriptive counts, not tested). Instruction-guided text-to-speech (ITTS) lets users specify voice properties in natural language. Applications from conversational AI character voices to synthetic training data for downstream speech models depend on the system producing many distinct voices when the same broad category is requested repeatedly. No prior work audits whether ITTS outputs are in fact diverse, either compared to real speech or across attribute values. We evaluate seven open-source ITTS systems using speaker embeddings whose representational capacity we independently validate. Every system produces speaker distributions markedly narrower than real speech. Furthermore, female prompts produce less diverse voice pools than male prompts across most systems. In contrast, accent and emotion prompts barely alter speaker diversity in most systems, but reveal a strong controllability bias toward North American English and neutral speech. These results show that diversity and controllability capture complementary weaknesses, neither of which alone is sufficient to evaluate ITTS. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/dlion168/ITTS-Speaker-Diversity.

Legal reasoning in civil-law systems is not rule-lookup: the German state examination asks for a structured opinion (Gutachten) that names the governing norms, applies them to the facts, and argues to a conclusion. We introduce GPBam (German Public Law Bar-style Exam), 81 public-law examination cases with reference solutions, paired with a recitation task over 200 statutory provisions. Drawn from state examination preparation, the cases are broad and rarely repeat, and are not publicly available - we find no evidence of exact-solution memorisation in the models we evaluate, and keeping them private limits contamination. Because each reference solution's cited norms form a retrieval gold set over the very instances the essays are graded on, GPBam scores retrieval and long-form generation jointly, which makes it a benchmark for legal retrieval as well as for legal writing and lets us ask how much retrieval quality a legal opinion actually needs. Across 32 open-weight and proprietary models evaluated without retrieval, scores span 4.81-76.42 out of 100. Supplying the law helps modestly: across seven models and eight retrieval configurations, retrieval performance varies nearly threefold and buys at most 4.1 essay points, and nothing significant for three of the seven, while an oracle with 91% gold-norm recall improves scores by 2-6 points. Essay quality strongly tracks prior knowledge: verbatim statute recall, measured in a separate task, correlates at $ρ= 0.92$ over 32 models.

Mapping the Afterlife of Future Work Statements in NLP Research
映射NLP研究中未来工作陈述的生命周期
Future work statements are one of the few places in scientific papers where authors explicitly describe what they think should happen next. We study what happens to such statements after publication. We construct a dataset of 72,070 future work items extracted from 23,113 ACL Anthology papers published between 1979 and 2025, categorize them by type, retrieve candidate follow-up papers through citation-based and content-based search, and use LLM-based judgments to assess whether later papers pursue the proposed directions. Using this resource, we analyze patterns across time, venues, categories, themes, and authors. We find that many items are later addressed, often within a few years, with clear differences across types and themes and a largely community-driven pattern. Our results suggest that future work statements provide useful evidence for studying how research directions develop in NLP. To support further research, we release our dataset at: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20385239.

Wrong with Confidence: Measuring Hallucination, Overconfidence and Identity-Conditioned Behaviour in Large Language Models
自信的错误：测量大语言模型中的幻觉、过度自信与身份条件行为
Large language models answer underspecified questions readily, and accuracy-only evaluation rewards guessing over abstaining. Observational studies link query underspecification to hallucination, but they cannot separate the effect of missing information from item difficulty, and they rarely ask what the model tells the user. We report a pre-registered, paired behavioural study of five open-weight models (Gemma 3 27B, Gemma 4 31B, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B and Nemotron 3 Super). Each of 142 factual questions was posed in a fully specified form and in a referentially underspecified form with the same answer key, and three probes measured identity-conditioned behaviour. Two raters scored 5,620 responses under a fixed rubric; effects were estimated with mixed-effects models. Without the referent, the models sought clarification on 33.7% of prompts and answered the rest. Among attempted answers, the error rate rose from 39.1% to 52.0% (mixed-effects odds ratio 4.12, 95% CI 2.76-6.14), and specialist-domain questions failed more often than general ones in every model. Unelicited verbal uncertainty did not track this risk: 75.3% of wrong answers carried no hedge, wrong answers to underspecified prompts were hedged no more often than wrong answers to clear prompts (27.3% vs 22.3%), and hedging separated correct from incorrect answers only weakly (AUROC 0.56). Gendered pronouns followed occupational stereotypes whenever a model committed to one; any stated user identity lengthened answers by about 45% relative to an anonymous user; claimed expertise did not reduce safety caveats. The models either ask or answer as if the question were well posed, and the wording of a guess does not reveal that it is one. Evaluations should score clarification as a distinct outcome and check label validity as well as rater agreement.

大语言模型能够轻易回答未充分指定的问题，而仅以准确率为评估标准会奖励猜测而非回避。观察性研究将查询不明确与幻觉联系起来，但无法区分信息缺失与题目难度的影响，且很少关注模型向用户传达的内容。我们报告了一项预先注册的配对行为研究，涉及五种开源模型（Gemma 3 27B、Gemma 4 31B、gpt-oss-120b、Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B 和 Nemotron 3 Super）。142个事实性问题分别以完全指定和指代不明确的形式提出，答案键相同，并通过三个探测器测量身份条件行为。两名评分员根据固定评分标准对5,620条响应进行评分；使用混合效应模型估计影响。在缺少指代对象的情况下，模型在33.7%的提示中寻求澄清，其余则直接作答。在尝试作答的部分中，错误率从39.1%上升至52.0%（混合效应优势比4.12，95%置信区间2.76–6.14），所有模型中专业领域问题失败频率均高于一般问题。未经诱导的言语不确定性并未反映这一风险：75.3%的错误回答没有使用缓和语，针对不明确提示的错误回答使用缓和语的频率并不高于清晰提示（27.3% vs 22.3%），且缓和语仅弱度区分正确与错误答案（AUROC 0.56）。当模型确定性别时，其使用的职业刻板印象性别代词；任何声明的用户身份使回答长度相比匿名用户增加约45%；声称的专业知识并未减少安全警告。这些模型要么像问题已明确一样提问，要么像已明确一样作答，而猜测的措辞并不能揭示其为猜测。评估应将澄清视为独立结果，并检查标签有效性及评分员一致性。

Criterion-Activated Preference Synthesis: Attribution-Preserving Preference Data from Explicit Standards
标准激活偏好合成：基于显式标准的可追溯偏好数据生成
Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is notoriously sensitive to attribution ambiguity: when chosen and rejected responses differ along multiple entangled dimensions, the model cannot identify which behavior the preference label teaches. We propose Criterion-Activated Preference Synthesis (CAPS), a criterion-first framework that turns explicit quality standards into attribution-verified preference pairs. CAPS synthesizes contexts and responses from a target criterion, then applies dual-signal scoring: a rubric-bound judge measures criterion compliance, while a blind general judge measures holistic quality. Two filters close the attribution loop: the Empirical Activation Test (EAT) keeps criterion-context pairs where satisfying the criterion improves blind quality, and the Attribution Ratio (AR) keeps pairs whose quality gap is dominated by the target criterion. Instantiated with general rubrics, medical rubrics, and Chinese legal statutes, CAPS shows strong data efficiency and domain transfer. With 20k general synthetic pairs, it outperforms 35k human-annotated HelpSteer3 pairs on IFEval, IFBench, AlpacaEval, and Creative Writing v3. In domain settings, CAPS improves HealthBench with 2k medical pairs and improves Qwen3-8B/14B by +4.9 to +6.6 points on legal benchmarks using only public statutes, without human preference labels. We additionally construct the CAPS-Legal preference dataset.

Skill Transfer: Adapting Agent Skills from Strong to Weak Agents
技能迁移：将强智能体的技能适配到弱智能体
Agent skills are modular bundles of instructions, code, and resources that an agent loads on demand, increasingly authored and validated on frontier models and shared as an open standard. The same skill behaves differently across models: a strong model turns it into a large performance gain, while a weak model realizes little of that gain and sometimes does worse than with no skill at all. Cost and resource constraints, however, often restrict real deployments to exactly these weaker agents. We hypothesize that the strong model silently supplies procedural steps the skill leaves implicit, which the weak model omits, and formalize closing this gap as \emph{Skill Transfer}: holding the skill's capability ceiling and the model's parameters fixed, we adapt the skill so a specific weak agent can execute it well. Our method abstracts strong and weak trajectories into typed execution structures, localizes their structural divergence with a graph edit distance (GED), and repairs the skill through an iterative diagnoser-patcher loop. Across three benchmarks and two model families, Skill Transfer raises pass rate over the unmodified skill significantly and well over other skill-evolution baselines. The adapted skill also improves the strong agent it was never adapted for, and transfers out of distribution to a structurally related, unseen task. Code is available at https://github.com/Yifan-Lan/Skill-Transfer
中文翻译
智能体技能是按需加载的指令、代码和资源模块化组合，越来越多地由前沿模型创建并验证，以开放标准共享。同一技能在不同模型上的表现差异显著：强模型能将其转化为显著性能提升，而弱模型则难以发挥其潜力，甚至有时表现不如不使用技能。然而，成本和资源限制常常使实际部署局限于这些较弱的智能体。我们假设强模型隐式提供了技能中未明确说明的程序步骤，而弱模型会忽略这些步骤，并将弥合这一差距形式化为‘技能迁移’：在保持技能能力上限和模型参数不变的前提下，调整技能使其能在特定弱智能体上高效执行。我们的方法将强弱智能体的轨迹抽象为类型化的执行结构，使用图编辑距离（GED）定位其结构差异，并通过迭代诊断-修复循环来修复技能。在三个基准测试和两个模型家族上，技能迁移显著提升了原始技能的通过率，且优于其他技能演化基线。经过适配的技能还改善了从未为其适配的强智能体的表现，并能泛化到结构相关但未见过的任务。代码已公开于 https://github.com/Yifan-Lan/Skill-Transfer。

Automated fact-checking benchmarks typically pair claims with clean, curated evidence in high-resource languages, but real-world evidence is often incomplete, misleading, or written in a language where models are weaker. We evaluate the robustness of fact-checking LLMs for different languages. Building on EuroVerdict, we construct gold evidence sets for 190 claims in each of English, German, Greek, and Romanian, then apply four corruption strategies at two severity levels. We test LLMs on a set of claims, providing them with evidence from the sets above. A rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge scores reasoning quality. Verdict accuracy proves highly sensitive to both factors: Misleading edit cut Llama 3.1 8B's English accuracy from 80.00% to 16.84%, and losses widen as language resource level decreases. Machine-translating Greek and Romanian claims into English recovers much, but not all, of the low-resource gap. Judge scores decline more slowly than accuracy, suggesting that automated reasoning evaluation underestimates degradation. These results caution against deploying LLM fact-checkers on noisy multilingual evidence, and we release our evidence datasets and evaluation code to support future work.

Tool-calling evaluations often report whether the final call matches a reference answer, but this single outcome merges different failures: choosing a function outside the available registry, violating the selected schema, or filling arguments with values not supported by the user request. These failures matter more when models must choose from larger tool registries. We introduce RFCD, a registry-scaled function-calling benchmark built from BFCL, Glaive Function Calling v2, and Tool-Call-Data, with standardized JSON-schema registries ranging from 5 to 3,000 functions. We also introduce TAAG, a deterministic stage-decomposed evaluator for registry conformance, structural completeness, and argument grounding. Across six locally served sub-4B models, three data sources, and four feedback modes, registry scale is the dominant source of degradation: single-pass TAAG pass rate drops sharply from small to large registries on all sources. Repeated feedback improves some grounding metrics but adds substantial token cost and does not consistently improve end-to-end F1. Requirement-level TAAG-R feedback gives modest gains over stage-only TAAG-S feedback, which indicates that TAAG signals are useful for analysis and correction probes but do not solve registry scaling by themselves. RFCD and TAAG provide an evaluation resource for measuring where tool-calling systems fail as registries grow.

CondRelBench: A Mixed-Domain Benchmark for Condition-Scoped Relation Understanding
CondRelBench：一种用于条件限定关系理解的跨领域基准测试
Relation extraction systems often identify what a relation is, but not the condition under which it holds. This can collapse condition-bound claims into unsupported generalizations, a failure we call relation overgeneralization. We introduce CondRelBench, a mixed-domain benchmark for evaluating condition-scoped relation understanding. Each claim is represented as (E1, R, E2 | C), where C is the condition licensing the relation. Using 3,000 synthetic paragraphs, 200 PubMed full-text papers, and 695 Reddit posts, we construct five probe variants per tuple that preserve, replace, remove, or contradict the condition, or contradict the relation itself. Models classify each probe as Supported, Not Supported, or Not Enough Evidence. We also introduce Overgeneralization Rate (OGR) and Scope Preservation Score (SPS) to measure false support for altered claims and consistency across probe families. Across prompted LLMs, fine-tuned LLMs, and encoder models, we find that Accuracy and Macro F1 often hide scope failures. Models frequently support the original scoped claim but fail when its condition is removed or altered. Domain-specific encoders achieve the strongest scope preservation, while instruction-tuned LLMs often show higher overgeneralization. Synthetic supervision helps but does not close the gap to real-world PubMed and Reddit performance.

关系抽取系统通常能识别关系本身，但无法判断该关系成立的条件。这可能导致将受条件限制的陈述简化为无支持的泛化，我们称之为关系过度泛化。本文提出CondRelBench，一个用于评估条件限定关系理解的跨领域基准测试。每个陈述表示为（E1, R, E2 | C），其中C是使该关系成立的条件。我们使用3000个合成段落、200篇PubMed全文论文和695条Reddit帖子，构建每组三元组的五个探测变体，以保留、替换、移除或矛盾条件，或矛盾关系本身。模型需对每个探测判断为‘支持’、‘不支持’或‘证据不足’。我们还引入了过度泛化率（OGR）和范围保持得分（SPS），用于衡量对修改后陈述的错误支持程度以及不同探测族之间的一致性。在提示型大模型、微调大模型和编码器模型中，我们发现准确率和宏F1常掩盖范围失败问题。模型常支持原始带条件的陈述，但在条件被移除或改变时表现不佳。领域特定编码器表现出最强的范围保持能力，而指令微调的大模型则往往表现出更高的过度泛化。合成监督有所帮助，但无法弥合与真实世界PubMed和Reddit性能之间的差距。

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate model-generated medical content, creating a potential circularity: an LLM judge may favor outputs generated by the same model independently of clinical quality. To characterize LLM judge self-preference in medical settings, we measured same-model affinity in single-turn specialist question answering and multi-turn standardized-patient encounters. We evaluated eight models, two from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Qwen, on 620 real point of care questions from clinicians (Real-POCQi). The same eight models also generated and judged 200 standardized patient-clinician scenarios (MedSP1000) up to 8 visible turns. In total, our analysis spans 13,760 LLM judgments. We define three complementary measures of self-preference. Answer Rank Bias, our primary measure, compared the rank assigned to a fixed response by its own-model judge with its average rank from outside judges. Answer Score Bias made the analogous comparison using rubric scores. Own-Answer Win Rate measured how often a judge ranked its own model's response above a competitor. Higher values across all these measures indicate greater degrees of self-preference. In Real-POCQi, pooled Answer Rank Bias was $+1.22$ positions, and all eight judges favored their own answers. Self-preference persisted both with and without a grading rubric. Revealing generator identities modestly weakened self-preference by an average of $-0.094$ positions. In MedSP1000, pooled Answer Rank Bias ranged from $+0.53$ to $+0.62$ positions, with no clear difference by conversation length ($p=0.17$). LLM judges systematically favored responses generated by their own models across multiple formats. Clinical AI deployments should exercise increased vigilance including multiple evaluation measures and judge panels spanning differing model families when deploying LLM-as-a-judge systems.
中文翻译
大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于评估模型生成的医疗内容，这可能引发循环性问题：LLM裁判可能会偏好由同一模型生成的输出，而不论其临床质量如何。为刻画医疗场景下LLM裁判的自我偏好，我们测量了在单轮专科问答和多轮标准化患者对话中的同模型亲和性。我们评估了八种模型（来自OpenAI、Anthropic、Google和Qwen），在620个来自临床医生的真实临床决策问题（Real-POCQi）上进行测试。同时，这些模型还生成并评估了200个标准化患者-医生情景（MedSP1000），最多8轮可见对话。总计分析了13,760次LLM判断。我们定义了三种互补的自我偏好度量：答案排名偏差（主度量），比较固定回答由自身模型裁判给出的排名与其由外部裁判给出的平均排名；答案评分偏差，使用评分量表进行类似比较；自身回答胜率，衡量裁判将自身模型的回答排在对手之上的频率。数值越高，表示自我偏好越强。在Real-POCQi中，合并答案排名偏差为+1.22位，所有八个裁判均偏好自身回答。无论是否提供评分量表，自我偏好均持续存在。揭示生成者身份仅略微减弱自我偏好（平均-0.094位）。在MedSP1000中，合并答案排名偏差介于+0.53至+0.62位之间，且对话长度差异不显著（p=0.17）。LLM裁判在多种格式下系统性地偏好自身模型生成的回答。临床AI部署应提高警惕，包括采用多种评估指标和涵盖不同模型家族的裁判小组，以应对LLM作为裁判系统的风险。

Bridging Semantics and Utilities: A Controllable and Scalable Market Simulation
连接语义与效用：一种可控且可扩展的市场模拟方法
Large language models(LLMs) have recently been used to construct generative agents for financial market simulation. Existing approaches typically prompt each agent separately with public market information and a private investor profile, and ask the model to directly generate trading actions. In this agent-wise design, the model repeatedly interprets information shared across the population, while individual behavior is controlled through textual descriptions of investor preferences and traits. This creates two structural difficulties: continuous traits such as risk sensitivity do not reliably induce ordered behavioral changes, and repeatedly processing the same public information causes inference costs to grow with the number of agents. We propose \textbf{SUM}, a Semantic-Utility Model that separates cohort-level semantic perception from agent-level utility-based decision-making. A language model interprets public market information for each investor type and produces semantic signals shared within the corresponding cohort. Individual agents then combine these signals with their private states, preferences, and constraints to generate orders through utility-based decisions. Experiments in an A-share limit-order-book market show that \textbf{SUM} provides more stable and monotonic behavioral control than prompt-based agents while substantially reducing repeated language-model inference as the population grows. Closed-loop simulations further reproduce directional market responses, volatility persistence, differentiated investment styles, and persistent wealth heterogeneity. These results establish \textbf{SUM} as a controllable, scalable, and semantically informed framework for financial market simulation.
中文翻译
大型语言模型（LLMs）最近被用于构建金融市场的生成式智能体。现有方法通常分别对每个智能体进行提示，输入公开市场信息和私有投资者画像，并要求模型直接生成交易行为。在这种以智能体为中心的设计中，模型反复解释群体共享的信息，而个体行为则通过描述投资者偏好和特质的文本进行控制。这带来了两个结构性难题：连续特征如风险敏感性无法可靠地引发有序的行为变化，且重复处理相同公共信息导致推理成本随智能体数量增长。我们提出 extbf{SUM}，一种将群体级语义感知与智能体级效用驱动决策分离的语义-效用模型。语言模型为每种投资者类型解析公共市场信息，生成在相应群体内共享的语义信号。个体智能体随后结合这些信号与其私有状态、偏好和约束，通过基于效用的决策生成订单。在A股限价订单簿市场的实验表明， extbf{SUM}在行为控制上比基于提示的智能体更稳定、更单调，同时显著降低了随着群体规模扩大而产生的重复语言模型推理开销。闭环模拟进一步重现了市场方向性响应、波动持续性、差异化投资风格以及持久的财富不平等。这些结果确立了 extbf{SUM}作为可控、可扩展且语义感知的金融市场模拟框架。
