When Helpful Agents Cause Financial Harm: Evaluating LLM Agent Safety in Executable Economic Worlds
有益的智能体为何造成财务损害：在可执行经济世界中评估LLM智能体的安全性
As LLM agents become increasingly capable of making consequential economic decisions, their safety under economic pressures remains poorly understood. We introduce EconSafeBench, the first benchmark for systematically evaluating the safety of LLM agents in executable economic environments. EconSafeBench contains 828 cases across five economic scenarios and four categories of safety violations. A key design is the matched evaluation of three sources of safety pressure, including explicit user requests, pressure from other actors, and pressure arising from the agent's own pursuit of a performance objective. We further evaluate safety at both static and dynamic scales through 30-period interactions with persistent memory and matched controls. Across eight LLMs, all evaluated models exhibit safety violations on the static benchmark, with overall violation rates ranging from 8.5% to 40.6%. We further find that violations can occur even without an explicit unsafe request, and that initially compliant agents may begin to violate as performance pressure increases over time. These findings highlight the need for stronger safety alignment and rigorous evaluation before LLM agents are deployed in high-stakes economic environments.

Many Paths to the Same Mistake: Generating Diverse Reasoning Paths Behind the Same Student Mistake

Realistic evaluation of AI systems requires user simulators that capture not only cooperative behavior, but also the errors and variability that arise in real interactions. In educational technology, simulating step-by-step flawed student reasoning is essential, yet datasets mapping these pathways are scarce, and Large Language Models (LLMs) often auto-correct rather than sustain simulated mistakes. To address this, we present a generate-and-filter pipeline that produces diverse and realistic student error traces. Our approach utilizes forward consistency, a metric verifying if a flawed reasoning trace can be used to recover the student's actual incorrect answer, paired with an LLM-as-a-judge to ensure realism. Our evaluation suggests that while many LLMs struggle to maintain incorrect reasoning mid-trace, smaller supervised fine-tuned models successfully capture these divergent paths. This work provides a framework for high-fidelity error trace generation, advancing realistic, non-cooperative user simulation.

Syntactic Complexity Convergence in Dialogue: Analysis of the Phenomenon and Application to LLM Detection

We revisit the under-explored phenomenon of syntactic complexity convergence in dialogue. Extending prior topic-level analyses to full conversations, we examine five human-human datasets and a set of human-LLM dialogues. We integrate and evaluate a multidimensional set of syntactic complexity metrics to quantify structural variation in dialogue. Our analyses reveal robust syntactic complexity convergence across human-human datasets, especially in task-oriented interactions, and statistical tests confirm that these effects are not due to chance. In contrast, human-LLM dialogues show no significant convergence under individual metrics; however, linear-CKA uncovers a distinct cross-metric convergence pattern. Motivated by these differences, we use syntactic complexity as a feature for detecting LLM-involved dialogue, achieving 96\% accuracy. Our classification results demonstrate its potential without relying on likelihood-based signals such as surprisal, which require a language model as the estimator.

One Question, Four Voices: How Advice for Alzheimer's Caregiving Differs Between Caregivers, Clinicians, and Large Language Models
一个问题，四种声音：阿尔茨海默病照护者、临床医生与大语言模型在建议上的差异
Online caregiver forums are an important source of emotional and informational support for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD). We compare responses to 85 real caregiver questions from ALZConnected across four responder groups: peer caregivers, physicians, ChatGPT, and a retrieval-augmented CareGPT grounded in peer discussions. Using 28 measures spanning linguistic form, emotional support, informational support, and topic scope, we examine how these voices differ when answering the same questions. Peers provided time-anchored narratives and community grounding; clinicians offered concise, advice-forward, clinically bounded guidance; and LLMs produced a formal, verbose, highly structured consultation style. CareGPT showed minimal measurable separation from ChatGPT, suggesting that retrieval plus prompt injection alone was insufficient to shift communicative stance. LLM outputs scored higher than peers on politeness and emotion-support markers and were comparable to clinicians on informativeness and physician-alignment measures, but were less narrative and less contextually situated. Topic modeling showed that LLM responses concentrated on advice-oriented themes, whereas peers covered a broader range, including emotional processing, legal and financial concerns, and daily care. These findings suggest that AI can complement, but not replace, human contributions to ADRD caregiver support and motivate hybrid systems that combine structured AI delivery with the distinct strengths of human voices.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Clinical Decision Support in Gait Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept
用于步态分析临床决策支持的检索增强生成：概念验证
Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential for clinical decision support but lack specialized biomechanical knowledge required for accurate gait analysis interpretation. We developed and evaluated a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to enhance LLM-generated clinical explanations for ankle fracture rehabilitation using ground reaction force data. Using the GaitRec dataset (503 subjects: 211 healthy, 292 ankle fracture patients), we implemented a five-stage pipeline integrating: (1) machine learning classification (91.3\% accuracy); (2) Layer-wise Relevance Propagation for explainable feature identification; (3) RAG knowledge base from peer-reviewed biomechanics literature; (4) GPT-5 explanation generation with and without retrieval augmentation; and (5) double-blind evaluation by experienced physical therapists across five clinical criteria. RAG augmentation produced statistically significant improvements in Clini-cal Benefit (mean difference=0.60, p=0.047, δ=0.49) and Completeness (mean difference=0.70, p=0.049, δ=0.49), both demonstrating large effect sizes. Baseline GPT-5 achieved strong performance across all criteria (\textgreater4.0/5.0). This proof-of-concept demonstrates that augmenting general-purpose LLMs with domain-specific knowledge meaningfully enhances actionable, evidence-based clinical guidance---dimensions most critical for rehabilitation decision-making. The framework provides a scalable approach for integrating AI into specialized clinical workflows without costly model retraining.

Jailbreak LLMs with Linguistic Style as a Hidden Attack Surface
以语言风格作为隐藏攻击面破解大语言模型
We show that linguistic style is a systematic and previously overlooked attack surface for LLM safety. Across a diverse taxonomy of styles and multiple state-of-the-art models, stylistic rewrites of identical harmful goals produce order-of-magnitude differences in Attack Success Rate (ASR), with some styles achieving up to 80\% ASR while others remain below 6\%. To exploit this vulnerability, we introduce a lightweight single-pass attack framework that combines a style-conditioned generator with a BERT-based style selector, achieving performance competitive with substantially more expensive multi-turn optimization methods. To understand why style affects safety behavior, we conduct mechanistic analysis on LLaMA-3.1-8B and find that stylistic rewrites disrupt refusal representations while preserving recoverable harmful intent, suggesting a distributed failure mode rather than a single refusal mechanism. Motivated by this finding, we develop a style-aware Direct Preference Optimization defense that reduces ASR from 86\% to 19.5\% while largely preserving utility. Together, our results establish linguistic style as a critical factor in adversarial robustness and provide both mechanistic insight and a practical defense.

ScopeBench: Evaluating Cultural Norm Scope Awareness in LLMs
ScopeBench：评估大语言模型的文化规范范围意识
Safety evaluation in large language models treats harm as culturally invariant, yet a model cannot correctly apply a safety norm without knowing whose norms bind. We introduce ScopeBench, a benchmark that treats cultural scope as a first-class safety dimension. It comprises 3,323 norms spanning 49 countries across nine cultural clusters, each annotated as Universal or Specific. We define three scope error types identically across four evaluation tasks: Scope Inflation, Scope Deflation, and Scope Displacement. Evaluating 21 frontier LLMs across seven model families, we surface three structural failures. First, the dominant error type inverts with prompt format: Scope Deflation reaches 70% in single-answer classification, while Scope Inflation reaches 33% when each candidate culture is judged independently. Second, scope-classification accuracy is empirically decoupled from behavioral safety: the six classifiers achieving at least 97% Task 1 accuracy still produce harmful responses to 40-42% of scope-violating statements. Third, no model is safe in interaction, with harmful-response rates ranging from 29% to 51% across the cohort, excluding one model that systematically refuses the task. We release all data, code, and model outputs to establish cultural scope as a distinct alignment axis.
中文翻译
大语言模型的安全评估通常将危害视为文化无差别的，但模型若不了解何种规范具有约束力，则无法正确应用安全规范。我们引入ScopeBench，一个将文化范围视为首要安全维度的基准测试。该基准涵盖来自49个国家的9个文化集群的3,323条规范，每条均标注为普遍性或特定性。我们在四个评估任务中定义了三种范围错误类型：范围扩大、范围缩小和范围错位。对21个前沿大模型（跨越七个模型家族）的评估揭示了三项结构性缺陷：首先，主导错误类型随提示格式变化：单答案分类中范围缩小达70%，而独立评估每个候选文化时范围扩大达33%；其次，范围分类准确率与行为安全性在实证上解耦：六个分类器在任务1中准确率达97%以上，但仍对40%-42%的范围违规陈述产生有害回应；第三，无一模型在交互中真正安全，有害回应率在29%至51%之间，仅一个模型因系统性拒绝任务而例外。我们公开所有数据、代码和模型输出，确立文化范围为一个独立的对齐轴。

Between the Lines: Multi-turn Contextual Investment Advice Detection
字里行间：多轮上下文投资建议检测
As large language models (LLMs) increasingly power financial conversational assistants, detecting investment advice in natural language has become a critical regulatory and safety challenge. Unlike explicit single-turn recommendations, investment advice often emerges implicitly and progressively over multi-turn conversations, shaped by user intent, delivery style, and contextual buildup. We introduce the first comprehensive framework for detecting both sequential and contextual investment advice in dialogue settings. Central to our approach is a modular, top-down synthetic data generation pipeline that systematically spans a taxonomy of advisory trajectories using an axis-bucket-descriptor schema. We simulate both benign and high-risk conversations across diverse user personas, financial instruments, and risk tiers, and evaluate detection capabilities using LLM-as-a-Judge with entropy-based uncertainty diagnostics. Our results show that contextual advisory detection remains substantially more challenging than sequential cases, even under few-shot prompting with tailored demonstrations. This work lays the foundation for scalable guardrail development in high-stakes, compliance-sensitive domains, where advisory risk is often subtle, distributed, and perception-dependent.

Deployed large language models must remain useful when untrusted text enters their prompt context. Adversarial prompting and red-teaming methods typically define the failures they seek through task labels, harmful targets, judge feedback, or downstream utility scores. We ask whether a frozen model's clean behavior can reveal a reusable context vulnerability when its task-level form is unknown, and downstream task feedback is withheld. To study this question, EndoUT uses a Siamese-style design that compares the same frozen victim on clean and span-modified versions of each unlabeled instruction. Without a task-level target, the clean pass supplies the victim's preferred response-onset token as an instruction-conditioned reference; Endogenous Preference Disruption (EPD) measures how insertion weakens that preference. An auxiliary generator supplies bounded-span proposals; EPD guides its update and ranks the pool without access to downstream information. The highest-scoring victim-specific span is fixed before evaluation and reused unchanged across all held-out inputs. Across four instruction-tuned models and nine benchmarks, fixed triggers reduce benign-task utility by 40.2 percentage points on average, with negative mean change on every benchmark and greater average degradation than every evaluated baseline under the reported protocols. Matched protocol ablations show stronger transfer for source-side selection followed by fixed reuse than for null-context fixed reuse or per-input generation. Transfer recurs across proposers with proposal-dependent strength; output-level analyses identify victim-specific associations between trigger families and downstream failure patterns. Thus, clean behavior can expose context vulnerabilities that transfer across inputs yet manifest through structured, victim-specific patterns of utility degradation. The code and data will be released upon acceptance.

Automating literature screening and knowledge synthesis with large language models
利用大语言模型自动化文献筛选与知识综合
Scientific literature is expanding rapidly, yet much of its knowledge remains difficult to organize and reuse due to the substantial workload needed to navigate large, heterogeneous literature corpora. Here, we develop a generalizable large language model (LLM)-powered framework that automates literature screening, structured information extraction, and knowledge synthesis within a unified workflow. We benchmarked 11 state-of-the-art proprietary and open-weight LLMs across three materials science screening tasks differing in scope, corpus size, and class imbalance. Seven LLMs achieved balanced accuracies above 0.90 across all tasks, with the best-performing LLM reaching 0.96--0.98, demonstrating the potential of LLMs to accurately screen large, highly imbalanced scientific corpora. The framework also substantially reduces manual effort, screening 10,000 records within four minutes compared with approximately 83 person-hours for manual screening. Beyond literature screening, the framework extracts structured information from full-text articles, enabling content-level quantification of research landscapes that extends traditional bibliometric analysis based on publication metadata. This capability reveals methodological trends and underexplored directions, as shown for machine learning in concrete materials science. We further demonstrate its utility for information and data discovery by identifying publications containing silicate glass density data that are difficult to retrieve using conventional search strategies, which can support downstream hypothesis development, research design, and data-driven scientific discovery. Overall, these results demonstrate the broad applicability of LLM-powered literature analysis across scientific domains and its potential to transform large, unstructured literature corpora into structured, analyzable knowledge at scale.

Human vs Machine Translation Detection: A Cross-Model, Cross-Domain, and Low-Resource Analysis

The growing reliance on web-crawled corpora for training large language models introduces a critical challenge: machine-translated (MT) content is often treated as human translation (HT), potentially degrading data quality and propagating synthetic artifacts, especially in low-resource settings. In this work, we study MT-HT detectability across high-resource (English, Spanish) and low-resource (Swahili, Afrikaans) languages using both decoder-only LLMs in zero-shot and few-shot settings, and fine-tuned multilingual encoders trained at the sentence level and on token-chunked inputs. We find that decoder-only models provide limited discrimination overall and exhibit a consistent class-asymmetric failure mode: they recognize human-written text reliably (high HT recall) but rarely flag fluent machine output (low MT recall). Encoder-based classifiers achieve high accuracy when evaluated on data generated by the same MT systems and translators used during training in a legislative domain, but their MT recall drops sharply on unseen translators and on unseen domains such as low-resource conversational text and medical content. To address this limitation, we evaluate models on longer inputs by chunking text into segments of up to 300 tokens, which substantially improves generalization, suggesting that sentence-level signals are insufficient for robust detection. Finally, we analyze the relationship between translation quality and detectability using COMET and BLEURT, showing that lower-quality MT is more easily identified, while high-quality MT remains difficult to distinguish from HT. Our results highlight the importance of input granularity, translator generalization, and translation quality in building robust MT detection systems across domains and languages.

Across qwen-32B, mistral-small-3.2-24B, and gpt- oss-20B, Trident achieves the best average performance and consistently outperforms non-learning, memory-based, reflection-based, and automated prompt optimization base- lines. Compared with the strongest baseline, APEX, Trident yields relative average gains of 30.7%, 30.8%, and 38.3% on the three backbones, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity stud- ies further show that the three designs provide complementary gains and remain robust to parameter variations.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for tutoring and professional knowledge retrieval, yet safety evaluations still focus mainly on overt harms such as toxicity while overlooking benevolent failure modes. We study epistemic infantilization, defined as an identity-conditioned reduction in technical depth that appears when disability disclosure precedes an expert-level query. To measure this effect, we construct a counterfactual dataset of matched question-answer pairs and compare model responses across three settings: no identity context, disability disclosed in prior conversational context, and disability disclosed via a short query prefix. We introduce two composite metrics, the Infantilization Bias Index (IBI) and the Epistemic Accessibility Response Score (EARS), which capture retention of mathematical and formal content, domain terminology, reasoning coverage, and tone signals such as simplification markers and unsolicited offers to adjust the level. Across five open-weight model families, we find consistent evidence that disability disclosure reduces epistemic access by replacing formal explanations with higher-level summaries, with Physics and Mathematics most affected. Using question-clustered inference that respects the repeated-measures structure of the data, the effect remains reliable after accounting for correlated observations. These findings suggest an inclusion tax, where disabled users must request rigor more explicitly than non-disabled users. We conclude by arguing that accessibility should mean format adaptation rather than content simplification.

Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination. We measure this memory on FOMC statements and minutes from 2000 to 2026 by comparing modern open models with chronologically consistent models, which are trained only on text from before a fixed date. Asked about past GDP outcomes given only a date, models that cannot know the answer still reach an AUC of up to 0.64 from priors on dates and eras, so chance is the wrong baseline. Against these memory-free models on the same questions, most modern models recall which years had strong growth. Membership-inference scores sort documents by era and document type rather than by whether a model saw them, as exact counts in an open pretraining corpus show. In real-time nowcasts, every lookahead premium we estimate on US GDP is smaller than the forecast comparison can detect at macroeconomic sample sizes, and none on GDP or inflation survives correction for multiple testing. Lookahead audits should therefore measure memory directly against memory-free models on the same items.

Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply. Across 20 LLMs, checks of whether the cited reasons are correct, computed or asked of an LLM judge, are close to chance at spotting this failure, as the argument predicts. A strong judge asked whether acting on the explanation would work does spot it. Stronger and reasoning models do better but still fail on many denials with four or more independent reasons. Asking for every rule helps every open model with room to improve. Explanations of eligibility decisions should be built from the decision function and judged by whether acting on them works.

乐观验证者易遭攻击：基于精确过程预言机的奖励劫持现象
Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards inherits whatever its verifier gets wrong. Outside mathematics and code the verifier is a proxy, a rubric, a learned judge or a hand-written checker, and its distance from the true objective is never measured, so a rising reward cannot be told apart from a hack. We build a setting where the true reward is exactly computable at the process level: executable authorization policies over 124,416 contexts admit an oracle that lists every minimal sufficient reason for every decision. We compile these policies into exact process rewards, degrade the verifier along seven realistic axes (outcome-only, sufficiency, recall-only, extraction noise, coarse taxonomy, stale policy, LLM judge), and train against each while the exact verifier scores every rollout. Four phenotypes appear. Optimistic verifiers are hacked by padding: the sufficiency proxy ends at 0.940 while true faithfulness falls from 0.731 to 0.667 on 96 held-out episodes. Outcome-only verifiers saturate and stop teaching, noise dilutes, and ranking-preserving gaps do no harm. A model-free audit of the verifier, its selection error and gap sign, together with a short saturation pilot, anticipates which phenotype a run will produce. Across nine configurations spanning two frameworks, two model vendors, two adapter sizes, three precisions, two initialisations and two seeds, the phenotypes recur, sufficiency damage is positive in all 10 replication cells and beyond two standard errors in 7, and optimistic gaps remain the steeper branch. The damage magnitude does not replicate, and five pre-registered attempts to explain it are reported as they fell. We release the testbed, the training instrumentation, and 14 real public policies (Cedar, OPA, Gatekeeper) ported to executable oracles.
中文翻译
从可验证奖励中进行强化学习会继承验证者的所有错误。在数学和代码之外，验证者通常是一个代理——如评分标准、学习型裁判或手工检查器，其与真实目标的距离无法衡量，因此上升的奖励无法与奖励劫持区分开来。我们构建了一个真实奖励可在过程层面精确计算的场景：在124,416个上下文上执行授权策略，存在一个预言机可列出每个决策的最小充分理由。我们将这些策略编译为精确的过程奖励，沿着七个现实维度降级验证者（仅结果、充分性、仅召回、提取噪声、粗粒度分类、过期策略、LLM裁判），并在每种情况下使用精确验证者评估每次轨迹。出现四种表型。乐观验证者易受填充攻击：充分性代理得分降至0.940，而真实忠实度从0.731降至0.667（在96个保留测试样本上）。仅结果验证者趋于饱和并停止教学，噪声导致性能稀释，保持排序差距无害。对验证者的无模型审计及其选择误差和差距符号，结合简短的饱和预实验，可预测运行产生的表型。在九种配置下（涵盖两个框架、两个模型供应商、两个适配器大小、三个精度、两个初始化和两个种子），表型重复出现，充分性损害在全部10个复现单元中均为正向，且在7个单元中超过两个标准误，而乐观差距始终是更陡峭的分支。损害幅度未复现，五次预先注册的解释尝试均未能成功。我们发布了测试平台、训练工具链以及14个真实公共策略（Cedar、OPA、Gatekeeper）移植到可执行预言机的版本。

Detection-Efficient Watermarking for Vision--Language Agents via Risk-Constrained Strength Allocation
基于风险约束强度分配的检测高效水印技术用于视觉-语言智能体
Vision--language agents generate descriptions, decisions, and instructions that may be reused by users, downstream agents, and automated workflows, creating a need for provenance mechanisms that support content authenticity and post-deployment auditing without unnecessarily degrading response quality. We present a risk-aware semantic watermarking framework that combines predictive uncertainty with a zero-shot multimodal relevance-risk proxy to allocate watermark strength during decoding. A single risk penalty $λ$ exposes a continuous operating frontier, allowing deployment-time selection of a detection--quality trade-off without model retraining. At a selected operating point, mean watermark strength is reduced by approximately 59.4\% relative to fixed-strength watermarking, while perplexity change falls from 0.3634 to 0.1689 and clean/paraphrased ROC-AUC reaches 0.9552/0.9459. A matched-strength analysis shows that this advantage reflects the allocation policy rather than lower average intervention: at comparable mean strength, risk-constrained allocation achieves substantially higher ROC-AUC than fixed, entropy-only, and criticality-only policies, identifying it as detection-efficient rather than quality-dominant. We further show that threshold calibration on finite samples produces substantial false-positive-rate drift, motivating calibration variance reporting as standard practice for auditable provenance.

AuXSpec: Learning to Autoformalize Program Specifications via Executable Postconditions
AuXSpec：通过可执行后置条件学习自动形式化程序规范
Formal specifications define intended program behavior and underpin verification, but writing them in theorem provers such as Lean is slow and expertise-intensive, making specification a major bottleneck to scaling formally correct code. Autoformalization from natural-language problems is promising, yet training specification models requires scalable feedback on whether generated specifications capture intended behavior. Prior approaches obtain this feedback through explicit proofs or separately implemented code with formal correspondence proofs, both expensive. We introduce AuXSpec, a Lean framework that pairs declarative postconditions with executable counterparts, obtained through type class resolution when possible and otherwise defined separately with an equivalence proof. Test cases can then evaluate declarative specifications by execution, letting us use agreement as a reinforcement-learning reward. Using AuXSpec, we synthesize 3,037 LeetCode problems and expand training to 19.5K samples through expert iteration on Codeforces. Experiments show that training Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B with the execution-based reward improves SpecGen pass@4 on AuXSpec-Test 0.7% $\to$ 82.7% and 14.3% $\to$ 84.3%, and the 27B model outperforms all frontier models. On the out-of-domain Verina benchmark with its original prompts, both models improve 7.0% $\to$ 90.5% and 21.9% $\to$ 90.5% and surpass VeriSpecGen-30B-A3B, the prior state of the art among open-source specification models, on pass@1 (theirs 47.6% vs. ours 73.7% and 84.5%) and pass@4 (theirs 63.9% at pass@10 vs. ours 90.5%). We release the weights of the trained 9B and 27B models and the 3,037 problems with test cases, including the 300-problem AuXSpec-Test benchmark with expert review and correctness proofs for future evaluation. Models and data: https://huggingface.co/collections/eth-algopt/auxspec. Website: https://auxspec.org

A Crowd-Audited Atlas of Implicit Bias in LLM-Powered Agents
由众包审计的大语言模型驱动智能体中的隐性偏见图谱
Prior work has shown that large language models (LLMs) express implicit biases in high-publicity, one-off decision scenarios such as hiring and intelligence assessment. However, as people increasingly employ autonomous, LLM-powered AI agents that make decisions on their behalf in doing day-to-day tasks, it is of critical importance that we understand how implicit biases, based on sociodemographic assumptions, emerge across a broad milieu of workaday decision scenarios. We used the 17 domains of daily activity in the American Time Use Survey (ATUS) to generate an atlas of 506 decision scenarios in which LLMs --- endowed with personas representing different races, gender identities, and political ideologies --- expressed significant implicit bias. Next, in a crowdsourced audit, 500 participants made 8,010 binary choices about which implicitly biased decision scenarios most deserved further review. We found that participants prioritized decision scenarios that had broad relevance (e.g., about food choices), were high stakes (e.g., about health), and where all members of a simulated sociodemographic group made unanimous decisions (because it was a clear indication of stereotyping). They were less swayed by the magnitude of an observed disparity or the specific ATUS domain the decision scenario represented. When examining the rationale behind their prioritization choices, we found that participants often interpreted disparities as traits of demographic groups and judged whether those traits seemed plausible, often based on their own internalized stereotypes. We discuss implications for building personalized AI agents, digital twins, social simulations, and for using crowdsourced bias audits.
中文翻译
先前研究已表明，大型语言模型（LLMs）在高曝光、一次性决策场景（如招聘和智力评估）中表现出隐性偏见。然而，随着人们越来越多地使用自主的、由 LLM 驱动的 AI 智能体代为处理日常任务，理解基于社会人口学假设的隐性偏见如何在广泛的生活日常决策场景中涌现变得至关重要。我们利用美国时间使用调查（ATUS）中的 17 个日常活动领域，生成了涵盖 506 个决策场景的图谱，其中赋予不同种族、性别身份和政治意识形态角色的 LLM 表现出显著的隐性偏见。随后，在众包审计中，500 名参与者对 8,010 个二元选择作出判断，决定哪些隐性偏见场景最值得进一步审查。我们发现，参与者更优先关注具有广泛相关性（如饮食选择）、高风险（如健康）且模拟社会人口群体成员决策一致的场景（因其是刻板印象的明显信号）。他们较少受观察到差异幅度或具体 ATUS 领域的影响。分析其优先级理由时发现，参与者常将差异解释为群体特质，并基于自身内化的刻板印象判断这些特质是否合理。我们讨论了其对构建个性化 AI 智能体、数字孪生、社会模拟以及使用众包偏见审计的意义。

AnachroBench: Evaluating Historical Consistency in Large Vision-Language Models
AnachroBench：评估大型视觉-语言模型中的历史一致性
Existing Large Vision-Language Model benchmarks primarily evaluate visual understanding in general everyday scenarios, leaving historical consistency with a specified era and country largely underexplored. To address this gap, we propose AnachroBench, a controlled discriminative benchmark for evaluating historical consistency in visual scenes. It contains 1,600 image pairs from eight countries spanning the late 19th to the early 20th century, each pairing an original historical image with an anachronistic version containing a seamlessly inserted modern object. AnachroBench evaluates three aspects: Inserted Object Perception, which tests whether models detect the inserted modern object; Era-Country Consistency, which assesses whether the scene is consistent with the specified era and country; and Conditional Era-Country Consistency, which measures consistency judgments only when the inserted object is correctly perceived. A false consistency judgment occurs when a model perceives the modern object but still judges the scene as historically consistent. Overall, AnachroBench reveals a gap between inserted object perception and era-country consistency judgments, providing a targeted evaluation of this behavior.
中文翻译
现有的大型视觉-语言模型基准主要评估一般日常场景下的视觉理解，而对特定时代和国家的历史一致性则研究不足。为填补这一空白，我们提出了AnachroBench，一个用于评估视觉场景中历史一致性的受控判别性基准。该基准包含来自八个不同国家、跨越19世纪末至20世纪初的1600对图像，每对图像由一张原始历史图像与一张插入了无缝现代物体的错位版本组成。AnachroBench从三个方面进行评估：插入物体感知，测试模型是否能检测到插入的现代物体；时代-国家一致性，评估场景是否符合指定的时代与国家背景；条件时代-国家一致性，仅在正确感知插入物体的前提下衡量一致性判断。当模型感知到现代物体但仍判断场景历史一致时，即为错误的一致性判断。总体而言，AnachroBench揭示了插入物体感知与时代-国家一致性判断之间的差距，提供了对该行为的针对性评估。

Anytime-Valid PAC-Bayes Certificates for Adaptive Test-Time Scaling
自适应测试时缩放的即时有效 PAC-Bayes 证书
Test-time scaling systems often choose how much to sample, which prompt to use, and which verifier or aggregation rule to trust after repeatedly inspecting a calibration set. Standard validation error bars are not valid after this adaptive selection. We model a test-time scaling recipe as a randomized predictor with a random cost and prove a time-uniform PAC-Bayes certificate that holds simultaneously over all calibration times, all posterior mixtures over recipes, and all data-dependent stopping rules. Thus the same event covers the recipe search that precedes deployment, not merely the fixed recipe finally reported. For a finite grid of budgets and verifiers, the penalty is the familiar $\log M/n$, which in the worst case no certificate valid after selection can avoid, while non-uniform priors and localized posterior mixtures can give sharper certificates for structured searches. We specialize the result to self-consistency and show a complementary margin law: plurality voting improves exponentially in the sample budget only on examples where the correct answer is the generator's unique mode; otherwise more compute can provably amplify errors. The same margin analysis yields an oracle water-filling law for compute allocation. A synthetic audit quantifies the optimism caused by adaptive budget selection, and a 192-example GSM8K audit using gpt-4.1-mini generations illustrates risk-cost reporting for a real inference pipeline. At scale, with two models on GSM8K and MATH-500, selected-best error bars fall below the out-of-split GSM8K risk in up to 22.5% of random splits at a nominal 5% while the certificate never does, and on the full GSM8K test split it tightens to 0.109 (held-out risk 0.039). The results give a lightweight, distribution-free way to report risk and compute claims for adaptive inference systems.

测试时缩放系统通常在反复检查校准集后，决定采样量、使用哪个提示以及信任哪个验证器或聚合规则。标准的验证误差条在自适应选择后不再有效。我们将测试时缩放方案建模为带有随机成本的随机预测器，并证明了一个时间统一的PAC-Bayes证书，该证书在所有校准时间、所有配方后验混合以及所有数据依赖的停止规则下同时成立。因此，同一事件覆盖了部署前的配方搜索过程，而不仅仅是最终报告的固定配方。对于有限预算和验证器网格，惩罚项为熟悉的 $\\(\log M/n$$$，这是任何在选择后有效的证书都无法避免的最坏情况；而使用非均匀先验和局部后验混合可为结构化搜索提供更紧的证书。我们将结果特化到自洽性，并展示了一个互补的边际定律：多数投票仅在正确答案是生成器唯一众数的情况下，随着样本预算呈指数提升；否则，更多计算可能反而会明确放大错误。相同的边际分析导出了计算分配的Oracle水填法则。一项合成审计量化了自适应预算选择带来的乐观偏差；使用gpt-4.1-mini生成的192个GSM8K示例审计展示了真实推理管道中的风险-成本报告。在大规模场景下，使用两个模型在GSM8K和MATH-500上的实验显示，选定最优的误差条在名义5%水平下，有高达22.5%的随机划分中低于未拆分的GSM8K风险，而证书始终未失效；在完整的GSM8K测试集上，其紧度达到0.109（保留风险为0.039）。这些结果为自适应推理系统提供了一种轻量级、分布无关的风险与计算声明报告方式。

Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
语言模型智能体的信念可通过开放渠道中的真实证据被操纵
Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others. Drawing on cognitive theory of narrative understanding and film theory of montage, we introduce Generative Montage to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives. Across 1,090 rumour targets from six Twitter events, agents often accepted rumours overconfidently, with overall acceptance exceeding 65 percent in twelve of fourteen models. Acceptance remained above 50 percent after majority voting or review of the same evidence, showing how errors can reach downstream decisions. To explain this susceptibility, fragment interventions identify posts that influence belief within complete narratives. Synthetic controls then show that similar response patterns arise from valid evidence, separating belief influence from evidential support. This distinction motivates Grounded Monitor, a proof-of-concept neuro-symbolic runtime monitor that checks direct evidential support to guide agents' judgements, improving decision accuracy by 5.6 to 29.0 percentage points across original and anonymized settings. These findings expose a cognitive route to rumour amplification and support monitoring inferred relationships before agent-generated conclusions guide public decisions.
中文翻译
语言模型智能体的信念可以通过社交媒体等开放渠道被操纵，即使它们接收到的信息是真实的。当智能体通过自我生成的关系填补信息片段之间的空白时，可能会将这些关系视为既定事实，并将其传播为谣言。基于叙事理解的认知理论和蒙太奇电影理论，我们提出了生成式蒙太奇方法，以操作化这一失败现象——即叙事过拟合，通过协调智能体将真实片段组合成误导性叙述。在六个推特事件中涉及的1,090个谣言目标上，智能体往往过度自信地接受谣言，十四种模型中有十二种的整体接受率超过65%。即使经过多数投票或对相同证据的审查，接受率仍高于50%，表明错误可传递至下游决策。为解释这种易受攻击性，片段干预识别出影响完整叙述中信念的关键帖子。合成对照实验显示，类似响应模式也由有效证据引发，从而将信念影响与证据支持区分开来。这一区分促使我们提出Grounded Monitor，一个概念验证性的神经符号运行时监控器，通过检查直接证据支持来引导智能体判断，在原始和匿名设置下，决策准确率提升了5.6至29.0个百分点。这些发现揭示了谣言放大的认知路径，并支持在智能体生成结论前监控推断关系，以指导公共决策。

Probabilistic safety judges return the probability of a safety label and cheaply score reinforcement learning rollouts. A confidence gate sends only uncertain verdicts to a stronger LLM judge, which leaves confidently passed harm in a blind spot. Policies can exploit this blind spot, and commercial judges release new versions. We propose a protocol that validates such a judge before and during training, separates the share of confidently passed harm from its amount, and re-validates it after each judge change. We apply it to two versions of Jev, a commercial decision-only judge, and to an open guard classifier. Under the probability reward of Jev, passed harm shrinks in all 11 runs under the primary reference, mostly more slowly than caught harm, and concentrates in the blind spot. Binarizing this judge meets the escape criterion on Llama, and the open guard classifier shows an escape signal in one seed under a second reference. Guard classifiers share this blind spot, and even frontier LLM judges catch at most one of 10 human-labeled confident misses. DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
DetourBench：基于精确最小动作边界的任务级交互智能体评估
Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields the full-information minimum action count $L_0$ with a replayable witness; from graph-recoverable terminal states it also yields exact residual work $R_T$, which separates an episode that stopped one access short from one that wandered, while an irreversible wrong commitment is recorded as having no finite residual distance rather than assigned one. Success, attainment, residual progress, and normalized detour are reported separately. Across 375 scored episodes --- five model endpoints, 25 integrated tasks, three repeats --- success ranges from 58.7% to 96.0% while conditional attainment ranges from 0.803 to 0.890 and orders the models differently. Among recoverable failures, residual work separates near-complete trajectories from costly incompletion and from irreversible commitment. We open-source the instances, oracle witnesses, and evaluation harness at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench.

RAMP: Rethinking Multimodal Evaluation through Answer Readout Protocols

Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are often evaluated by converting model outputs into discrete answers. The conversion protocol determines which scores become predictions and can strongly influence the reported results. We introduce RAMP (Readout Aware Multimodal Protocol), a systematic framework that compares direct yes/no token logits, surface-form scores, and typed or reversed A/B interfaces under fixed model checkpoints and paired visual questions. On 500 POPE adversarial questions, typed versus bare readout changes accuracy by $-20.2$ percentage points for SmolVLM-256M, $-16.4$ for TinyLLaVA-1.1B, and $+1.8$ for Qwen2.5-VL-3B. Paired transitions reveal extensive prediction changes even when the net accuracy difference is small: 79 of 104 binary ChartQA items change correctness for SmolVLM-500M, despite a $+1.0$-point net difference. We further analyze prompt wording, candidate forms, option position, cross-task effects, and calibration. An independent offline replay reproduces 16,140 first-token decisions from saved raw scores with exact agreement. Our findings establish answer readout as a measurable component of multimodal evaluation and provide a reproducible protocol for analyzing model comparisons.

Necessary for What? Auditing Demographic Disclosure to LLM Synthetic Respondents
必要为何？对LLM合成应答者进行人口统计披露的审计
Large language models (LLMs) increasingly answer surveys on behalf of real panelists, and each panelist's recorded demographic attributes (e.g., age, education, ethnicity) are often placed in the prompt on the premise that richer profiles make more faithful synthetic respondents. While data minimization limits personal data to what a purpose requires, a synthetic survey serves several purposes at once, from predicting individual answers to estimating how opinions are distributed and comparing groups. We ask which of these purposes require the respondent's record, and whether improved estimates support sound conclusions about groups. We vary whose profile a model receives, where it comes from, and how many fields it contains, in two U.S. surveys with eleven open-weight and three hosted models, and compare each model with a statistical model fit to the same information. We make four contributions. First, we show that the record adds little to individual predictions and that, for the open-weight models, most of its gain in population estimates remains when it is replaced by census data or a synthetic persona. Second, we find that group comparisons improve only with the respondent's own record, and that even then the models' group differences rest more on the demographic label in the prompt than on the individual respondent, which the usual check of reproducing known group differences does not reveal. Third, we find that the models make groups look more alike than they are, keeping differences in circumstances while flattening or reversing differences in attitudes, most sharply for religious affiliation and ethnic origin, both special categories of personal data. Fourth, we outline an audit that a survey organization can run on questions it has already fielded to decide which estimates may use the record.

大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地代表真实受访者回答调查，且常将受访者的记录人口统计属性（如年龄、教育程度、族裔）放入提示中，前提是更丰富的档案能生成更忠实的合成应答者。尽管数据最小化原则要求仅保留目的所需的数据，但合成调查服务于多重目的，包括预测个体回答、估计观点分布以及群体比较。我们探讨这些目的中哪些需要受访者记录，以及改进的估计是否支持关于群体的合理结论。我们在两个美国调查中，使用十一个开放权重模型和三个托管模型，改变模型接收到的档案来源、内容字段数量，并将其与基于相同信息拟合的统计模型进行比较。我们做出四项贡献。第一，我们发现记录对个体预测帮助甚微，且对于开放权重模型，当用普查数据或合成人格替代时，多数人口估计增益仍保持不变。第二，群体比较仅在使用受访者本人记录时才改善，且即便如此，模型的群体差异更多依赖于提示中的身份标签而非个体受访者，这通常通过再现已知群体差异的检验无法察觉。第三，模型使群体看起来比实际更相似，保留了处境差异却弱化或反转了态度差异，尤其在宗教信仰和民族起源方面，这两类均为敏感个人数据。第四，我们提出一种审计方法，调查机构可对已有问卷执行，以决定哪些估计可使用记录。

ReconPotBench: Evaluating LLM Honeypots in Multi-Round Linux Reconnaissance
ReconPotBench：在多轮Linux侦察中评估LLM蜜罐
Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to build interactive honeypots, yet existing evaluations mainly assess isolated command outputs and cannot determine whether a system remains believable when later commands depend on earlier results. We present ReconPotBench, a multi-round benchmark for Linux reconnaissance honeypots. It contains 1{,}032 three-round reconnaissance interactions across eight reconnaissance categories, with reference outputs collected from a real Linux environment. Under a unified testing protocol, we compare Cowrie, open-source LLMs, and closed-source LLMs along three dimensions: round-level authenticity, cross-round contextual consistency, and hacker-oriented reconnaissance value. Results show that multi-round evaluation exposes failures hidden by single-round testing, as authenticity declines with interaction depth and both open-source and closed-source LLMs struggle to maintain coherent state across rounds. LLM-based honeypots nevertheless outperform Cowrie in authenticity and reconnaissance value, while Cowrie remains more consistent because of its rigid templated behavior. Category-level analysis further shows that tasks requiring systems to preserve network relationships across rounds are harder than tasks centered on explicit entities such as ports. ReconPotBench enables reproducible evaluation of LLM honeypots across authenticity, entity consistency, and hacker-perspective utility in dependent multi-round interactions. The dataset is available at: https://github.com/qianli-wang/ReconPotBench

LLM-based agents can automate model post-training, accelerating progress toward recursive self-improvement. Despite their promise, existing approaches remain under-explored and face two main challenges: (1) strategy lock-in that limits exploration beyond the initial strategy; and (2) coupled execution that obscures the effects of individual modifications. To address these challanges, we propose TrainExplorer, a multi-agent framework for autonomous post-training, that incorporates strategy planning and execution decoupling, to achieve broaden strategy exploration. First, strategy planning draws on scientific literature to construct a candidate search space of training strategies. Then, decoupled execution enables single-component interventions and attribution to guide strategy exploration. Extensive experiments on PostTrainBench demonstrate that TrainExplorer achieves a weighted aggregate score of 39.02, outperforming Claude Code using the same LLM by 7.32 and surpassing GPT-5.6 Sol-powered Codex, which scores 36.23. Code will be available.

When the Cheapest Feasible Router Fails: Auditing Deployment Commitments in Cost-Aware LLM Routing

Cost-aware LLM routing often selects the cheapest policy meeting empirical risk and coverage constraints. Yet a router that passes an audit can violate its fixed service contract on new requests, even when candidate policies are constructed independently. We study this deployment-commitment decision with disjoint construction, audit, and test samples. Across 19 RouterBench task families, the cheapest audit-feasible router deploys in 91.82% of opportunities but violates the held-out contract in 32.22% of deployments. We introduce Menu-Aware Routing Commitment (MARC), which qualifies policies using audit evidence and a serving-cost tolerance to retain the apparent winner, deploy a supported alternative, or defer. Its practical policywise variant (MARC-P) reduces observed conditional failure to 0.73% at 85.79% deployment, with higher serving cost; fixed-margin and formal risk-control procedures provide competitive alternatives. Nested audits show how added evidence changes deployable policy sets, and learned semantic routing exhibits the same commitment failure. These results establish deployment commitment as a distinct operational decision connecting router evaluation, service reliability, and inference cost.

Trait Collapse in Text-to-Image Generation: Evaluating and Mitigating Personality Inconsistency in Visual Storytelling

In visual storytelling, a believable character must not only look consistent across scenes but also \textit{behave} in ways that reflect their personality. Current text-to-image (T2I) models preserve visual appearance effectively, yet consistently fail to maintain personality-relevant behavior---a failure we term \textit{trait collapse}. We show that conventional metrics (CLIP Score, DINO similarity) are blind to this failure, and that abstract personality descriptors and scene-level emotion labels do not produce consistent improvements over neutral prompts across models. To systematically diagnose trait collapse, we introduce \textbf{ViStoryBench-Personality}, a story-level benchmark combining an expert-validated Visual Cues Lexicon (Fleiss' $κ= 0.757$) with a six-dimensional metric suite covering personality alignment, cross-scene stability, and behavioral coherence. Evaluating seven T2I systems, we confirm a persistent semantic gap between abstract trait labels and visual evidence, and find that visual identity consistency does not imply personality consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose \textbf{Trait-Behavior-Visual (TBV)}, a training-free prompting framework that decomposes personality traits into renderable visual constraints. TBV improves Personality Alignment Score by up to $+22.1\%$, with larger gains in models with stronger language-conditioning capacity.

通过未来研究方向选择激发大语言模型的研究品味
Research taste is increasingly discussed in the context of AI scientists, yet remains little studied or measured in LLMs. This judgment matters especially in open-ended research, where a direction must be chosen before a verifiable objective is available. We operationalize research taste through one task of the scientific workflow: choosing which future research direction to pursue given a research goal and current results. Rather than predicting downstream scientometric metrics or treating author choices as objectively correct, we evaluate models against human-authored future-work directions and report author alignment, stable divergence, and unstable choice as behavioral measures of research-direction preference. We construct an order-controlled evaluation of 80 pairwise comparisons from 19 ML papers published between December 2025 and February 2026 across four subdomains. Each query presents a research goal, hypotheses tested with key results, and two candidate future directions: one author-recommended direction and one plausible distractor sampled from a similar paper. Across eight LLMs, author alignment ranges from 45.0% to 67.5%, while stable divergence ranges from 15.0% to 36.2%. These divergences largely persist under similarity controls, prompt ablations, and an author-preference framing check, and inter-model agreement suggests that some non-author preferences are shared across models. We characterize what models diverge toward using transition-category labels and selected reasoning examples, finding recurring movement toward scaling/generalization and trade-offs between methodological and infrastructure/data extensions. We view this as an early descriptive evaluation for eliciting research taste profiles in LLMs, and as a step toward understanding and steering their research preferences as they take on more autonomous roles in novel open-ended scientific discovery.
中文翻译
研究品味在AI科学家背景下日益受到关注，但在大语言模型中仍缺乏深入研究或测量。这一判断尤其在开放式研究中至关重要，因为必须在可验证目标出现前就做出方向选择。我们通过科学工作流中的一个任务——基于研究目标和当前结果，选择应推进的未来研究方向——来操作化研究品味。不同于预测下游科学计量指标或将作者选择视为客观正确，我们以人类撰写的未来工作方向为基准，报告作者一致率、稳定分歧和不稳定选择作为研究方向偏好的行为度量。我们构建了一个有序控制的评估，涵盖19篇2025年12月至2026年2月发表的ML论文中的80组两两比较，覆盖四个子领域。每个查询呈现一个研究目标、已测试的假设及关键结果，以及两个候选未来方向：一个由作者推荐的方向和一个从类似论文中采样的合理干扰项。在八种大语言模型中，作者一致率范围为45.0%至67.5%，稳定分歧率为15.0%至36.2%。这些分歧在相似性控制、提示消融和作者偏好框架检查下仍持续存在，且模型间的一致性表明部分非作者偏好在模型间共享。我们通过转换类别标签和精选推理示例，分析模型偏离的方向，发现其反复趋向于扩展/泛化，以及方法论与基础设施/数据扩展之间的权衡。我们认为这是对大语言模型研究品味轮廓进行早期描述性评估的尝试，也是迈向理解并引导其研究偏好的重要一步，尤其是在它们承担更多自主角色参与新型开放式科学发现时。

Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
大语言模型智能体应在测试时何处进行适应？在上下文中、权重中，还是两者兼有？
LLM agents operating repeatedly in the same environment, such as a code repository, a database, or an application suite, encounter tasks that share latent structure. Experience can reveal this structure, allowing agents to reuse environment knowledge and learn from environmental feedback. Agents can adapt at test-time using this experience through two channels: retaining it in context and updating their weights. These channels are usually studied separately, leaving unclear what each contributes and when they complement each other. We compare in-context learning (ICL), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using GRPO, and self-distillation using SDPO, alone and in combination, using a shared online protocol and modular framework. Agents encounter matched task streams, are evaluated on each task before adapting to it, and learn only from their own attempts and environment feedback. We evaluate 14 adaptation mechanisms and a stateless baseline with Qwen3.5-9B on 109 tasks from four environments drawn from SWE-bench Verified, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, and BIRD-Critic-SQLite, using five task orders per environment. ICL provides the largest standalone gain: its best policy raises mean success across environments from 28.8% to 49.4%. Adding GRPO to this policy achieves the highest mean success, 51.6%. While adding GRPO improves the overall mean under every ICL policy, SDPO has mixed effects. Trace analyses show fewer lookups and shorter attempts under ICL, consistent with reusing knowledge of the shared structure. However, ICL also frequently skips inspection and verification for the current task. Adding GRPO to ICL helps restore these behaviors while preserving its reduced environment lookups. These observations suggest that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can refine how agents use retained experience, motivating the joint study of context management and weight updates.

在相同环境中反复运行的大语言模型智能体，如代码仓库、数据库或应用套件，会遇到具有潜在结构的任务。经验可以揭示这种结构，使智能体能够复用环境知识并从环境反馈中学习。智能体可通过两种渠道在测试时适应：将经验保留在上下文中，或更新其权重。这两种渠道通常被分别研究，导致难以明确各自贡献以及何时相互补充。我们通过共享在线协议和模块化框架，比较了上下文学习（ICL）、使用GRPO的可验证奖励强化学习，以及使用SDPO的自蒸馏，单独及组合使用。智能体面对匹配的任务流，在适应前对每项任务进行评估，并仅从自身尝试和环境反馈中学习。我们在SWE-bench Verified、AppWorld、ScienceWorld和BIRD-Critic-SQLite四个环境抽取的109个任务上，使用每种环境五个任务顺序，评估了14种适应机制和一个无状态基线，采用Qwen3.5-9B模型。ICL带来最大的独立收益：其最优策略将跨环境平均成功率从28.8%提升至49.4%。在该策略基础上加入GRPO，达到最高平均成功率51.6%。尽管在所有ICL策略下加入GRPO均提升整体平均表现，但SDPO效果参差不齐。轨迹分析显示，ICL条件下查找次数更少、尝试时间更短，符合对共享结构知识的复用。然而，ICL也常跳过当前任务的检查与验证。在ICL中加入GRPO有助于恢复这些行为，同时保留其减少环境查找的优势。这些观察表明，具有可验证奖励的强化学习可以优化智能体对保留经验的使用方式，从而推动对上下文管理与权重更新联合研究的必要性。

MathaMAGICal: Validating Trajectory Data Attribution During Capability Acquisition
MathaMAGICal：能力获取过程中轨迹数据归属的验证
Influence-function-based methods like MAGIC provide exact first-order scores for trajectory data attribution, yet only retraining indicates whether those scores accurately predict data removal. We evaluate MAGIC on $86$M- and $152$M-parameter GPT-2-style models learning multistep arithmetic from scratch on filtered web text and four synthetic math families. Full-run attribution at $86$M suffers from numerical overflow, and even with metagradient clipping, scores correlate near chance with retraining (linear datamodeling score, LDS, $0.17$--$0.22$). In contrast, short checkpoint windows yield stable, accurate predictions at both scales (LDS $0.86$--$0.99$ across four $100$-step windows at $152$M), whereas a single-checkpoint gradient-dot baseline shows near-zero correlation. Rankings of individual training blocks predict retraining only within that single run and do not transfer across seeds or hyperparameters ($ρ\le 0.09$), whereas format-level patterns replicate across runs. Two data families, worked examples and primitive facts, occupy $2.1$--$2.6\times$ their corpus share in both the helpful and harmful $5\%$ score tails, reflecting strong bidirectional local sensitivity distinct from net benefit under multi-epoch family deletion. These results show that trajectory attribution is reliable within short, validated windows and yields family-level insights that generalize across runs.

基于影响函数的方法（如MAGIC）可为轨迹数据归属提供精确的一阶评分，但只有通过重新训练才能判断这些评分是否准确预测数据移除的影响。我们在8600万和1.52亿参数的GPT-2风格模型上评估MAGIC，这些模型从过滤后的网络文本和四个合成数学家族中从零开始学习多步算术。在8600万参数规模下，完整运行的归属分析因数值溢出而不可行；即使采用元梯度裁剪，评分与重新训练结果的相关性接近随机水平（线性数据建模得分LDS为0.17–0.22）。相比之下，短检查点窗口在两个规模下均产生稳定且准确的预测（在15200万参数模型上，四个100步窗口的LDS为0.86–0.99），而单检查点梯度点积基线的相关性几乎为零。单个训练块的排名仅在该次运行内有效，无法跨种子或超参数迁移（ρ≤0.09），而格式级模式则可在不同运行中复现。两类数据——示例题解和基础事实——在有益和有害的前5%评分尾部中占据其语料库份额的2.1–2.6倍，反映出与多周期家族删除下的净收益不同的强双向局部敏感性。这些结果表明，轨迹归属在短期、经验证的窗口内是可靠的，并能生成可跨运行泛化的家族级洞见。

Objectify, Don't Delete: Complaint-Derived Evaluation of Ambient Clinical Notes
对象化，而非删除：基于投诉的环境临床笔记评估
Evaluating the quality of AI-generated clinical notes is hard: standard metrics like ROUGE measure lexical similarity to reference notes, while expert checklists encode what committees believe matters. Neither captures what clinicians actually complain about. Recent work has shown that evaluation criteria can be mined from user feedback and filtered to criteria that LLM judges can reliably enforce. We argue that this is where much of the value is lost. The criteria that fail enforceability are disproportionately the ones clinicians raise most often, because high-frequency complaints are stated as several questions glued together. No yes/no judgment can grade such composites as posed. We introduce an objectification step that rewrites such criteria into sets of scoped, determinate decisions. We demonstrate the approach through an evaluation pipeline that mines criteria from complaints, objectifies them, and deploys LLM judges against both planted defects and production notes. Across eleven defects planted into ACI-bench reference notes, objectified judges localize violations with median recall of 0.95, while reference metrics change by at most 0.037. Given the complaint as one broad question, the same judges still find every planted defect, but they also flag 70% of the unperturbed reference notes; one section-pair question per call raises Youden's J from 0.30 to 0.72 (by 0.19 to 0.26 with prompt effort matched). We release ACI-Defect, a perturbation benchmark; clinician-reviewed instance-level labels showing quality gaps in the ACI-bench gold standard (32 of 40 notes contain hallucinations; 40 of 40 omit discussed facts); and grounding-judge verdicts. On 1,446 production notes, mean instance-rate burden falls at every clinician-rating step (rho=-0.15), a small association. Defect counts have to be kept per span rather than collapsed into one pass/fail bit per note.
中文翻译
评估AI生成临床笔记的质量非常困难：标准指标如ROUGE仅衡量与参考笔记的词汇相似性，而专家清单则反映委员会认为重要的内容。两者均未能捕捉临床医生实际抱怨的问题。近期研究显示，评估标准可从用户反馈中挖掘，并筛选出LLM评判员能够可靠执行的标准。我们认为，这正是价值流失的关键所在。那些难以执行的标准恰恰是临床医生最常提出的，因为高频投诉通常由多个问题拼接而成。单一的“是/否”判断无法对这类复合问题进行评分。我们引入了‘对象化’步骤，将此类标准重写为一系列有范围限定、确定性的决策。我们通过一个评估流程展示了该方法：从投诉中挖掘标准，进行对象化处理，并使用LLM评判员对植入缺陷和生产笔记进行评估。在ACI-bench参考笔记中植入11种缺陷，对象化评判员的中位召回率达0.95，而参考指标变化不超过0.037。若将投诉视为一个宽泛问题，同一评判员仍能发现所有植入缺陷，但也误报了70%的未扰动参考笔记；每通电话对应一个段落对问题时，Youden's J值从0.30提升至0.72（提示努力匹配时，从0.19升至0.26）。我们发布了ACI-Defect，一个扰动基准；经临床医生评审的实例级标签，揭示了ACI-bench黄金标准中的质量差距（40篇中有32篇包含幻觉；40篇全部遗漏讨论的事实）；以及基于判据的判决结果。在1446条生产笔记上，每个临床评分步骤的平均实例负担呈轻微下降趋势（rho=-0.15）。缺陷计数必须按片段保留，而非合并为每篇笔记一个通过/失败比特。

Macro Control and Capability Evaluation of Black-Box World Models: A Two-Regime Framework for LLM-Agent Markets
黑箱世界模型的宏观控制与能力评估：面向LLM智能体市场的双范式框架
Large language model (LLM) agents can be organized into multi-agent markets that act as world models, mapping macro information to emergent macro dynamics while the evaluator observes only macro inputs and outputs. This paper separates a model's capability into two stages that a single aggregate score cannot separate: information simulation, from macro information to micro behavior, and macro emergence, from micro behavior to the macro outcome. We introduce a soft macro-control method that announces a public reference path day by day without touching individual decisions, orders, or matching, and a two-regime evaluation framework that measures both stages from macro observations alone. In the reference-only regime the symmetric true and flipped references share a common level R, which measures realization under the announced reference, while their paired gap B measures structural bias; in the information-injection regime external information dilutes the reference, so only the true-flipped gap Delta remains interpretable. On five single-index LLM-agent markets, announcing a target path shifts the realized path toward the announced target on both announced references under both information conditions. Relative to the no-reference path, the tracking score is higher by 0.306 and 0.415 without news and by 0.183 and 0.329 with news; within the stock/cash scan structural bias is lowest at 70/30 (B=0.042); realization peaks at a 3:7 technical share (R=0.894 versus 0.358 for technical-only); and Delta is 0.0341 with fundamental data and 0.0487 with news. Both stages use the same two observable scores, each read in the regime where it is interpretable.
中文翻译
大型语言模型（LLM）智能体可组织为多智能体市场，作为世界模型，将宏观信息映射为涌现的宏观动态，而评估者仅观察宏观输入与输出。本文将模型能力分为两个阶段，单一综合评分无法区分：信息模拟（从宏观信息到微观行为）和宏观涌现（从微观行为到宏观结果）。我们提出一种软宏观控制方法，每日公布公开参考路径，而不干预个体决策、订单或匹配；并引入双范式评估框架，仅通过宏观观测测量这两个阶段。在仅参考范式中，真实与翻转参考共享同一水平R，衡量在公布参考下的实现程度，而其配对差距B衡量结构性偏差；在信息注入范式中，外部信息稀释参考，因此仅真实-翻转差距Delta具有可解释性。在五个单指数LLM智能体市场中，公布目标路径在两种信息条件下均使实现路径向公布目标靠拢。相对于无参考路径，跟踪得分分别提高0.306和0.415（无新闻时）以及0.183和0.329（有新闻时）；在股票/现金扫描中，结构性偏差最低为70/30（B=0.042）；实现度在技术占比3:7时达到峰值（R=0.894，技术仅时为0.358）；Delta在基本面数据下为0.0341，在新闻下为0.0487。两个阶段均使用相同的两个可观测分数，每个在可解释的范式中读取。

Staged Semantic Distillation: Preserving Free-Form Semantics in a Low-Compute Non-LLM Surrogate of a Staged LLM Agent
分阶段语义蒸馏：在低计算量的非LLM代理中保留分阶段LLM代理的自由形式语义
Staged LLM agents make market and social simulators realistic, but one 102-day run of a 200-agent, ten-index market simulator issues 203,100 language-model calls and returns one realization. Conventional low-compute distillation drops their free-form intermediate state. We present staged semantic distillation, a low-compute method that preserves non-structured semantics in a non-LLM student trained from one recorded trace. A frozen encoder maps each teacher output to a 1024-d vector; the student sees typed stage-tagged vectors with stage-specific visibility, is jointly supervised, and trains with scheduled self-history. One TwinMarket trace yields a 13.2M-parameter deterministic student that trains in 1,658 seconds on one 8-GB GPU and runs with zero teacher or decoder calls and no text generation (0.14 ms per decision). Its analysis stays close to the teacher (cosine 0.943), and swapping semantic inputs between agents moves 64.7% of decisions against 12.8% for a matched donor, so the channel is preserved and live. We use the surrogate to study what the transfer carries. It reaches 0.8347 balanced accuracy on the teacher-forced replay and 0.7783 [0.766,0.791] on the deployment decoder; the five-seed gain over a no-semantic retrain is +2.2 [1.21,3.14]. Against the teacher's own re-sampling level, round-one R is 97.1% [95.8,98.4] and 92.3% [89.0,95.4]; R is a diagnostic, not an accuracy. A five-seed content-by-schedule study isolates the gain: scheduled self-history carries it (+2.2 [1.21,3.14]); shuffled and constant content controls reproduce it, while content matters teacher-forced. The design rule: invest in the deployment schedule, let content earn its place at the teacher-forced operating point. A 20-seed, 200,000-decision sweep takes 12 minutes with zero LLM calls, versus three hours for the teacher. The paper is a method-and-case-study contribution on one simulator and trace.

分阶段LLM代理使市场和社交模拟器更加真实，但一个包含200个智能体、十指标的市场模拟器运行102天会发出203,100次语言模型调用，仅返回一次结果。传统的低计算量蒸馏方法会丢失其自由形式的中间状态。我们提出分阶段语义蒸馏，一种低计算量的方法，能够在从单条记录轨迹训练的非LLM学生模型中保留非结构化语义。冻结编码器将每个教师输出映射为1024维向量；学生模型看到带有阶段标签的向量，并具有阶段特定的可见性，接受联合监督并使用调度自历史进行训练。一条TwinMarket轨迹生成了一个1320万参数的确定性学生模型，可在单个8GB GPU上用1658秒完成训练，运行时无需教师或解码器调用，也不生成文本（每次决策耗时0.14毫秒）。其分析结果与教师模型高度接近（余弦相似度0.943），在智能体间交换语义输入时，有64.7%的决策发生变化，而匹配捐赠者仅为12.8%，说明通道被有效保留且处于活跃状态。我们利用该代理研究转移内容的特性。在教师强制重播任务上达到0.8347的平衡准确率，在部署解码器上达到0.7783 [0.766,0.791]；相较于无语义重训练，五种子实验提升+2.2 [1.21,3.14]。与教师自身重采样水平相比，第一轮R值为97.1% [95.8,98.4] 和 92.3% [89.0,95.4]；R是诊断指标而非准确率。五种子内容-调度研究揭示了提升来源：调度自历史带来了这一增益（+2.2 [1.21,3.14]）；打乱和恒定内容控制组重现了该效果，而内容在教师强制条件下至关重要。设计原则：投资于部署调度，让内容在教师强制操作点上自然获得位置。20种子、20万次决策的全面扫描仅需12分钟，且无需LLM调用，相较教师模型的三小时大幅缩减。本文是对单一模拟器和轨迹的方法与案例研究贡献。

Beyond Plain MCP: Do Decision Models and Code Mode Make Tool Use Cheaper and Faster?
超越普通MCP：决策模型与代码模式是否使工具使用更便宜更快？
Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways manage tool catalogs for language model agents using two primary paradigms: code mode where agents write scripts against tool stubs and decision layers which are cheap routers that preselect tool subsets. Using a controlled harness across 12 servers, up to 1,958 distractor tools, and three open-weight agents including Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron, we present a preregistered evaluation on a sealed test split to determine when each approach succeeds. Code mode substantially outperforms plain MCP, cutting token usage by 70 to 90 percent while significantly boosting utility. Declaring return-shape hints in code mode stubs is a first-order variable, swinging success by up to 39.5 points for lower-performing agents, an effect larger than adding a router. The central hypothesis that a decision layer in front of code mode beats code mode alone is not confirmed, showing minor, statistically non-significant improvements for weaker agents and a slight cost for the strongest. We publicly release our harness, a finetuned 4B tool selection model, and all evaluation traces to support robust community experimentation on local AI privacy and agent architectures.

Relative to the full menu on the three smaller label sets, accuracy differences range from -0.5 to +7.2 percentage points, while input token usage falls by factors of 3.2-22.9. Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Models classified children as over 13 on 2.5% to 42.5% of audio responses, and every model that answered placed some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18. While measuring these rates, we uncovered three distinct failure modes. A client library silently double-encoded speech samples, leading one model to classify children aged 5 to 10 years old as being in their thirties and forties with hallucinated explanations. A second model's endpoint was replaced by a successor that refused nearly every age-related question and never produced an age. Every model sometimes placed the same speech sample under 13 and over 18 years of age, but a third model went further, giving threshold answers that contradicted its own numeric estimates. None of these failure modes produced a warning, a status code, or a change in output format, so they would all pass standard monitoring. These results demonstrate why child-safety claims about age assurance should be evaluated at the level of the pipeline rather than the model. We describe the reporting practices that would make such failures detectable.

MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?

Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, externalizing the agent's event understanding, declared priorities, and harm acknowledgment. Across ten models from four frontier model families, harmful selection rates remain consistently high and rise by +15 percentage points on average under an economic survival incentive. Frontier alignment-trained models commit to harm-tolerant selection at initialization while suppressing the explicit harm acknowledgment that previously accompanied it. In competitive tournaments, ethical agents finish higher overall, yet moderation penalties fail to suppress harm: harmful selection rates remain elevated in rounds following a removal, indicating the moderation mechanism does not function as a deterrent. We further train MemeAgent, a 2B-parameter verifier on the simulation's BDI logs, which outperforms zero-shot frontier verifiers on in-distribution audits (97.5% vs. 63-74% accuracy on the Pass vs. Block decision) and generalizes to external multimodal harm benchmarks (78% vs. 50-56% on Hateful Memes). The same logs that surface the failure mode also help train the model that detects it.

对齐训练的大语言模型（LLM）代理越来越多地部署在自主、多轮环境中，此时伦理合规性可能与任务成功直接冲突。尽管安全文献详尽记录了诸如奉承和奖励劫持等失败模式，却大多忽视了一个关键脆弱性：代理在模拟存在性经济压力下的行为。我们引入MemeEconomy，一个包含多模态代理市场的仿真环境，其中LLM代理扮演 meme 投资者角色。代理从五级危害分类体系中选择内容，并针对低压力和高压力（生存）环境的目标社区进行决策。每个决策均以信念-欲望-意图（BDI）框架记录，作为诊断工具，外化代理对事件的理解、声明的优先事项及对危害的承认。在来自四个前沿模型家族的十种模型中，有害选择率始终保持高位，并在经济生存激励下平均上升15个百分点。前沿对齐训练模型在初始状态即承诺容忍危害的选择，同时压制此前伴随的显式危害承认。在竞争性锦标赛中，道德代理总体排名更高，但监管处罚未能抑制危害：在被移除后的回合中，有害选择率仍居高不下，表明监管机制未起到威慑作用。我们进一步训练了MemeAgent——一个基于仿真BDI日志的20亿参数验证器，在分布内审计中表现优于零样本前沿验证器（97.5% vs. 63-74%准确率），并在外部多模态危害基准测试中实现泛化（78% vs. 50-56%在Hateful Memes上的表现）。揭示失败模式的日志也用于训练检测该模式的模型。

T2T Technical Report: Synthesizing GUI Agent Trajectories at Scale from Video Tutorials
T2T技术报告：从视频教程大规模合成GUI代理轨迹
Training generalist GUI agents requires large volumes of interaction trajectories comprising screenshot sequences paired with grounded UI actions, yet collecting such data through human demonstration is expensive and difficult to scale. Although public software tutorial videos contain rich operational demonstrations, their continuous pixel streams lack discrete action boundaries, semantic intents, and precise spatial coordinates, making them difficult to use directly for model training. To address this, we present T2T (Tutorial-to-Trajectory), a fully automated pipeline for synthesizing GUI agent trajectories at scale. T2T spans desktop, web, and mobile platforms to convert unannotated video tutorials into structured, executable interaction trajectories. To guarantee trajectory quality, T2T combines active segment filtering, keyframe identification via localized UI change, shortcut-free observation frame selection, presence-aware grounding, and two-stage action-space normalization. These refined trajectories are then converted into multi-task training views spanning navigation, planning, forward dynamics, and grounding. We fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B on a subset of the more than one million human-annotation-free training samples generated by this pipeline. Evaluations show that the model achieves consistent gains across multiple benchmarks covering desktop, web, and mobile environments, including OSWorld-G, ScreenSpot-Pro, AndroidControl, and AgentNetBench, indicating improved core capabilities in grounding, step-level instruction execution, and trajectory-level decision-making. Notably, all gains are achieved without any in-distribution training data from target domains. Learning exclusively from trajectories extracted from public videos via the T2T pipeline, the model exhibits cross-application and cross-task generalization capabilities.

How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
如何打造一个道德代理：情感主义与理性主义作为AI视角
Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), for those refined capabilities. Our approach offers several benefits. Firstly, it may demonstrate whether the behaviors of AI systems are aligned, or in a broad sense desirable. Secondly, the debate may inform policy questions (e.g., what models should be deployed in which contexts?). Thirdly, our approach may complement engineering and design efforts: when capabilities can be precisely characterized, they can inform the development of models. Fourthly, applying our moral reasoning concepts in the new context of AI systems should improve our understanding of those concepts.

Knowledge graphs constructed from text can contain facts that are individually plausible yet inconsistent with their relational context. We introduce SERAG, a supervised anomaly detector that combines two complementary plausibility estimates: a semantic score computed from separately encoded subject, relation, and object labels, and a relational score obtained through a relational graph convolutional network. The scores are standardized, calibrated, and fused. We evaluate the method on a subset of ICEWS18 with vocabulary-constrained synthetic anomalies generated by an LLM, using pooled and chronological splits. At 10% anomaly prevalence, SERAG achieves test AUPRCs of 0.321 and 0.258, respectively, compared with 0.159 and 0.146 for the strongest adapted baseline. Fusion improves mean test AUPRC over either branch alone, with a larger gain in the pooled protocol and a smaller validation-selected gain in the chronological protocol. Additional anomaly supervision improves performance. These results support the complementarity of textual and relational signals for detecting synthetic anomalies under the evaluated protocols.

A unified capability representation connects tool discovery, world execution, and task synthesis, allowing new capabilities to enter evaluation through a shared construction pipeline. Error analysis reveals challenges in answer delivery, feasibility diagnosis, and temporal coordination. Construction experiments demonstrate scalability across domains and token efficiency: world distillation reduces token consumption by 0.9-66.0% and 46.2-92.5% relative to Codex with low and xhigh reasoning effort, respectively, while achieving broader capability coverage. We distil it into LATTE-WordSeg-Lite, a CPU segmenter of 1.17M parameters that keeps the lattice as features. A Generative AI-Driven Architecture for Whole-Home Intelligent Services: Edge Models, Memory Management, and Household Applications
面向全屋智能服务的生成式AI驱动架构：边缘模型、记忆管理与家庭应用
Generative artificial intelligence is entering the home. Cloud-based assistants face governance limitations in data transmission, continuous availability, and the reliability of physical actions, which are especially salient in households where devices remain online, data accumulate over time, and commands trigger real-world actions. Using the home local server as a unifying organizing axis, this article develops a design-oriented review framework. Sources from arXiv, CNKI, ACL Anthology, and official documentation were searched through November 2026 and coded into five evidence categories: reviews, system prototypes, benchmarks, HCI and eldercare studies, and official documentation. System designs were mapped onto shared architectural modules, identifying nine recurrent responsibilities of the home local server. Generative models support perceptual interpretation, intent understanding, and candidate planning, while deterministic validation, knowledge-graph constraints, and authorization leases confine candidate actions to an inspectable space. Home control, emotional companionship, and intelligent guarding can be compared within a common framework: they share state and memory but differ in latency, false positive and negative rates, proactivity, and permissions. Existing benchmarks rely on virtual environments and cannot substitute for real-deployment evaluation. Local deployment is not inherently safer, and technical continuity alone does not establish the social or medical effects of companionship and guarding. The article proposes a five-dimensional evaluation framework covering architectural capability, system resources, privacy, safety and reliability, and human experience, together with six design principles and a future research agenda for local-first intelligent home systems.

Visual grounding benchmarks usually do not consider the contextual uncertainty of real-world scenarios. In this study, we construct a novel benchmark, the Japanese evaluation for Ambiguous visual Grounding with Dialogue (JAG-D) dataset. It consists of human-robot conversational multimodal interactions covering different types of ambiguity, arising from visual and linguistic categories. We evaluate the capabilities of different state-of-the-art Visual Language Models (VLMs) for ambiguity recognition and resolution. We compare dialogue context grounding performance for visual and linguistic ambiguity resolution. Our experiments show that VLMs can substantially improve the resolution of linguistic ambiguity, especially Japanese zero anaphora, by using dialogue context. SWE-WhatIf: Simulating Real Users of Coding Agents from Recorded Session

Recorded sessions between users and coding agents offer a way to evaluate how agents complete real-world tasks and interact with users. However, these sessions cannot simply be replayed with new agents, because recorded user replies may no longer apply when an agent takes a different trajectory. We introduce SWE-WhatIf, which replays recorded sessions with new agents by modeling the user's intents, the criteria for satisfying them, and the conditions under which they arise. Using this model, a user simulator generates replies that adapt to unseen agent turns while remaining grounded in the recording. Across 89 real-world sessions, SWE-WhatIf generated the replies most similar to those of real users and matched the strongest baseline when sessions were rewritten. To test adaptation, we replay sessions with agents instructed to avoid or repeat actions that the recorded user pushed back on. SWE-WhatIf produced the highest win rate for avoiding these actions (66.3%), significantly above chance. We further demonstrate its utility by ranking five LLMs as coding agents, where the highest-ranked model depended on how users specified and developed their intents, and a study with 16 users, where replaying their own sessions changed 14 participants' rankings and informed their future agent use.
