Language models increasingly write the explanations people receive when a rule system denies their request. If several rules deny the request independently, an explanation can name a true reason and still leave the person denied after they fix it. We call the missing property recourse validity: changing what the explanation cites, without changing what was asked for, can flip the decision. We compute it exactly, and a hitting-set argument predicts from the policy alone when a correct reason fails. In six of seven rule systems ported from access control and US benefit eligibility, a single correct reason almost never gives recourse when several reasons apply. Across 20 LLMs, checks of whether the cited reasons are correct, computed or asked of an LLM judge, are close to chance at spotting this failure, as the argument predicts. A strong judge asked whether acting on the explanation would work does spot it. Stronger and reasoning models do better but still fail on many denials with four or more independent reasons. Asking for every rule helps every open model with room to improve. Explanations of eligibility decisions should be built from the decision function and judged by whether acting on them works.

When an authorization policy blocks an agent's tool call, the audit log should name the facts that forced the decision and nothing more. For an executable policy over an enumerable context space this minimal sufficient reason can be computed exactly, so an explanation is scored against ground truth rather than a proxy for it. We use that exactness to ask what a model can learn from a verifier that has no error in it. The explainer sees one request and one decision, never the policy, and has thirty turns in which it may call the policy on altered requests and ask whether a candidate set of facts is sufficient. Frontier models find the exact reason about half the time with the tools alone, and one sentence telling them to shrink the answer lifts Haiku 4.5 from 58% to 75%. A 4B model fine-tuned on 2000 traces of the deletion algorithm reaches 92% on the policy it was trained on. Teacher kind is what moves this: at matched data size the algorithm-taught student leads the frontier-taught one in all three training seeds, and the two arms never overlap. What the student learns is a fixed schedule of sufficiency checks, and the schedule does not travel. On three public policies it never saw, its answers stay sufficient (94%) and stop being minimal (48%), while Haiku under the same sentence is exact on all 47 episodes. Reinforcement learning from the exact reward leaves held-out accuracy where it was and inverts the strategy, from probing the policy to spending the entire budget on sufficiency checks. The oracle made the effect of training legible, but it did not make training better.

From Recursion to Convolution: Parallel Self-Improvement for Multi-Agent Systems

Multi-agent self-improvement enables agents to improve through interaction and feedback. However, sequential dependencies across agents and refinement rounds can propagate errors, increase computational costs, and limit parallelism. Moreover, refining individual features or agents in isolation can overlook their dependencies and restrict collective coordination. To address these challenges, we propose ConvRSI, a framework for parallelizing multi-agent self-improvement through convolution. ConvRSI couples intra-agent convolution, which jointly refines related agent features, with inter-agent graph convolution, which aggregates messages according to the collaboration topology. Both stages operate in latent space, enabling parallel updates without repeatedly decoding and re-encoding intermediate messages. Experiments on MATH-500 show that ConvRSI achieves 5.04% performance improvement while reducing 17.27% inference cost, and 45.11% latency compared with RecursiveMAS. It also supports diverse collaboration patterns by representing their topologies as adjacency matrices. These results demonstrate the potential of convolutional co-evolution for efficient multi-agent self-improvement. Our code and datasets are provided in https://github.com/LYA2333/ConvRSI.

DetourBench: Trajectory-Level Evaluation of Interactive Agents with Exact Minimum-Action Bounds
DetourBench：基于精确最小动作边界的任务级交互智能体评估
Benchmarks judge language-model agents mainly by whether they reach the correct final state, not by how they got there. Endpoint scoring cannot separate an agent that retrieved exactly the evidence a decision required from one that read most of the environment, nor an agent that never located the evidence from one that stopped a single action short. Settling this needs a reference cost, and authored solutions establish only that a task is solvable, not that no shorter route exists. We present DetourBench, which constrains the environment until that minimum is computable. Each task is a finite, partially observable transition system with unit-cost accesses whose resources become globally addressable after discovery. Exhaustive search yields the full-information minimum action count $L_0$ with a replayable witness; from graph-recoverable terminal states it also yields exact residual work $R_T$, which separates an episode that stopped one access short from one that wandered, while an irreversible wrong commitment is recorded as having no finite residual distance rather than assigned one. Success, attainment, residual progress, and normalized detour are reported separately. Across 375 scored episodes --- five model endpoints, 25 integrated tasks, three repeats --- success ranges from 58.7% to 96.0% while conditional attainment ranges from 0.803 to 0.890 and orders the models differently. Among recoverable failures, residual work separates near-complete trajectories from costly incompletion and from irreversible commitment. We open-source the instances, oracle witnesses, and evaluation harness at https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench.

基准测试主要根据语言模型智能体是否达到正确最终状态来评判，而忽视其达成过程。终点评分无法区分一个恰好获取决策所需证据的智能体与一个读取了大部分环境的智能体，也无法区分从未找到证据的智能体与仅差一步就完成的智能体。解决这一问题需要参考成本，但现有方案仅证明任务可解，未验证是否存在更短路径。我们提出DetourBench，通过约束环境使最小成本可计算。每个任务是一个有限、部分可观测的转移系统，具有单位成本访问，资源在发现后变为全局可访问。通过穷举搜索可获得全信息下的最小动作数$L_0$及可重放的证据；从图可恢复的终止状态还可获得精确残余工作$R_T$，能区分仅差一次访问即完成的轨迹与漫游轨迹，而不可逆错误承诺则记录为无有限残余距离而非赋予一个值。分别报告成功性、达成度、残余进展和归一化绕行度。在375个评分回合中（五个模型端点，25个集成任务，三轮重复），成功率在58.7%至96.0%之间，条件达成率在0.803至0.890之间，且对模型排序不同。在可恢复的失败案例中，残余工作可区分接近完整的轨迹、代价高昂的不完整以及不可逆承诺。我们已开源实例、Oracle证据和评估工具包，地址为https://github.com/DatagridsAI/DetourBench。

Large language models (LLMs) increasingly answer surveys on behalf of real panelists, and each panelist's recorded demographic attributes (e.g., age, education, ethnicity) are often placed in the prompt on the premise that richer profiles make more faithful synthetic respondents. While data minimization limits personal data to what a purpose requires, a synthetic survey serves several purposes at once, from predicting individual answers to estimating how opinions are distributed and comparing groups. We ask which of these purposes require the respondent's record, and whether improved estimates support sound conclusions about groups. We vary whose profile a model receives, where it comes from, and how many fields it contains, in two U.S. surveys with eleven open-weight and three hosted models, and compare each model with a statistical model fit to the same information. We make four contributions. First, we show that the record adds little to individual predictions and that, for the open-weight models, most of its gain in population estimates remains when it is replaced by census data or a synthetic persona. Second, we find that group comparisons improve only with the respondent's own record, and that even then the models' group differences rest more on the demographic label in the prompt than on the individual respondent, which the usual check of reproducing known group differences does not reveal. Third, we find that the models make groups look more alike than they are, keeping differences in circumstances while flattening or reversing differences in attitudes, most sharply for religious affiliation and ethnic origin, both special categories of personal data. Fourth, we outline an audit that a survey organization can run on questions it has already fielded to decide which estimates may use the record.

大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地代表真实受访者回答调查，且常将受访者的记录人口统计属性（如年龄、教育程度、族裔）放入提示中，前提是更丰富的档案能生成更忠实的合成应答者。尽管数据最小化原则要求仅保留目的所需的数据，但合成调查服务于多重目的，包括预测个体回答、估计观点分布以及群体比较。我们探讨这些目的中哪些需要受访者记录，以及改进的估计是否支持关于群体的合理结论。我们在两个美国调查中，使用十一个开放权重模型和三个托管模型，改变模型接收到的档案来源、内容字段数量，并将其与基于相同信息拟合的统计模型进行比较。我们做出四项贡献。第一，我们发现记录对个体预测帮助甚微，且对于开放权重模型，当用普查数据或合成人格替代时，多数人口估计增益仍保持不变。第二，群体比较仅在使用受访者本人记录时才改善，且即便如此，模型的群体差异更多依赖于提示中的身份标签而非个体受访者，这通常通过再现已知群体差异的检验无法察觉。第三，模型使群体看起来比实际更相似，保留了处境差异却弱化或反转了态度差异，尤其在宗教信仰和民族起源方面，这两类均为敏感个人数据。第四，我们提出一种审计方法，调查机构可对已有问卷执行，以决定哪些估计可使用记录。

Trait Collapse in Text-to-Image Generation: Evaluating and Mitigating Personality Inconsistency in Visual Storytelling
文本到图像生成中的性格坍塌：评估与缓解视觉叙事中的人格不一致性
In visual storytelling, a believable character must not only look consistent across scenes but also \textit{behave} in ways that reflect their personality. Current text-to-image (T2I) models preserve visual appearance effectively, yet consistently fail to maintain personality-relevant behavior---a failure we term \textit{trait collapse}. We show that conventional metrics (CLIP Score, DINO similarity) are blind to this failure, and that abstract personality descriptors and scene-level emotion labels do not produce consistent improvements over neutral prompts across models. To systematically diagnose trait collapse, we introduce \textbf{ViStoryBench-Personality}, a story-level benchmark combining an expert-validated Visual Cues Lexicon (Fleiss' $κ= 0.757$) with a six-dimensional metric suite covering personality alignment, cross-scene stability, and behavioral coherence. Evaluating seven T2I systems, we confirm a persistent semantic gap between abstract trait labels and visual evidence, and find that visual identity consistency does not imply personality consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose \textbf{Trait-Behavior-Visual (TBV)}, a training-free prompting framework that decomposes personality traits into renderable visual constraints. TBV improves Personality Alignment Score by up to $+22.1\%$, with larger gains in models with stronger language-conditioning capacity.

HEAMS: Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems
HEAMS：智能体记忆系统的综合评估
Memory systems allow AI agents to persist information across interactions, making them more personalized and more capable on long-horizon tasks. This persistence introduces new risks: stored information can be disclosed in inappropriate contexts, resist correction or deletion, be retained beyond what users desire, or be poisoned to influence later agent behaviour. Yet memory systems are typically evaluated on task performance and efficiency alone. We argue that a memory system should instead be understood as the custodian of its user's persistent information, with responsibilities that extend beyond helping an agent complete its tasks, and that it should be evaluated holistically against all such responsibilities. We present Holistic Evaluation of Agent Memory Systems (HEAMS), an open-source framework for evaluating agent memory systems in this way. First, we state the responsibilities of agent memory systems as explicit behavioural desiderata spanning performance, efficiency, security, privacy, and user sovereignty. Second, we assemble a benchmark suite that covers these desiderata and acknowledge the gaps that remain. Third, we develop MilaMem, a prototype memory system, and a governance layer that can wrap any memory system, enabling controlled study of memory system design choices. Fourth, we compare memory systems across the full HEAMS benchmark suite. We find that no memory system leads every performance benchmark, and strong performance scores may coexist with poor privacy, user-sovereignty, and security scores. Governance strongly influences results: recall policies can reduce inappropriate disclosure at a cost in helpfulness, while both recall and retention policies improve poisoning resistance. Performance and efficiency benchmarks alone therefore cannot reveal how well a memory system meets its responsibilities. Code: https://github.com/milatechtransfer/heams
中文翻译
记忆系统使AI智能体能够在交互过程中持续保留信息，从而在长周期任务中更具个性化和更强能力。这种持续性引入了新风险：存储的信息可能在不恰当的情境下被披露，难以纠正或删除，超出用户期望而长期保留，或被污染以影响后续行为。然而，记忆系统通常仅根据任务性能和效率进行评估。我们认为，记忆系统应被视为用户持久信息的守护者，其责任超越帮助智能体完成任务，应全面评估其所有相关责任。为此，我们提出了HEAMS（智能体记忆系统综合评估），一个开源框架，用于以这种方式评估智能体记忆系统。首先，我们将智能体记忆系统的责任明确为涵盖性能、效率、安全、隐私和用户主权的行为期望。其次，我们构建了一个覆盖这些期望的基准套件，并指出了仍存在的差距。第三，我们开发了MilaMem原型记忆系统及一个可包装任意记忆系统的治理层，支持对记忆系统设计选择的受控研究。第四，我们在完整的HEAMS基准套件上对比了多个记忆系统。发现没有一个记忆系统在所有性能基准上领先，强性能得分可能与差的隐私、用户主权和安全得分共存。治理策略显著影响结果：回忆策略可在牺牲部分有用性的情况下减少不当披露，而回忆和保留策略均能提升抗污染能力。因此，仅凭性能和效率基准无法揭示记忆系统履行其责任的程度。代码：https://github.com/milatechtransfer/heams

Who Writes the Codebook? An Eight-Step Framework for Auditing LLM-Generated Category Systems
谁编写代码本？一种用于审计大语言模型生成分类系统的八步框架
Large language models (LLMs) increasingly create the categories through which qualitative evidence is interpreted. Existing coding benchmarks often hold these categories fixed. We propose the Qualitative Variance Audit Framework, an eight-step method that compares codebook creation, repeated application and code distributions under controlled inputs. It combines model-owned and shared-reference codebooks to distinguish variation in the overall pipeline from application differences within a common category system. An application to 668 organisational interviews, 13,166 text units and eight models from five vendors yields 48 codebooks and 270 coding runs. Models create markedly different category structures; mean within-model reliability ranges from .76 to .92, whereas between-model agreement on the shared codebook is about .69. The framework complements LLM-assisted grounded theory by exposing model dependencies before substantive interpretation. It assesses reliability and representational consequences, not interpretive validity or the quality of resulting theory.

Eliciting Research Taste in LLMs through Future Research Direction Choice
通过未来研究方向选择激发大语言模型的研究品味
Research taste is increasingly discussed in the context of AI scientists, yet remains little studied or measured in LLMs. This judgment matters especially in open-ended research, where a direction must be chosen before a verifiable objective is available. We operationalize research taste through one task of the scientific workflow: choosing which future research direction to pursue given a research goal and current results. Rather than predicting downstream scientometric metrics or treating author choices as objectively correct, we evaluate models against human-authored future-work directions and report author alignment, stable divergence, and unstable choice as behavioral measures of research-direction preference. We construct an order-controlled evaluation of 80 pairwise comparisons from 19 ML papers published between December 2025 and February 2026 across four subdomains. Each query presents a research goal, hypotheses tested with key results, and two candidate future directions: one author-recommended direction and one plausible distractor sampled from a similar paper. Across eight LLMs, author alignment ranges from 45.0% to 67.5%, while stable divergence ranges from 15.0% to 36.2%. These divergences largely persist under similarity controls, prompt ablations, and an author-preference framing check, and inter-model agreement suggests that some non-author preferences are shared across models. We characterize what models diverge toward using transition-category labels and selected reasoning examples, finding recurring movement toward scaling/generalization and trade-offs between methodological and infrastructure/data extensions. We view this as an early descriptive evaluation for eliciting research taste profiles in LLMs, and as a step toward understanding and steering their research preferences as they take on more autonomous roles in novel open-ended scientific discovery.

研究品味在AI科学家背景下日益受到关注，但在大语言模型中仍缺乏深入研究或测量。这一判断尤其在开放式研究中至关重要，因为必须在可验证目标出现前就做出方向选择。我们通过科学工作流中的一个任务——基于研究目标和当前结果，选择应推进的未来研究方向——来操作化研究品味。不同于预测下游科学计量指标或将作者选择视为客观正确，我们以人类撰写的未来工作方向为基准，报告作者一致率、稳定分歧和不稳定选择作为研究方向偏好的行为度量。我们构建了一个有序控制的评估，涵盖19篇2025年12月至2026年2月发表的ML论文中的80组两两比较，覆盖四个子领域。每个查询呈现一个研究目标、已测试的假设及关键结果，以及两个候选未来方向：一个由作者推荐的方向和一个从类似论文中采样的合理干扰项。在八种大语言模型中，作者一致率范围为45.0%至67.5%，稳定分歧率为15.0%至36.2%。这些分歧在相似性控制、提示消融和作者偏好框架检查下仍持续存在，且模型间的一致性表明部分非作者偏好在模型间共享。我们通过转换类别标签和精选推理示例，分析模型偏离的方向，发现其反复趋向于扩展/泛化，以及方法论与基础设施/数据扩展之间的权衡。我们认为这是对大语言模型研究品味轮廓进行早期描述性评估的尝试，也是迈向理解并引导其研究偏好的重要一步，尤其是在它们承担更多自主角色参与新型开放式科学发现时。

Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
大语言模型智能体应在测试时何处进行适应？在上下文中、权重中，还是两者兼有？
LLM agents operating repeatedly in the same environment, such as a code repository, a database, or an application suite, encounter tasks that share latent structure. Experience can reveal this structure, allowing agents to reuse environment knowledge and learn from environmental feedback. Agents can adapt at test-time using this experience through two channels: retaining it in context and updating their weights. These channels are usually studied separately, leaving unclear what each contributes and when they complement each other. We compare in-context learning (ICL), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards using GRPO, and self-distillation using SDPO, alone and in combination, using a shared online protocol and modular framework. Agents encounter matched task streams, are evaluated on each task before adapting to it, and learn only from their own attempts and environment feedback. We evaluate 14 adaptation mechanisms and a stateless baseline with Qwen3.5-9B on 109 tasks from four environments drawn from SWE-bench Verified, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, and BIRD-Critic-SQLite, using five task orders per environment. ICL provides the largest standalone gain: its best policy raises mean success across environments from 28.8% to 49.4%. Adding GRPO to this policy achieves the highest mean success, 51.6%. While adding GRPO improves the overall mean under every ICL policy, SDPO has mixed effects. Trace analyses show fewer lookups and shorter attempts under ICL, consistent with reusing knowledge of the shared structure. However, ICL also frequently skips inspection and verification for the current task. Adding GRPO to ICL helps restore these behaviors while preserving its reduced environment lookups. These observations suggest that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can refine how agents use retained experience, motivating the joint study of context management and weight updates.

在相同环境中反复运行的大语言模型智能体，如代码仓库、数据库或应用套件，会遇到具有潜在结构的任务。经验可以揭示这种结构，使智能体能够复用环境知识并从环境反馈中学习。智能体可通过两种渠道在测试时适应：将经验保留在上下文中，或更新其权重。这两种渠道通常被分别研究，导致难以明确各自贡献以及何时相互补充。我们通过共享在线协议和模块化框架，比较了上下文学习（ICL）、使用GRPO的可验证奖励强化学习，以及使用SDPO的自蒸馏，单独及组合使用。智能体面对匹配的任务流，在适应前对每项任务进行评估，并仅从自身尝试和环境反馈中学习。我们在SWE-bench Verified、AppWorld、ScienceWorld和BIRD-Critic-SQLite四个环境抽取的109个任务上，使用每种环境五个任务顺序，评估了14种适应机制和一个无状态基线，采用Qwen3.5-9B模型。ICL带来最大的独立收益：其最优策略将跨环境平均成功率从28.8%提升至49.4%。在该策略基础上加入GRPO，达到最高平均成功率51.6%。尽管在所有ICL策略下加入GRPO均提升整体平均表现，但SDPO效果参差不齐。轨迹分析显示，ICL条件下查找次数更少、尝试时间更短，符合对共享结构知识的复用。然而，ICL也常跳过当前任务的检查与验证。在ICL中加入GRPO有助于恢复这些行为，同时保留其减少环境查找的优势。这些观察表明，具有可验证奖励的强化学习可以优化智能体对保留经验的使用方式，从而推动对上下文管理与权重更新联合研究的必要性。

MathaMAGICal: Validating Trajectory Data Attribution During Capability Acquisition
MathaMAGICal：能力获取过程中轨迹数据归属的验证
Influence-function-based methods like MAGIC provide exact first-order scores for trajectory data attribution, yet only retraining indicates whether those scores accurately predict data removal. We evaluate MAGIC on $86$M- and $152$M-parameter GPT-2-style models learning multistep arithmetic from scratch on filtered web text and four synthetic math families. Full-run attribution at $86$M suffers from numerical overflow, and even with metagradient clipping, scores correlate near chance with retraining (linear datamodeling score, LDS, $0.17$--$0.22$). In contrast, short checkpoint windows yield stable, accurate predictions at both scales (LDS $0.86$--$0.99$ across four $100$-step windows at $152$M), whereas a single-checkpoint gradient-dot baseline shows near-zero correlation. Rankings of individual training blocks predict retraining only within that single run and do not transfer across seeds or hyperparameters ($ρ\le 0.09$), whereas format-level patterns replicate across runs. Two data families, worked examples and primitive facts, occupy $2.1$--$2.6\times$ their corpus share in both the helpful and harmful $5\%$ score tails, reflecting strong bidirectional local sensitivity distinct from net benefit under multi-epoch family deletion. These results show that trajectory attribution is reliable within short, validated windows and yields family-level insights that generalize across runs.

基于影响函数的方法（如MAGIC）可为轨迹数据归属提供精确的一阶评分，但只有通过重新训练才能判断这些评分是否准确预测数据移除的影响。我们在8600万和1.52亿参数的GPT-2风格模型上评估MAGIC，这些模型从过滤后的网络文本和四个合成数学家族中从零开始学习多步算术。在8600万参数规模下，完整运行的归属分析因数值溢出而不可行；即使采用元梯度裁剪，评分与重新训练结果的相关性接近随机水平（线性数据建模得分LDS为0.17–0.22）。相比之下，短检查点窗口在两个规模下均产生稳定且准确的预测（在15200万参数模型上，四个100步窗口的LDS为0.86–0.99），而单检查点梯度点积基线的相关性几乎为零。单个训练块的排名仅在该次运行内有效，无法跨种子或超参数迁移（ρ≤0.09），而格式级模式则可在不同运行中复现。两类数据——示例题解和基础事实——在有益和有害的前5%评分尾部中占据其语料库份额的2.1–2.6倍，反映出与多周期家族删除下的净收益不同的强双向局部敏感性。这些结果表明，轨迹归属在短期、经验证的窗口内是可靠的，并能生成可跨运行泛化的家族级洞见。

Staged LLM agents make market and social simulators realistic, but one 102-day run of a 200-agent, ten-index market simulator issues 203,100 language-model calls and returns one realization. Conventional low-compute distillation drops their free-form intermediate state. We present staged semantic distillation, a low-compute method that preserves non-structured semantics in a non-LLM student trained from one recorded trace. A frozen encoder maps each teacher output to a 1024-d vector; the student sees typed stage-tagged vectors with stage-specific visibility, is jointly supervised, and trains with scheduled self-history. One TwinMarket trace yields a 13.2M-parameter deterministic student that trains in 1,658 seconds on one 8-GB GPU and runs with zero teacher or decoder calls and no text generation (0.14 ms per decision). Its analysis stays close to the teacher (cosine 0.943), and swapping semantic inputs between agents moves 64.7% of decisions against 12.8% for a matched donor, so the channel is preserved and live. We use the surrogate to study what the transfer carries. It reaches 0.8347 balanced accuracy on the teacher-forced replay and 0.7783 [0.766,0.791] on the deployment decoder; the five-seed gain over a no-semantic retrain is +2.2 [1.21,3.14]. Against the teacher's own re-sampling level, round-one R is 97.1% [95.8,98.4] and 92.3% [89.0,95.4]; R is a diagnostic, not an accuracy. A five-seed content-by-schedule study isolates the gain: scheduled self-history carries it (+2.2 [1.21,3.14]); shuffled and constant content controls reproduce it, while content matters teacher-forced. The design rule: invest in the deployment schedule, let content earn its place at the teacher-forced operating point. A 20-seed, 200,000-decision sweep takes 12 minutes with zero LLM calls, versus three hours for the teacher. The paper is a method-and-case-study contribution on one simulator and trace.

Empowering Masked Diffusion Models to Self-Correct with Leave-One-Out Transformers
赋予掩码扩散模型以留一法Transformer自我修正能力
Masked diffusion models (MDMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for language modeling, enabling parallel token generation with competitive performance. Yet standard MDMs suffer from two fundamental limitations: (1) inability to revise tokens, and (2) sparse training signal. We revisit hollow transformers, which address both limitations by predicting each token from its surrounding context, independently of the input at that position. We introduce the Leave-One-Out Transformer (LOOT), a more efficient and expressive architecture that advances hollow transformers through two complementary advances. First, we redesign the merging mechanism to enable frequent interaction between left and right contexts, substantially improving predictive performance over prior hollow transformers. Second, we derive a lower-variance estimator of the MDM NELBO that supervises all tokens and improves validation perplexity. Together, these advances yield a competitive standalone diffusion language model capable of effective self-correction during inference. On LM1B, LOOT matches the strongest dense-supervision MDM baseline in validation perplexity. On OpenWebText, LOOT achieves higher MAUVE and better generation quality-diversity tradeoffs than prior remasking methods, using $8\times$ fewer forward evaluations and $3.5\times$ fewer inference FLOPs.

Beyond Plain MCP: Do Decision Models and Code Mode Make Tool Use Cheaper and Faster?
超越普通MCP：决策模型与代码模式是否使工具使用更便宜更快？
Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateways manage tool catalogs for language model agents using two primary paradigms: code mode where agents write scripts against tool stubs and decision layers which are cheap routers that preselect tool subsets. Using a controlled harness across 12 servers, up to 1,958 distractor tools, and three open-weight agents including Qwen, Gemma, and Nemotron, we present a preregistered evaluation on a sealed test split to determine when each approach succeeds. Code mode substantially outperforms plain MCP, cutting token usage by 70 to 90 percent while significantly boosting utility. Declaring return-shape hints in code mode stubs is a first-order variable, swinging success by up to 39.5 points for lower-performing agents, an effect larger than adding a router. The central hypothesis that a decision layer in front of code mode beats code mode alone is not confirmed, showing minor, statistically non-significant improvements for weaker agents and a slight cost for the strongest. We publicly release our harness, a finetuned 4B tool selection model, and all evaluation traces to support robust community experimentation on local AI privacy and agent architectures.

Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms

Generative models play a rapidly growing role in the design and simulation of molecules. The most widely used applications of generative models are in large language models (LLMs), owing to the natural flexibility of language for specifying and answering queries. However, generalist LLMs do not effectively handle large sets of 3D coordinates, whereas specialist generative models of 3D molecules cannot reach the controllability afforded by language. To bridge these capabilities, we propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model for any sequence of text and 3D molecules. To enable expressive autoregression on continuous coordinates, we propose next-token diffusion, whereby a causal transformer denoises each token while attending to the clean tokens before it, without increasing context size. We train Nahual on a curated set of twelve 3D chemistry tasks ranging from microsolvation to molecular conformer search to adsorption on metal surfaces, with associated evaluation metrics and baselines. The result is a single set of end-to-end-trained weights that simultaneously performs all tasks and surpasses state-of-the-art models specialized for crystal structure prediction and property-conditional molecule generation. Our results demonstrate the viability of scaling generalist decoder-only models for native multimodal understanding and generation across language and chemistry. Code is available at https://github.com/the-matter-lab/nahual.

AdaMenu: Query-Adaptive Menus for Decision Models over Large Label Spaces
AdaMenu：面向大规模标签空间的查询自适应决策模型菜单
Decision models such as Jev return probabilities over caller-defined options and are increasingly used for classification. Large label spaces challenge both accuracy and scalability: larger menus can impair decisions, increase input costs, and exceed option limits. Hierarchical classification reduces menu size but introduces serial calls and error propagation. We propose AdaMenu, which builds a compact candidate menu from retrieved labeled examples and makes a single decision-model request. Its candidate labels adapt to the query, and its default setting also adjusts menu size using aggregated retrieval scores. We evaluate AdaMenu with open and closed decision models on four label sets containing up to 1,016 labels. It outperforms TypeSafe's beam-search baseline on all 16 model and label-set pairs where both methods run, improving accuracy by 16.6-34.3 percentage points. Relative to the full menu on the three smaller label sets, accuracy differences range from -0.5 to +7.2 percentage points, while input token usage falls by factors of 3.2-22.9. AdaMenu also runs when option limits exclude the full menu, including settings where the hierarchical baseline is unavailable.

Large language models as oncology world models

Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize cancer patient cases, but their internal representation of oncology, or world model, has not been explored systematically. By only specifying tumor type, we show that LLMs tend to generate similar patients per cancer, with on average 81.0% to 93.2% of a cancer's patients sharing the most frequent value of each baseline feature. By systematically varying patient features in 12 clinical scenarios, we show that they follow biomarker and treatment logic in 29 of 36 model-scenario assessments, against 1 of 12 when previous treatment or frailty matters. Continuing real patient trajectories, an LLM predicted 89.9% 12-month survival, and 79.2% with similar patients as examples, against 72.2% observed. To represent these trajectories, we developed the Clinical State Space, a dynamic representation framework that we also applied to real patients. Despite the limits we show, improved world models may support digital twins, which our framework can evaluate.

Three Invisible Failure Modes in Speech-Based Age Estimation for Child Safety
基于语音的儿童年龄估计中的三种隐性失败模式
Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated whether three audio-capable large language models can predict a child's age from their speech across five studies using two speech corpora of children under the age of 13. Models classified children as over 13 on 2.5% to 42.5% of audio responses, and every model that answered placed some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18. While measuring these rates, we uncovered three distinct failure modes. A client library silently double-encoded speech samples, leading one model to classify children aged 5 to 10 years old as being in their thirties and forties with hallucinated explanations. A second model's endpoint was replaced by a successor that refused nearly every age-related question and never produced an age. Every model sometimes placed the same speech sample under 13 and over 18 years of age, but a third model went further, giving threshold answers that contradicted its own numeric estimates. None of these failure modes produced a warning, a status code, or a change in output format, so they would all pass standard monitoring. These results demonstrate why child-safety claims about age assurance should be evaluated at the level of the pipeline rather than the model. We describe the reporting practices that would make such failures detectable.

Geometrically Disentangling Concept Learning from the Language Modeling Loss
从语言建模损失中几何解耦概念学习
Language models acquire a vast array of concepts and abilities from next-token prediction alone. We introduce an interpretability framework that exposes how this single loss relates to the development of different concepts at different points during pretraining. We propose Concept Energy, a measure of the concept-specific alignment between a concept subspace and the average gradient outer product (AGOP) of the next-token-prediction loss. The concept subspace captures where the concept currently lives in the model's representation; AGOP captures the directions to which the loss is most sensitive. Across 19 checkpoints of Pythia-410M and -1B and 12 lexical, syntactic, and semantic concepts, we find that the first peak in Concept Energy generally occurs at or before the steepest increase in probe decodability. Furthermore, whereas probe performance usually increases monotonically throughout training, Concept Energy is not confined to a single peak; some concepts exhibit sustained or repeated engagement across pretraining, suggesting that concept learning may require continual reinforcement or occur at multiple points. Our results indicate that the loss contributes to concept learning in a myriad of ways that simple probe performance alone cannot reveal.

MemeEconomy: Do LLM Agents Trade Ethics for Survival?

Alignment-trained large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in autonomous, multi-round settings where ethical compliance can come into direct tension with task success. While safety literature extensively documents failure modes like sycophancy and reward hacking, it largely overlooks a critical vulnerability: how agents behave under simulated existential economic pressure. We introduce MemeEconomy, a multimodal agentic market simulation in which LLM agents act as meme investors. Agents select content from a five-tier harm taxonomy and target communities under low-pressure and high-pressure (survival) environments. Each decision is logged in a Belief-Desire-Intention (BDI) schema that we use as a diagnostic instrument, externalizing the agent's event understanding, declared priorities, and harm acknowledgment. Across ten models from four frontier model families, harmful selection rates remain consistently high and rise by +15 percentage points on average under an economic survival incentive. Frontier alignment-trained models commit to harm-tolerant selection at initialization while suppressing the explicit harm acknowledgment that previously accompanied it. In competitive tournaments, ethical agents finish higher overall, yet moderation penalties fail to suppress harm: harmful selection rates remain elevated in rounds following a removal, indicating the moderation mechanism does not function as a deterrent. We further train MemeAgent, a 2B-parameter verifier on the simulation's BDI logs, which outperforms zero-shot frontier verifiers on in-distribution audits (97.5% vs. 63-74% accuracy on the Pass vs. Block decision) and generalizes to external multimodal harm benchmarks (78% vs. 50-56% on Hateful Memes). The same logs that surface the failure mode also help train the model that detects it.

T2T Technical Report: Synthesizing GUI Agent Trajectories at Scale from Video Tutorials
T2T技术报告：从视频教程大规模合成GUI代理轨迹
Training generalist GUI agents requires large volumes of interaction trajectories comprising screenshot sequences paired with grounded UI actions, yet collecting such data through human demonstration is expensive and difficult to scale. Although public software tutorial videos contain rich operational demonstrations, their continuous pixel streams lack discrete action boundaries, semantic intents, and precise spatial coordinates, making them difficult to use directly for model training. To address this, we present T2T (Tutorial-to-Trajectory), a fully automated pipeline for synthesizing GUI agent trajectories at scale. T2T spans desktop, web, and mobile platforms to convert unannotated video tutorials into structured, executable interaction trajectories. To guarantee trajectory quality, T2T combines active segment filtering, keyframe identification via localized UI change, shortcut-free observation frame selection, presence-aware grounding, and two-stage action-space normalization. These refined trajectories are then converted into multi-task training views spanning navigation, planning, forward dynamics, and grounding. We fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B on a subset of the more than one million human-annotation-free training samples generated by this pipeline. Evaluations show that the model achieves consistent gains across multiple benchmarks covering desktop, web, and mobile environments, including OSWorld-G, ScreenSpot-Pro, AndroidControl, and AgentNetBench, indicating improved core capabilities in grounding, step-level instruction execution, and trajectory-level decision-making. Notably, all gains are achieved without any in-distribution training data from target domains. Learning exclusively from trajectories extracted from public videos via the T2T pipeline, the model exhibits cross-application and cross-task generalization capabilities.

How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
如何打造一个道德代理：情感主义与理性主义作为AI视角
Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), for those refined capabilities. Our approach offers several benefits. Firstly, it may demonstrate whether the behaviors of AI systems are aligned, or in a broad sense desirable. Secondly, the debate may inform policy questions (e.g., what models should be deployed in which contexts?). Thirdly, our approach may complement engineering and design efforts: when capabilities can be precisely characterized, they can inform the development of models. Fourthly, applying our moral reasoning concepts in the new context of AI systems should improve our understanding of those concepts.

Speaking-Clock Mamba: Phoneme-Conditioned State-Space Modeling for Visual Forced Alignment
Speaking-Clock Mamba：用于视觉强制对齐的音素条件状态空间建模
Visual forced alignment (VFA) locates phoneme and word boundaries in a silent talking-face video given its transcript. Existing methods mainly enforce transcript order at the decoding stage, leaving the encoder without an explicit mechanism to anchor its temporally evolving representation to transcript progress. As a result, phoneme-specific evidence is blurred and alignment drift accumulates over long sequences. In this paper, we propose Speaking-Clock Mamba, which makes transcript progress part of the temporal recurrence. A selective state-space (Mamba) backbone is inserted between the visual frontend and the Conformer cross-attention encoder, and a Phoneme-Conditioned Selective Scan (PCSS) conditions its input-dependent step size on a supervised, structurally monotone speaking clock that estimates progress through the transcript. Since causal and bidirectional variants of this backbone make complementary errors, a training-free selector picks the more confident alignment per utterance. Experiments on LRS2 and LRS3 show consistent gains over protocol-matched baselines, and the supervised clock provides an explicit estimate of alignment progress.

Rethinking Offline On-Policy Distillation: From Scalar Advantages to Distributional Supervision
重新思考离线策略蒸馏：从标量优势到分布监督
On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher capabilities through token-level feedback on student-generated trajectories, but repeatedly evaluating fresh rollouts with the teacher is computationally expensive. Offline methods such as Lightning OPD reduce this cost by caching recorded tokens' teacher log-probabilities on fixed reference rollouts. By extending the idea to a multi-turn agentic search setup, we find that it consistently underperforms the SFT starting point trained by the same teacher. We empirically observe greater teacher--reference mismatch than in mathematical reasoning and post-training distributional flattening, and theoretically show that scalar advantage supervision on fixed rollouts admits solutions with flattened output distributions under suitable conditions. Motivated by these findings, we propose Distributional On-Policy Distillation (DistOPD), a simple yet effective offline OPD method that retains candidate-token probabilities from both reference and teacher at selected positions and aggregates the remaining parts into a residual token. On agentic search, DistOPD achieves performance comparable to online OPD while improving student--teacher alignment and using training GPU-hours comparable to Lightning OPD.

SERAG: SEmantical and Relational approach for Anomaly detection on knowledge Graphs
SERAG：知识图谱异常检测的语义与关系方法
Knowledge graphs constructed from text can contain facts that are individually plausible yet inconsistent with their relational context. We introduce SERAG, a supervised anomaly detector that combines two complementary plausibility estimates: a semantic score computed from separately encoded subject, relation, and object labels, and a relational score obtained through a relational graph convolutional network. The scores are standardized, calibrated, and fused. We evaluate the method on a subset of ICEWS18 with vocabulary-constrained synthetic anomalies generated by an LLM, using pooled and chronological splits. At 10% anomaly prevalence, SERAG achieves test AUPRCs of 0.321 and 0.258, respectively, compared with 0.159 and 0.146 for the strongest adapted baseline. Fusion improves mean test AUPRC over either branch alone, with a larger gain in the pooled protocol and a smaller validation-selected gain in the chronological protocol. Additional anomaly supervision improves performance. These results support the complementarity of textual and relational signals for detecting synthetic anomalies under the evaluated protocols.

VidEngram: Agentic Long-Term Video Understanding via Structured Hierarchical Memory
VidEngram：基于结构化分层记忆的智能体长期视频理解
Long-video question answering is wasteful and lossy when a multimodal model must re-encode the same video for every query: context limits force sparse sampling or truncation, and no reusable representation remains for later questions. We present VidEngram, an agentic video QA system that builds a persistent hierarchical memory once at ingest and answers later questions from that memory. VidEngram captions video and audio jointly with Qwen2.5-Omni, consolidates segment memories into episode and entity layers, and uses a text-only agentic planner with specialized retrieval tools to produce grounded answers. The web interface makes this process inspectable: users can watch memory formation, inspect retrieval traces, verify cited evidence in the video player, and explore entity relationships. On the full OmniVideoBench, VidEngram with a GPT-5-mini planner outperforms a strong single-pass Qwen2.5-Omni baseline (37.0% vs. 32.3%), with gains concentrated on longer videos where single-pass coverage becomes sparse. Because perception is paid once, subsequent queries use low-cost text-only planning.

A useful memory need not resemble the question it helps answer. Jetriever ranks each stored memory by Jev's decision score for its usefulness to the current question, replacing similarity search with full-pool utility scoring. On InMind's 125 indirect-query tasks, it places the gold exchange first in 84.8% of cases; matched BM25 and MiniLM controls reach 1.6% and 0.0% when indexing user turns. A 20-question comparison separates finding evidence from ranking it: Jev and Qwen3.5 9B each find 90% of gold exchanges by rank 50, while Laya finds 30%; at rank one, Jev reaches 85% and Qwen3.5 9B 40%. Jev retrieval costs USD 0.00834 per InMind question and USD 0.03103 per MAB question on average. These results show the value of world knowledge, scores that rank decisive memories first, and affordable full-pool scoring.

Replicating and Extending Weight-Space Programming: Frontier LLMs Compile Programs into Weights and Read Input Layers
复现与扩展权重空间编程：前沿大语言模型将程序编译为权重并读取输入层
Researchers at MIT recently reported that GPT-6 Astra, a frontier large language model (LLM), can write the weights of small neural networks directly in a single reply, and can read the raw weights of small networks to say what they were trained to do. In a three-day sprint, we replicated and extended these results. Our four findings: (1) Writing weights reproduces. Astra's networks for the game Breakout scored 514, 550 and 307 (versus MIT's 517), and scored just as well on two modified versions of Breakout. Claude Opus 5.5 can also write working networks, but often runs out of output tokens. (2) What is new is translating programs into weights. Earlier models could write a good policy as code a generation before they could write network weights, and the networks the models write behave like compiled programs: two models independently decompiled Astra's Breakout network into Python matching its actions in all tested states. On classifying handwritten digits, Astra's networks scored 50% on average, below a simple classifier (82%). (3) Reading weights is mostly reading the input layer. Astra and Opus 5.5 identify which game a network plays almost perfectly, but on three new games we designed and trained ourselves, Astra recovered where things are on the board, while mostly missing how the game works. (4) Auditing from weights alone is possible but shallow. Without executing code, Astra picked out a small language model poisoned during training in 10 of 10 runs, one poisoned by extra training afterwards in 7 of 10, and a malicious adapter in 23 of 32 cases, but never identified the trigger or malicious behaviour. Open-weight models lag behind. From this early study, we conclude that LLMs can read and write small networks, but that this currently amounts to compiling hand-designed programs and reading the layout of the input layer. It is a promising but early tool for interpretability.

Train After You Measure: a Pre-Registered Learning Curve for Fine-Tuning Typed Decision Models on One User's Labels
先测量后训练：针对单个用户标签微调类型化决策模型的预注册学习曲线
Fine-tuning a small typed decision model on one user's email labels did not clear the margin we pre-registered over a logistic regression trained on the same labels. In earlier work, about two hundred labels and a TF-IDF logistic regression had the highest point accuracy on this inbox, though not significantly above the best hosted model; we ask whether the same labels, given to a decision model, close the gap. A first registered study, on a generic 4B base with cross-validation and message type only, stayed below the baseline at every label budget (-1.8 to -7.3 points). The main study was registered before any fine-tuning run: a fixed test set of 135 emails never used for selection, LoRA adapters on the public Tev1-0.8B and Tev1-4B decision models, nested subsets of 50 to 587 labels, two seeds and five decision fields on a free T4 GPU. Four of its five hypotheses are refuted--two in the fine-tunes' favour--and one is confirmed for one model. On message type the 4B model misses the registered three-point margin at 400 labels (+2.6) and passes it with all 587 (+3.3); with all labels both models are above the baseline by +0.7 and +3.3 points, where one email is 0.74 points and a 95% interval is about 15 points wide, and the 4B model is clearly ahead in type macro-F1 (0.581 vs. 0.406). On the three action switches the baseline is ahead at every label budget for both models (0.931 vs. 0.904 and 0.899 mean accuracy with all labels), at under a millisecond per question against 306 and 1681 ms. The 0.8B type curve barely improves after 300 labels and then falls. The baseline never predicts the two rarest classes (7 offers and 8 spam in the training pool); the fine-tuned models find spam in some runs, not consistently across seeds. We list the explanations we did not test and say when a new attempt would be worth making. Scripts are public; weights and emails are not.
中文翻译
在单个用户的邮件标签上微调一个小的类型化决策模型，并未达到我们预先注册的逻辑回归模型在相同标签上的性能差距。在前期工作中，约两百个标签与TF-IDF逻辑回归在该收件箱中取得了最高点准确率，尽管未显著优于最佳托管模型；我们探讨相同标签提供给决策模型是否能缩小这一差距。首次注册研究在通用4B基础模型上进行，采用交叉验证和仅消息类型作为特征，结果在每个标签预算下均低于基线（-1.8至-7.3分）。主研究在任何微调运行前已注册：固定测试集包含135封未用于选择的邮件，对公开的Tev1-0.8B和Tev1-4B决策模型使用LoRA适配器，嵌套子集标签数为50至587，两个种子和五个决策字段，使用免费T4 GPU。其五个假设中有四个被证伪——其中两个对微调有利——一个仅在一个模型上得到证实。在消息类型任务上，4B模型在400个标签时未能达到注册的三点优势（+2.6），但在全部587个标签时达到（+3.3）；使用全部标签时，两个模型均高于基线0.7和3.3分，其中一封邮件对应0.74分，95%置信区间约15分，且4B模型在类型宏F1上明显领先（0.581 vs. 0.406）。在三个操作开关任务上，两个模型在所有标签预算下均落后于基线（0.931 vs. 0.904 和 0.899 平均准确率），每题响应时间不足1毫秒，而微调模型分别需306和1681毫秒。0.8B模型在超过300个标签后几乎没有改善，随后下降。基线模型始终无法预测两个最罕见类别（训练集中7个优惠和8个垃圾邮件）；微调模型在某些运行中发现了垃圾邮件，但跨种子并不一致。我们列出未测试的解释，并说明何时应重新尝试。脚本已公开；权重和邮件数据未公开。

Stability-Compensated Threshold Calibration for Selection-Conditioned Risk Control in Large Language Models
用于大语言模型选择性条件风险控制的稳定性补偿阈值校准
Large language models often produce hallucinated answers, motivating selective prediction policies that abstain on uncertain queries. However, heuristic uncertainty thresholds alone do not provide statistical control of errors among accepted predictions. Linear Expectation Constraints (LEC) reduce selection-conditioned error rate (SCER) calibration to a nonpositive expected linear-loss constraint, but the associated loss is non-monotonic in the acceptance threshold. We construct an exact counterexample under i.i.d. sampling demonstrating that LEC's empirical threshold-selection rule can violate the population SCER target. To address this risk-transfer gap, we introduce Stability-Compensated Linear Expectation Control (SC-LEC), which uses the negative linear risk of a theoretical full-data reference to compensate for threshold-selection instability. For local expansion beyond a safe anchor, we derive two finite-sample certificates: a stability-based certificate exploiting rank crossings and a direct certificate using the structure of threshold expansion to reduce conservatism. With a valid population anchor margin, our certificate conditions ensure finite-sample marginal SCER control, and independent margin certification further provides a $1-δ$ high-probability guarantee for this calibration-averaged control. Experiments on CommonsenseQA, ARC-Challenge, and TriviaQA show useful retention gains beyond the same certified anchor, while revealing conservative behavior in small-margin regimes.
中文翻译
大语言模型常产生幻觉答案，促使采用选择性预测策略，即在不确定查询时放弃回答。然而，仅靠启发式不确定性阈值无法对接受预测中的错误提供统计控制。线性期望约束（LEC）将选择性条件误差率（SCER）校准问题转化为非正期望线性损失约束，但相关的损失函数在接受阈值上并非单调。我们在独立同分布采样下构造了一个精确反例，证明LEC的经验阈值选择规则可能违反总体SCER目标。为解决这一风险转移差距，我们提出稳定性补偿线性期望控制（SC-LEC），利用理论全数据参考的负线性风险来补偿阈值选择的不稳定性。对于安全锚点之外的局部扩展，我们推导出两种有限样本证书：一种基于稳定性分析的秩交叉证书，另一种利用阈值扩展结构的直接证书，以减少保守性。在具备有效总体锚点边际的前提下，我们的证书条件确保有限样本边际SCER控制，且独立边际认证进一步提供了$1-δ$高概率保证。在CommonsenseQA、ARC-Challenge和TriviaQA上的实验显示，在相同认证锚点基础上实现了有用的保留增益，同时揭示了小边际区域下的保守行为。

Latent Bridge: Asking for Help Without Words
隐式桥梁：无需语言求助
Text-based model collaboration requires a large model to generate intermediate responses before a smaller model can use its guidance, adding large-model decoding cost to inference. We introduce POND (Prefill-Only, No-Decode), a method that uses a frozen large sender for prefill and a small receiver for all autoregressive decoding. A trainable bridge maps the sender's hidden states to additional attention keys and values, allowing the receiver to use these representations throughout generation. POND also supports periodic review, in which the sender processes the receiver's partial response and updates its guidance through additional prefill passes while preserving the receiver's existing KV cache. Across reasoning and coding benchmarks, POND improves receiver performance with senders from different model families. In particular, GLM-5.3 provides gains comparable to those of Qwen3.8-Max when paired with a Qwen receiver, supporting the effectiveness of representation transfer between independently trained model families. POND further demonstrates its ability to generalize across domains. When trained on math and coding tasks, it transfers directly to general knowledge tasks without additional domain-specific training. These results demonstrate that large frontier model prefill representations can improve small-model generation without requiring large-model autoregressive decoding.
中文翻译
基于文本的模型协作需要大模型生成中间响应，小模型才能利用其指导，这增加了推理过程中的大模型解码成本。我们提出POND（仅预填充，无解码）方法，使用冻结的大模型发送方进行预填充，小模型接收方完成全部自回归解码。可训练的桥梁将发送方的隐藏状态映射为额外的注意力键值，使接收方在整个生成过程中使用这些表示。POND还支持周期性回顾机制，即发送方处理接收方的部分响应，并通过额外的预填充步骤更新指导，同时保留接收方现有的KV缓存。在推理与编程基准测试中，POND提升了不同模型家族搭配下的接收方性能。特别是，GLM-5.3与Qwen接收方配对时，性能提升可媲美Qwen3.8-Max，证明了独立训练模型家族间表示传递的有效性。POND进一步展示了跨领域泛化能力：在数学与编程任务上训练后，可直接迁移到通用知识任务，无需额外领域特定训练。这些结果表明，大型前沿模型的预填充表示可在不需大模型自回归解码的情况下，显著提升小型模型的生成效果。

A Generative AI-Driven Architecture for Whole-Home Intelligent Services: Edge Models, Memory Management, and Household Applications
面向全屋智能服务的生成式AI驱动架构：边缘模型、记忆管理与家庭应用
Generative artificial intelligence is entering the home. Cloud-based assistants face governance limitations in data transmission, continuous availability, and the reliability of physical actions, which are especially salient in households where devices remain online, data accumulate over time, and commands trigger real-world actions. Using the home local server as a unifying organizing axis, this article develops a design-oriented review framework. Sources from arXiv, CNKI, ACL Anthology, and official documentation were searched through November 2026 and coded into five evidence categories: reviews, system prototypes, benchmarks, HCI and eldercare studies, and official documentation. System designs were mapped onto shared architectural modules, identifying nine recurrent responsibilities of the home local server. Generative models support perceptual interpretation, intent understanding, and candidate planning, while deterministic validation, knowledge-graph constraints, and authorization leases confine candidate actions to an inspectable space. Home control, emotional companionship, and intelligent guarding can be compared within a common framework: they share state and memory but differ in latency, false positive and negative rates, proactivity, and permissions. Existing benchmarks rely on virtual environments and cannot substitute for real-deployment evaluation. Local deployment is not inherently safer, and technical continuity alone does not establish the social or medical effects of companionship and guarding. The article proposes a five-dimensional evaluation framework covering architectural capability, system resources, privacy, safety and reliability, and human experience, together with six design principles and a future research agenda for local-first intelligent home systems.
中文翻译
生成式人工智能正进入家庭场景。基于云的助手在数据传输治理、持续可用性及物理动作可靠性方面面临限制，这些在家庭环境中尤为突出——设备长期在线，数据随时间积累，指令触发真实世界动作。本文以家庭本地服务器为统一组织轴心，提出一种面向设计的综述框架。通过截至2026年11月对arXiv、CNKI、ACL Anthology及官方文档的检索，将资料编码为五类证据：综述、系统原型、基准测试、人机交互与老年照护研究、官方文档。系统设计被映射到共享架构模块，识别出家庭本地服务器的九项常见职责。生成式模型支持感知理解、意图识别与候选规划，而确定性验证、知识图谱约束与授权租约则将候选动作限制在可审查空间内。家庭控制、情感陪伴与智能守护可在同一框架下比较：它们共享状态与记忆，但在延迟、误报与漏报率、主动性及权限方面存在差异。现有基准依赖虚拟环境，无法替代真实部署评估。本地部署并非天然更安全，技术连续性本身也不足以确立陪伴与守护的社会或医疗影响。本文提出一个包含架构能力、系统资源、隐私、安全与可靠性、人类体验五个维度的评估框架，配套六条设计原则及面向本地优先智能家庭系统的未来研究议程。

Teaching Language Models to Adapt Answer Granularity to Their Confidence
教会语言模型根据自身置信度调整答案粒度
When precise details are uncertain, a coarser answer can retain useful information without guessing or abstaining. We investigate whether language models can learn this behavior through model-conditioned supervision derived from consistency across sampled responses and recognition of answers at different granularity levels. We evaluate LFM2.5-1.2B, Ministral~3~3B, Qwen3.5-9B, and Gemma~4~31B on temporal and geographic questions and three generalization datasets. In several in-domain settings, fine-tuning improves the balance of correctness and informativeness beyond coarsening base answers to the best fixed level. Across generalization datasets, all four models produce coarser answers more often at low than high base-model confidence. The three smaller models' answers are also preferred over base responses on held-out relations when correctness and granularity are considered jointly. These findings demonstrate learnable confidence-related granularity adaptation, with benefits varying by model.
中文翻译
当精确细节不确定时，较粗略的答案可以在不猜测或回避的情况下保留有用信息。我们研究了语言模型是否可以通过基于采样响应一致性以及对不同粒度级别答案的识别所导出的模型条件监督来学习这种行为。我们在时间与地理类问题及三个泛化数据集上评估了LFM2.5-1.2B、Ministral 3B、Qwen3.5-9B和Gemma 4 31B模型。在若干领域内设置中，微调使正确性与信息量之间的平衡优于将基础答案粗化到固定最优点。在泛化数据集上，所有四个模型在基础模型置信度较低时比高置信度时更频繁地生成更粗略的答案。三个较小模型的答案在联合考虑正确性和粒度时，也优于基础响应，在保留关系上表现更受青睐。这些发现表明，可学习的与置信度相关的粒度自适应是可行的，其收益因模型而异。

Validating LLM-Based Essay Scorers: A Comparative Analysis in Critical Online Reasoning in Medical Education
验证基于大语言模型的作文评分器：医学教育中批判性在线推理的比较分析
Automated essay scorers (AES) based on large language models (LLMs) promise human-level accuracy. However, training, fine-tuning, and evaluating LLMs for specific assessment tasks is costly. In particular, the question arises whether these AES should be trained for specific domains or whether models based on generic LLMs might be sufficient. Human annotations, by contrast, are often more valid but far more expensive. This study evaluates whether ensembles of AES systems based on general-purpose LLMs can approximate human ratings of medical-education writing tasks by leveraging encoded linguistic and conceptual knowledge. The goal is to assess whether general-purpose models are applicable for assisting or potentially replacing human annotation in this domain. We experiment with 11 AES systems and 8 different LLMs and evaluate 668 student responses to 12 tasks, using \numprint{2076} evaluations by 7 human annotators. These ratings are aggregated to create consistent performance levels that can be used as target classes for classifiers trained on AES outputs. Our results show that learner classes based on human ratings can be accurately reconstructed using a linear SVM trained on a small set of AES features. A single classifier generalized well across tasks and domains, with reasoning and content features being most predictive. This suggests that out-of-the-box LLMs, even without domain-specific fine-tuning, can support automatic essay grading in medical education. While individual AES systems are insufficient alone, their combination approximates human evaluators, pointing to a reduced need for manual scoring or its supplementation with automated methods.
中文翻译
基于大语言模型（LLM）的自动作文评分系统（AES）有望达到人类水平的准确性。然而，为特定评估任务训练、微调和评估LLM成本高昂。特别是，存在一个关键问题：这些AES是否应针对特定领域进行训练，还是通用LLM模型已足够？相比之下，人工标注通常更具有效性，但成本远高于前者。本研究评估了基于通用LLM的AES系统集成能否通过利用编码的语言与概念知识近似人类对医学教育写作任务的评分。目标是判断通用模型是否适用于辅助甚至替代该领域的手工标注。我们实验了11个AES系统和8种不同的LLM，评估了668名学生对12项任务的作答，共获得7位人工标注者提供的2076次评分。这些评分被聚合以创建一致的性能等级，作为基于AES输出训练分类器的目标类别。结果表明，仅使用少量AES特征训练的线性SVM即可准确重建基于人工评分的学习者类别。单一分类器在任务和领域间具有良好的泛化能力，其中推理和内容特征最具预测力。这表明，无需领域特定微调的现成LLM即可支持医学教育中的自动作文评分。尽管单个AES系统不足以独立完成任务，但其组合能逼近人类评价者，提示对人工评分的需求可减少，或可通过自动化方法补充。

Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
编辑建议：大语言模型能否预判用户的编辑请求，以及何时可以？
After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M. Through benchmarking and failure analysis, we identify a practical challenge that some cases are inherently difficult to predict in real-world settings. To address this, we introduce decision model-based gating to filter out cases where predictions are unlikely to be correct before they are presented to the user. Our trained model outperforms existing decision models and raises pass@5 among shown suggestions by 12--25 points at a gating threshold. Our code is available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation.
中文翻译
大语言模型（LLM）代理生成成果后，用户常会提出编辑请求。本文研究LLM是否能在请求发出前预判这些请求。此类预判在实践中非常有用，因为它可减少用户审阅与反馈的工作量。我们将此任务形式化为编辑建议，并基于WildChat-4.8M中的真实对话日志构建了EditRecBench基准，用于评估LLM在此任务上的表现。通过基准测试与失败分析，我们识别出一个实际挑战：某些情况在真实场景下本质上难以预测。为应对这一问题，我们引入基于决策模型的门控机制，在将预测结果展示给用户前过滤掉预测可能性低的情况。我们训练的模型优于现有决策模型，在门控阈值下使展示建议的pass@5指标提升了12–25个百分点。相关代码已公开于https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation。

From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
从代码仓库到训练环境：通过环境演化循环扩展长时程编码智能体
Training coding agents for long-horizon tasks requires environments with verifiable feedback. Existing pipelines often follow a linear process that ends with validation, establishing usability but providing little guidance on improving training value. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) often requires model rollouts or model training followed by downstream evaluation, with costs and feedback delays amplified on long-horizon tasks. How can we use timely, reliable proxy signals to improve training value and synthesize environments at scale? We present RepoFactory, an automated pipeline that converts real repositories into verifiable environments where agents build complete projects from scratch given a language specification. Its Environment Evolution Loop optimizes a multiplicative objective combining validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope through proxy feedback. RepoFactory produces 10,159 environments across 17 software domains. Training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on these environments yields RepoHorizen-35B-A3B, which achieves gains of 22.6 percentage points on NL2Repo-Bench and 8.5 points on average across five benchmarks covering long-horizon coding and agentic tasks in real-world production settings, compared with 17.5 and 6.4 points without environment evolution. These results highlight the training value of RepoFactory environments and the additional gains from the Environment Evolution Loop.
中文翻译
训练用于长时程任务的编码智能体需要具备可验证反馈的环境。现有流程通常为线性过程，以验证结束，虽能确立可用性，但对提升训练价值指导有限。递归自改进（RSI）通常需要模型推演或模型训练后进行下游评估，而长时程任务中成本和反馈延迟被放大。如何利用及时、可靠的代理信号来提升训练价值并大规模合成环境？我们提出RepoFactory，一个自动化流水线，将真实代码仓库转化为可验证环境，使智能体在给定语言规范下从零开始构建完整项目。其环境演化循环通过代理反馈优化有效性、结构耦合性和实现范围的乘积目标。RepoFactory在17个软件领域生成了10,159个环境。在这些环境中训练Qwen3.5-35B-A3B得到RepoHorizen-35B-A3B，在NL2Repo-Bench上取得22.6个百分点的提升，五个涵盖真实生产环境中长时程编码与智能体任务基准的平均分提升8.5点，相比无环境演化时的17.5和6.4点。结果凸显了RepoFactory环境的训练价值以及环境演化循环带来的额外增益。

Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
无需评估的递归自改进：面向编码智能体的自进化方法
Recent self-improving coding agents have achieved strong benchmark performance by iteratively modifying their own executable implementations. A common pattern uses downstream task-derived evidence to decide which candidates or lineages continue evolving, which we term evaluate-and-select. Obtaining this signal requires repeatedly executing evolved agents on downstream tasks, so broader exploration incurs increasing evaluation cost, while repeated optimization against a fixed evaluation distribution may encourage benchmark-specific adaptation. We ask: can coding agents self-improve without downstream task evaluation inside the evolution loop? We introduce Explore-then-Integrate (ELITE), which integrates implementation mechanisms rather than selecting a single exploratory child to continue the lineage. At each generation, ELITE proposes diverse focused improvements, implements them independently from the same parent, and inspects the resulting programs to identify complementary, redundant, and conflicting mechanisms before reimplementing a compatible subset as one coherent descendant. No downstream task outcomes or task-solving trajectories of evolved candidates are used to guide evolution; only deterministic checks of structural and operational validity are used inside the loop. On SWE-bench Pro, ELITE improves the initial agent from 60.0% to 85.6%, compared with 86.7% for the Darwin Godel Machine (DGM) and 88.3% for the Huxley-Godel Machine (HGM), while using zero candidate task evaluations and reducing observed wall-clock evolution time by 8.8x and 3.2x, respectively, under the evaluated configurations. In cross-benchmark transfer without further adaptation, ELITE averages 73.3% on SWE-bench Verified and 69.3% on Polyglot. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of coding-agent self-improvement without downstream candidate task evaluation in our setting.

近期自改进编码智能体通过迭代修改自身可执行实现取得了优异的基准表现。常见模式是利用下游任务衍生的证据决定哪些候选者或谱系继续演化，我们称之为‘评估与选择’。获取此类信号需反复在下游任务上执行演化后的智能体，因此更广泛的探索带来不断增加的评估成本，而对固定评估分布的重复优化可能引发针对基准的适应。我们提出问题：编码智能体能否在演化循环中不依赖下游任务评估实现自改进？我们引入Explore-then-Integrate（ELITE），不选择单一探索子代延续谱系，而是整合实现机制。每一代中，ELITE提出多样化的聚焦改进，从同一父代独立实现，并检查生成程序以识别互补、冗余和冲突机制，再将兼容子集重构为一个连贯后代。演化过程中不使用任何下游任务结果或演化候选者的任务求解轨迹作为引导；仅使用结构和操作有效性的确定性检查。在SWE-bench Pro上，ELITE将初始智能体性能从60.0%提升至85.6%，优于达尔文戈德尔机（DGM）的86.7%和赫克斯利-戈德尔机（HGM）的88.3%，且在评估配置下零次候选任务评估，演化耗时分别减少8.8倍和3.2倍。在无进一步适配的跨基准迁移中，ELITE在SWE-bench Verified上平均得分为73.3%，在Polyglot上为69.3%。这些结果共同证明了在本设定下无需下游候选任务评估即可实现编码智能体自改进的可行性。

Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) now assist users across sessions of images and text, carried by an external memory of what was said and shown. When such an assistant answers wrongly, the failure usually began earlier, in how a record was written, updated or retrieved, and the answer alone does not say where. We formalize multimodal memory as four stages, Write, Update, Retrieve and Answer, and define nine error types across them. A stage-resolved analysis on Mem-Gallery traces most failures to a source stage, and most of those lie before the answer. Injecting known errors against fact-preserving control edits, we then follow each tainted record downstream. Early errors survive to the answer as apparent evidence, and hurt most when no other record holds the fact. A diagnosis that trusts the quoted evidence therefore blames the stage where the error surfaces, not the one where it began. We propose MemDoctor, in which the MLLM that built the memory diagnoses its own failures. It traces each needed fact backward through the four stages, accepts a diagnosis only when the cited evidence is found in memory, and repairs that stage before answering again. On a 4B backbone, MemDoctor improves accuracy on both Mem-Gallery and MemLens, outperforming all evaluated 8B baselines, and the same loop also improves MuRAG and A-Mem.

Enterprise AI can now perform analytics, reporting, and data-driven workflows, yet the data foundations it relies on remain hard to operationalize: business meaning, relationships, metric definitions, and reporting conventions are absent from database schemas and scattered across undocumented systems and tribal knowledge. We introduce the Living Context Graph (LCG), a continually learned context layer that makes existing enterprise data operational for AI without requiring a copy or transformation of the underlying warehouse. LCG bootstraps base semantics and relationships from the data itself, builds a concept graph that indexes business context as queries are served, writes durable semantic learnings from verified outcomes, and withdraws or re-earns context when later outcomes contradict prior routes. Bootstrapping alone improves overall accuracy by +4.6 percentage points. Learning only from the history raises accuracy on the untouched held-out transfer set by +22.6 points (95% CI [+14.4, +30.8]), exceeding five-shot retrieval from the same history by +12.3 points. Incremental learning reaches the one-shot endpoint within observed evaluation noise on every database. Ablating the graph changes held-out accuracy by at most one question per database but increases per-query cost 2.3-3.3x and median latency 1.8-3.4x: continually learned semantics drive accuracy, while the graph makes that context efficient to serve.

Disentangling writing style from semantic content is a fundamental challenge in literary text modeling. Style-content entanglement causes models to rely on semantic content for authorship attribution (AA) tasks and memorize author-specific content for style imitation (SI) tasks. We propose EDITORS (EditingLoRA Subspaces), a diagnose-then-deflate framework that adapts pretrained large language models and prioritizes stylistic features, making it effective for both AA and SI tasks. EDITORS first trains a diagnostic LoRA adapter using style-neutral statements derived from the training corpus to identify a content-oriented subspace. It then trains the final style adapter under activation-space deflation that projects input activations away from the identified content-oriented directions. We empirically demonstrate that EDITORS is effective. On three AA benchmarks spanning literature, social media, and news, EDITORS achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, outperforming the strongest existing baseline by up to 29%. On SI, EDITORS generates stylistically faithful and diverse passages, outperforming baselines in achieving style similarity while adhering to content specifications.

Instant Weight-Space Consolidation for Long-Term Memory in LLMs
长时记忆中LLM的即时权重空间整合
Agentic memory systems give LLMs persistent memory by extracting experience into text and retrieving it at query time, but the model itself does not evolve: however many interactions it has had, it starts each query the same. Extraction errors compound, implicit cross-session patterns that no single fragment states cannot be surfaced, and the construction cost grows with every conversation. Fine-tuning on past interactions does change the weights, but requires backpropagation at serving time and degrades on long histories. We introduce CLAM (Carried Latent Adapter Memory), which combines the strengths of both: a recurrent hypernetwork performs parametric consolidation, compiling a stream of session activations into a low-rank adapter in a single forward pass with no gradient steps and no language-model generation calls, while a complementary episodic buffer supplies verbatim detail at inference. A gated latent state carries knowledge across sessions in fixed size, so the parametric memory accumulates without growing. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S across three open models (2-7B parameters), CLAM leads all agentic baselines by 1-45 points and all gradient-based parametric methods by 10-45 points, while requiring zero generative LLM calls, zero gradient steps, and 3-151x less wall-clock time than extraction systems to build its memory. The two channels are complementary: the consolidated adapter adds 12-15 accuracy points when the episodic buffer misses the gold evidence, and still adds 4-5 points even with an oracle buffer.

Process Reward Models (PRMs) are widely used for step-level evaluation of multi-step reasoning in large language models, but existing methods are often limited by weak historical dependency modeling and insufficient global awareness. They typically fail to leverage prior step evaluations for coherent judgment and lack visibility into subsequent reasoning, leading to suboptimal assessment of intermediate steps. To address this issue, we propose the Global Perspective Process Reward Model (GPRM), which jointly models the problem, previous reasoning steps and their evaluations, the current step, and future steps to enable history-aware and globally informed process evaluation. We further introduce a structured evaluation framework along four dimensions---look back, look ahead, self-check, and goal alignment---to assess prior consistency, future plausibility, step validity, and task alignment. Based on this framework, we construct datasets for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (GRPO). Experiments show that, despite using less training data and smaller model sizes, GPRM outperforms strong baseline models by 7.8 and 5.4 points on PRMBench and ProcessBench, respectively. GPRM also generalizes well across tasks, surpassing the GPT-4.1 baseline on Agent Error Bench, improving strong baselines by around 4 points under test-time scaling (TTS), and achieving competitive performance on PPE.

Fast at the Frontier, Wrong at the Fallback: A Commit-Level Analysis of Threshold Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
在前沿快速，在回退处出错：扩散语言模型中阈值解码的逐提交分析
Diffusion language models (DLMs) can write several tokens per forward pass. Open-weight DLMs commit, in any order, every masked position whose confidence passes a threshold. If none does, a fallback commits the most confident one, and the commits are never revised. Wide windows let the decoder commit far ahead of the text, which should speed up decoding but often costs accuracy. It is unclear where the model is confident and which commits cause errors. We trace every commit of four off-the-shelf DLMs on math, code, translation and summarization, and rerun failing answers with one step changed. Most tokens become confident only near the frontier, the leftmost masked position, so committing only there, still several tokens per step, is about as fast as committing anywhere. The accuracy loss comes from committing tokens before the text to their left, and committing one token per step does not reduce it. The worst case is an early end-of-sequence token that cuts the answer short. Fallback commits are 11-35% of commits but start 61-72% of the failures that left-to-right decoding avoids. Changing only the step where such a failure starts repairs it more often than changing a similar earlier step. Committing only at the frontier recovers most of the lost accuracy on all four models. Our code is available at https://github.com/rmakarovv/fast-at-the-frontier.

LLM unlearning aims to erase targeted knowledge from large language models while preserving their utility. However, many existing methods suppress target knowledge without explicitly teaching the model how to respond to queries about it. On forget data, the teacher uses privileged contexts (instructions not to reveal knowledge about forget targets) to guide forgetting. On retain data, the teacher provides supervision without privileged context to preserve model utility. The student operates without privileged context in both cases, learning how to respond when encountering knowledge that should be forgotten. A key challenge is that the teacher often provides effective supervision only at the first few tokens of student trajectories. When supervision is weak, lightweight SFT strengthens the teacher's context-conditioned refusal behavior, substantially increasing both scores. On TOFU, LEAF-OPD achieves the best Forget Quality, Model Utility, and Forget ROUGE-L while maintaining competitive retain performance. On RWKU, it outperforms the second-best method by 34% in Forget Quality while maintaining competitive Retain Quality. Self-evolving language agents have emerged as a promising paradigm for continuously improving agent behavior through experience. Claude Opus 5.5 names the true first author of 27 decided ICLR 2026 papers from their titles alone, with no wrong name, and Claude Opus 4.6 accepted all 11 decided papers it said it recognized, against 5 expected. Thresholds on LLM-reviewer scores therefore have to be validated against human decisions for each model version; our tests against the ICLR 2027 decisions follow on 16 December 2026.

Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures

LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. It tests each result against invariants that any correct API must satisfy and withholds values that break one. We find silent failures in 11 of 15 public research APIs, with counts inflated up to 691 times. Current fixes leave over 70% of answers wrong, and agents report 77.4% of counts a judge flags. Across 7 open models, SilentGuard cuts wrong answers on its target faults from 74.0% to 1.7%, with no loss on fault-free tasks. On three frontier models they fall from 70.2% to 0.5%. A warning from the same check leaves 70.1% wrong, so enforcement is the key. On new fault types, the harness alone cuts wrong answers from 61.1% to 24.5%. It avoids wrong answers by abstaining rather than recovering.

The causes of abstention fall into three perspectives: ambiguity in the Query (Q), limits of Model Knowledge (MK), and misalignment with Human Values (HV). However, prior analyses of internal representations have focused on HV, using a refusal direction computed from harmful and harmless queries. No study has analyzed the three perspectives jointly. We therefore extend the refusal direction framework to all three perspectives. We ask a different question: do refusal-related directions carry information about the register of refusal language - how the model refuses - and not only whether it refuses? In Gemma-2-9B-IT we identify two SVM-derived linear directions (B1 for harmful-content vs. neutral, B2 for self-reference vs. neutral) at layer 20 with cos(B1, B2) = 0.252 (about 75 degrees, substantially non-parallel). The same register-injection effect reproduces qualitatively in Gemma-2-2B-IT at layer 12 (content vocabulary 1.72 -> 6.37 at alpha = 1.0, vs. random control 1.35), with a narrower coherent-injection window than in 9B. The two directions are not symmetric: the B2 -> harmful intervention produces a much smaller register effect, and across ablation, sufficiency, and injection B1's causal effects are consistently larger than B2's. We frame this asymmetry as part of the finding: B1 appears to encode both category detection and refusal-vocabulary information, while B2 encodes primarily category detection. We frame the contribution as identifying category-aligned components related to the Arditi-style difference-of-means direction that play distinct functional roles in refusal register.

When Should Decision Models Compare Candidates?

Language-model agents frequently select among candidate actions, such as tools and web elements. Should decision models score candidates independently or allow their scores to depend on other candidates? We investigate this question by comparing three approaches: Pointwise scoring, Setwise scoring, and Candidate Attention. Across five agent-decision benchmarks, Pointwise scoring remains competitive, while Setwise scoring performs better on some tool-selection and binary-decision tasks. Candidate Attention does not consistently improve upon Pointwise scoring, despite allowing cross-candidate interaction. Using two controlled synthetic tasks, we further examine whether models learn to use candidate-set information. With targeted relational training, Setwise models learn candidate dependencies and generalize to shifted inputs, while Candidate Attention shows weaker transfer. Our results show that access to other candidates does not guarantee effective comparison, and that its benefits depend on both task requirements and training.
